Color can vary from dark charcoal to pale blue-gray, so rely on the curly blue-toned coat and bearded terrier appearance rather than exact shade alone.

name: Irish Terrier
Canis lupus familiaris
184.description: A medium-sized terrier with a lean, athletic build, a harsh wiry coat, and a solid red, wheaten-red, or golden-red color. It has a long rectangular head and muzzle, small folded ears, a bearded face, and relatively long legs, giving it a racy, upright outline.
184.guidelines: Classify as Irish Terrier when the dog shows the classic red wiry terrier coat, narrow rectangular muzzle, and leggy, athletic build. Distinguish it from the Lakeland Terrier and Welsh Terrier, which are usually black-and-tan or grizzle rather than solid red; from the Airedale Terrier, which is much larger and typically black-and-tan with a broader head; and from the Border Terrier, which is shorter-legged, less racy, and usually grizzle or tan rather than bright red.

name: Norfolk Terrier
Canis lupus familiaris
185.description: A small, low-set terrier with a compact, sturdy body, short legs, and a harsh, wiry coat. The coat is commonly red, wheaten, black and tan, or grizzle, with a shaggy face and small V-shaped ears that fold forward close to the cheeks.
185.guidelines: Classify as Norfolk Terrier when the dog is a small rough-coated terrier with distinctly dropped ears. Do not confuse with Norwich Terrier, which is very similar but has erect pointed ears. Also distinguish from Border Terrier, which is leggier with an otter-like head, and Cairn Terrier, which usually has erect ears and a scruffier, more tousled outline.

name: Norwich Terrier
Canis lupus familiaris
186.description: A very small, compact terrier with a rough, wiry coat, a short sturdy body, and a foxlike face. It has small, pointed upright ears, dark round eyes, a relatively short muzzle, and a harsh coat that is often red, wheaten, black and tan, or grizzle.
186.guidelines: Classify as Norwich Terrier when the dog is a tiny rough-coated terrier with erect ears and a compact, low, sturdy build. Distinguish it from the Norfolk Terrier, which is very similar but has folded drop ears rather than upright ears. Also avoid confusion with Cairn Terrier, which is usually shaggier, broader-faced, and less compact, and with Yorkshire Terrier, which has a silkier coat instead of a harsh wiry one.

name: Yorkshire Terrier
Canis lupus familiaris
187.description: A very small toy dog with a compact body, fine-boned legs, and a long, silky coat that is typically steel blue or blackish on the body with tan or golden hair on the face, chest, and legs. It has a small pointed muzzle, dark eyes, and erect V-shaped ears; the coat may be floor-length or clipped shorter.
187.guidelines: Classify as Yorkshire Terrier when the dog is a tiny toy breed with a silky blue-and-tan or black-and-tan coat and a neat terrier face. Distinguish it from silky terriers by its smaller size and more compact toy-dog build, from Norwich or Cairn terriers by its much silkier coat rather than a wiry one, and from Maltese by the usual blue/tan coloring instead of solid white. Exclude mixed small companion dogs unless the characteristic Yorkshire Terrier coat texture, coloring, and ear/head shape are clear.

name: Wire Fox Terrier
Canis lupus familiaris
188.description: A small, compact terrier with a square, athletic build, a dense wiry coat, and a long, narrow muzzle. The coat is usually predominantly white with black and/or tan markings, often in a saddle pattern on the back and patches on the head. It has a bearded face, folded V-shaped ears, and long legs for its size.
188.guidelines: Classify as a Wire Fox Terrier when the dog shows a harsh broken coat, white-dominant coloring with black or tan patches, and the breed’s distinctive long, brick-shaped head with a beard. Do not confuse it with the Smooth Fox Terrier, which has a short flat coat, or with Airedale and Welsh terriers, which are larger and more uniformly tan-and-black. It can also resemble schnauzers or other wire-coated terriers, but those usually have different head shape, heavier eyebrows, or less white in the coat.

name: Lakeland Terrier
Canis lupus familiaris
189.description: A small, compact terrier with a sturdy build, a harsh wiry coat, and a distinct rectangular muzzle with beard and furnishings. The coat is often black-and-tan, grizzle, wheaten, red, or pale tan, and the ears are small and folded. The legs are relatively long for a terrier, giving an alert, upright outline.
189.guidelines: Classify as Lakeland Terrier when the dog is a small wire-coated terrier with a neat rectangular head, pronounced beard, and balanced, leggy build. It is commonly confused with the Welsh Terrier and Airedale Terrier; Lakeland Terriers are typically smaller and finer-boned than both. They can also resemble Wire Fox Terriers, but Lakelands usually have a shorter, less narrow head and are less exclusively white-bodied. Avoid using this class for other rough-coated terriers that lack the characteristic rectangular muzzle and compact, square-to-slightly-rectangular proportions.

name: Sealyham Terrier
Canis lupus familiaris
190.description: A small, low-set terrier with a long, sturdy body, short legs, and a mostly white harsh or wiry coat. It has a rectangular outline, folded ears, a strong muzzle, and a distinctive facial furnishing of bushy eyebrows, beard, and whiskers; some dogs show light lemon, tan, or gray markings on the head or ears.
190.guidelines: Classify as Sealyham Terrier when the dog is a compact white terrier with a long low body, short legs, and prominent beard and eyebrows. Distinguish it from the West Highland White Terrier, which is usually more upright with prick ears and a rounder face; from the Scottish Terrier, which is typically black or darker and has erect ears; and from the Wire Fox Terrier, which is leggier, narrower, and more athletic in outline. The Sealyham’s key cues are its low, sturdy build, folded ears, and heavy facial furnishings.

name: Airedale Terrier
Canis lupus familiaris
191.description: A large terrier with a sturdy, square-built body, long legs, and a harsh wiry coat. The typical coloring is tan on the head, legs, and underparts with a black or dark grizzle saddle across the back. It has a long, rectangular head, folded V-shaped ears, a bearded muzzle, and a tidy terrier outline.
191.guidelines: Classify as Airedale Terrier when the dog is a relatively large terrier with the classic tan-and-black wiry coat, long rectangular head, and pronounced beard. Do not confuse it with Welsh Terrier or Lakeland Terrier, which are smaller and more compact, or with Irish Terrier, which is usually solid red rather than black-and-tan. It can also resemble other wirehaired terriers or doodle-type dogs, but Airedales have the distinctive black saddle, longer head, and cleaner terrier build.

name: Cairn Terrier
Canis lupus familiaris
192.description: A small, sturdy terrier with a compact body, short legs, and a shaggy, wiry double coat. The ears are small, pointed, and held erect, and the face is tousled with a bearded muzzle and alert expression. Common coat colors include cream, wheaten, red, gray, and brindle, often with darker shading on the muzzle and ears.
192.guidelines: Classify as Cairn Terrier when the dog is a small rough-coated terrier with erect pointed ears, a natural shaggy appearance, and a compact build. Distinguish it from the Norwich Terrier by the Cairn’s messier, harsher coat and less foxlike face; from the Norfolk Terrier by the Cairn’s upright ears; and from silky or long-haired toy breeds such as the Yorkshire Terrier by the Cairn’s wiry texture, broader head, and sturdier terrier build.

name: Australian Terrier
Canis lupus familiaris
193.description: A small, sturdy terrier with a rough, shaggy double coat, erect pointed ears, and a compact body. Typical coloration includes blue-and-tan, sandy, or red, with a scruffy face and short legs.
193.guidelines: Classify as Australian Terrier when the dog is a small rough-coated terrier with upright ears, a compact build, and a harsh weatherproof coat in blue-and-tan, sandy, or red. Distinguish it from Yorkshire Terrier by the Australian Terrier’s harsher, less silky coat and sturdier body; from Norwich Terrier by its longer body and less rounded head; and from Cairn Terrier by its more consistent erect ears and typical tan or blue-and-tan pattern.

name: Dandie Dinmont Terrier
Canis lupus familiaris
194.description: A small terrier with a long, low body, short legs, and a distinctive silky topknot on the head. The coat is hard or wiry along the body with softer hair on the head and ears, and is commonly pepper (gray-silver to blue-gray) or mustard (cream to reddish tan). The ears hang down, the muzzle is fairly long, and the tail is curved like a scimitar.
194.guidelines: Classify as Dandie Dinmont Terrier when the dog is notably low-slung and elongated, with a soft rounded topknot and drop ears rather than erect ears. Distinguish it from Skye Terrier by the Dandie’s fuller topknot, shorter overall coat, and more terrier-like head; from Scottish Terrier and Cairn Terrier by its much longer body and pendant ears; and from Sealyham Terrier or West Highland White Terrier by its longer outline, softer topknot, and typical pepper or mustard coloring rather than a compact all-white appearance.

name: Boston Terrier
Canis lupus familiaris
195.description: A small, compact terrier breed with a smooth short coat, a square sturdy build, a short muzzle, and large upright ears. The typical coloration is tuxedo-like black-and-white, though dark brindle-and-white also occurs, usually with a white blaze on the face, white chest, and white feet.
195.guidelines: Classify as Boston Terrier when the dog is small and compact with a flat short-faced head, erect pointed ears, and neat black-and-white or brindle-and-white markings. Distinguish it from the French Bulldog by its lighter, less heavy build and longer legs; from the Bulldog by its much smaller size and erect ears; and from pit bull-type terriers by its shorter muzzle, more brachycephalic face, and characteristic tuxedo pattern.

name: Miniature Schnauzer
Canis lupus familiaris
196.description: A small, sturdy terrier-like dog with a compact square body, harsh wiry coat, and distinctive facial furnishings: prominent bushy eyebrows and a full beard and moustache. Common coat colors include salt-and-pepper, black-and-silver, solid black, and white.
196.guidelines: Classify as Miniature Schnauzer when the dog is clearly small and has the breed’s hallmark wiry coat, rectangular muzzle with pronounced beard, and heavy eyebrows. Distinguish it from Standard or Giant Schnauzers by its much smaller size. Separate it from other small terriers by the especially groomed schnauzer face, deep beard, and salt-and-pepper or black-and-silver patterning rather than a softer or shaggier coat.

name: Giant Schnauzer
Canis lupus familiaris
197.description: A large, robust schnauzer with a square, muscular build, a harsh dense wiry coat, and a distinctive long beard and bushy eyebrows. The coat is usually solid black or pepper-and-salt gray, with erect folded ears or cropped upright ears and a strong, rectangular head.
197.guidelines: Classify as Giant Schnauzer when the dog is a large schnauzer-type with the breed’s hallmark beard, heavy eyebrows, and wiry coat. Distinguish it from the Standard Schnauzer and Miniature Schnauzer by its noticeably larger, taller, heavier build. It can resemble black terriers such as the Scottish Terrier or Bouvier des Flandres, but Giant Schnauzers are taller, longer-legged, and more squarely built than Scotties, and cleaner-outlined and less shaggy than Bouviers.

name: Standard Schnauzer
Canis lupus familiaris
198.description: Medium-sized, sturdy, square-built dog with a harsh wiry coat, prominent bushy beard and eyebrows, and a rectangular muzzle. Usually shown in salt-and-pepper, gray, silver, or solid black, often with cropped-looking or naturally folded V-shaped ears and a docked or very short tail.
198.guidelines: Classify as Standard Schnauzer when the dog is medium in size and has the classic schnauzer outline: wiry body coat, strong beard, heavy brows, and balanced square proportions. Distinguish it from the Miniature Schnauzer by its larger, sturdier build, and from the Giant Schnauzer by its clearly smaller size and less massive frame. Avoid confusing it with Scottish Terrier or other terriers, which are lower-set or differently proportioned and do not show the same square schnauzer build.

name: Scottish Terrier
Canis lupus familiaris
199.description: A small, sturdy terrier with a low, short-legged body, a harsh wiry coat that is most often black, and a long rectangular muzzle with pronounced beard and eyebrows. The ears are small, upright, and pointed, and the tail is typically carried upright. Other coat colors such as wheaten or brindle can occur, but black is most common.
199.guidelines: Classify as Scottish Terrier when the dog is a compact, low-set terrier with a wiry coat, erect pointed ears, and a distinctive long bearded muzzle. Distinguish it from the West Highland White Terrier by coat color (Scottish Terriers are usually black, brindle, or wheaten, not white), from the Schnauzer by the Scottie's lower body, shorter legs, and more compact outline, and from the Cairn Terrier or Norwich Terrier by its longer head, heavier beard, and more formal upright ear-and-tail silhouette.

name: Tibetan Terrier
Canis lupus familiaris
200.description: Small-to-medium dog breed with a sturdy, square build, a broad head, and a profuse long double coat that often falls over the eyes and face. The coat may be straight or slightly wavy and appears in many colors, commonly white, black, cream, gold, gray, or mixed patterns. It has a bearded muzzle, heavily feathered ears and legs, and a plumed tail carried curled over the back.
200.guidelines: Classify as Tibetan Terrier when the dog has a shaggy, full-body coat, hair covering the eyes, a compact medium build, and a tail that curls over the back. Do not confuse with Lhasa Apso, which is usually lower, longer-bodied, and smaller; Bearded Collie, which is larger and longer-faced; or Soft-coated Wheaten Terrier, which is typically more uniformly wheaten-colored and has a terrier outline rather than the rounded, heavily coated Tibetan Terrier look.

name: Silky Terrier
Canis lupus familiaris
201.description: Small toy terrier with a fine, straight, silky coat, typically blue and tan or silver-gray and tan. It has a slightly longer body than a Yorkshire Terrier, an elegant but compact build, erect V-shaped ears, and a longer muzzle than many other toy breeds. The coat often parts along the back and hangs smoothly rather than appearing fluffy or curly.
201.guidelines: Classify as Silky Terrier when the dog is a small terrier with a long, smooth blue-and-tan silky coat and a somewhat elongated body. Distinguish it from the Yorkshire Terrier by its slightly larger size, longer body, and less compact, less doll-like face. Avoid confusing it with Australian Terrier, which has a harsher, scruffier coat and a less sleek outline, or other toy dogs with long hair that lack the characteristic blue-and-tan terrier coloring and erect terrier ears.

name: Soft-coated Wheaten Terrier
Canis lupus familiaris
202.description: A medium-sized terrier with a compact, sturdy build; a soft, silky to gently wavy wheaten-colored coat ranging from pale cream to warm tan; a bearded muzzle; dark eyes partly hidden by shaggy facial hair; and small V-shaped ears that fold forward. Puppies are often darker brown or blackish before the coat lightens with age.
202.guidelines: Classify as Soft-coated Wheaten Terrier when the dog has a uniformly wheaten, soft shaggy coat and terrier outline with a distinct beard and folded ears. Do not confuse it with Irish Terrier, which has a harsher wiry red coat and a narrower, more angular head; Kerry Blue Terrier, which is blue-gray rather than wheaten; or doodle-type mixes and Portuguese Water Dogs, which usually have curlier coats and lack the classic wheaten terrier head and expression. Distinguish from Glen of Imaal Terrier and Border Terrier by the softer, silkier coat, lighter wheaten color, and taller leggier build.

name: West Highland White Terrier
Canis lupus familiaris
203.description: A small, sturdy terrier breed with a compact body, a harsh pure white double coat, erect pointed ears, dark round eyes, and a black nose. The face is rounded and shaggy, and the tail is fairly short and carried upright.
203.guidelines: Classify as West Highland White Terrier when the dog is a small white terrier with erect triangular ears and a compact, sturdy build. Do not confuse it with the Maltese or Bichon Frise, which have longer or curlier coats and drop ears, or with other white terriers such as the Sealyham Terrier or Miniature Schnauzer, which typically have longer bodies, heavier furnishings, or distinctive beards and eyebrow shaping. The key cues are the all-white coat, upright ears, terrier proportions, and typical Westie face.

name: Lhasa Apso
Canis lupus familiaris
204.description: A small, sturdy toy dog with a compact body, short muzzle, dark round eyes, and pendant ears hidden by a long, dense coat. The coat is typically straight or slightly wavy and often floor-length, especially around the head, where it forms a heavy facial fall with a distinct beard and mustache. Common colors include gold, cream, white, black, gray, parti-color, and mixed light shades.
204.guidelines: Classify as Lhasa Apso when the dog is small and heavily coated with a long curtain-like coat, pronounced beard and mustache, and a relatively longer muzzle than very flat-faced toy breeds. Distinguish it from the Shih Tzu by its less brachycephalic face and usually less wide-set eyes; from the Maltese by its silkier pure-white coat and finer build; and from the Havanese by the Havanese's softer, more obviously wavy coat and lighter, springier outline.

name: flat-coated retriever
Canis lupus familiaris
205.description: A medium-to-large retriever with a solid black or liver coat, a long narrow head, dropped ears, and a straight, moderately long coat with clear feathering on the ears, legs, chest, and especially the tail. The body is athletic and slightly leggy, giving a leaner outline than heavier retriever breeds.
205.guidelines: Classify as flat-coated retriever when the dog has a sleek mostly flat coat with feathering, a long retriever muzzle, and an elegant athletic build. Do not confuse it with a black Labrador retriever, which has a shorter coat, broader head, thicker "otter" tail, and less feathering. Also distinguish it from a golden retriever or wavy-coated retriever by the typically solid black or liver color and flatter, less curly coat.

name: Curly-coated Retriever
Canis lupus familiaris
206.description: A medium-to-large retriever with a lean, athletic build, long wedge-shaped muzzle, and a dense coat of tight, crisp curls. The curls usually cover most of the body, while the face is smoother with shorter hair. Common colors are solid black or liver, and the ears are small and pendant.
206.guidelines: Classify as Curly-coated Retriever when the dog has a distinctly curly all-over coat combined with a long, narrow retriever head and relatively long legs. Do not confuse it with the Chesapeake Bay Retriever or Flat-coated Retriever, which have wavy or straight coats rather than tight curls, or with Poodles, which usually have a curlier coat but a different head shape, grooming style, and overall outline. Also distinguish it from Irish Water Spaniels, which are curl-coated but typically have a more spaniel-like build and a characteristic rat tail.

name: golden retriever
Canis lupus familiaris
207.description: A medium-to-large retriever with a sturdy, athletic build, a broad head, drop ears, and a dense wavy or straight coat in shades of light cream to rich golden. The coat is often feathered on the legs, chest, tail, and underside, and the expression is soft and friendly.
207.guidelines: Classify as golden retriever when the dog has a solid cream-to-golden coat, floppy ears, a broad retriever head, and noticeable feathering. Puppies may be paler and fluffier but keep the same retriever shape. Avoid confusing it with Labrador retrievers, which usually have shorter, smoother coats with less feathering; flat-coated retrievers, which are typically darker and more slender-headed; and Great Pyrenees or other pale long-haired dogs, which are bulkier and not golden in type.

name: Labrador Retriever
Canis lupus familiaris
208.description: A medium-large, sturdy but athletic retriever with a broad head, medium-length muzzle, drop ears, and a short, dense coat. Typical colors are black, yellow, or chocolate. Compared with a Golden Retriever, it is usually more compact and muscular, with a smoother coat lacking long feathering.
208.guidelines: Classify as Labrador Retriever when the dog has a solid black, yellow/cream, or chocolate short coat, a broad skull, and an overall athletic retriever build without long fur on the legs, tail, chest, or ears. The main confusion is with Golden Retriever: Goldens have a longer, wavier coat with obvious feathering and a narrower, more elegant outline. Also distinguish from Flat-coated Retriever, which is slimmer with a longer head and longer coat, and from mixed-breed dogs that may share the color but lack the Labrador’s characteristic broad head, thick neck, and short dense coat.

name: Chesapeake Bay Retriever
Canis lupus familiaris
209.description: A medium-large retriever with a strong, muscular build, broad chest, and a short dense coat that is slightly wavy, especially over the shoulders, neck, and back. The coat is usually solid brown in shades from dark chocolate to lighter deadgrass or sedge tones, with a weather-resistant, somewhat oily texture. It has a broad head, medium drop ears, and an athletic working-dog posture.
209.guidelines: Classify as Chesapeake Bay Retriever when the dog shows a sturdy retriever build plus a short, dense, slightly wavy brown coat rather than a long or feathery one. Do not confuse with Labrador Retriever, which usually has a smoother straight coat and a less distinctly wavy, harsher-looking texture; or Flat-Coated Retriever, which has a much longer, shinier coat with feathering. Also distinguish from curly-coated retrievers by the absence of tight curls, and from generic brown mixed-breed dogs by the characteristic retriever proportions, broad head, and short wavy waterproof coat.

name: German Shorthaired Pointer
Canis lupus familiaris
210.description: A medium-to-large, athletic pointing dog with a short, sleek liver-and-white coat. Common patterns include solid liver, liver patches on white, roaning, and dense ticking. It has a lean muscular build, deep chest, long legs, a broad but refined head, and medium-length floppy ears.
210.guidelines: Classify as German Shorthaired Pointer when the dog is a short-coated, athletic pointer with liver-and-white coloring, often roaned or ticked, and a balanced sporting-dog build. Distinguish it from English Pointer by the German Shorthaired Pointer’s heavier liver roaning/ticking and slightly more solid, versatile gundog look; from German Wirehaired Pointer by the lack of a wiry coat, beard, and bushy eyebrows; and from Dalmatian by the brown liver markings and pointer body shape rather than black spots.

name: Vizsla
Canis lupus familiaris
211.description: A lean, medium-sized sporting dog with a smooth, short coat in solid golden-rust to reddish-gold. It has a deep chest, long legs, a refined head, a brown or liver nose, and long, thin, drooping ears. The body is athletic and lightly built rather than heavy or stocky.
211.guidelines: Classify as Vizsla when the dog is a sleek, short-haired pointer with a uniform golden-rust coat and soft drooping ears. Do not confuse it with the Rhodesian Ridgeback, which is larger, heavier, and usually shows a ridge along the back; the Redbone Coonhound, which is typically darker red with a houndier face and longer ears; the Weimaraner, which is gray rather than rust-colored; or the German Shorthaired Pointer, which usually has liver-and-white patterning instead of a solid coat.

name: English setter
Canis lupus familiaris
212.description: A medium-to-large sporting dog with a lean, elegant build, a long silky coat with feathering on the ears, chest, legs, belly, and tail, and a distinctive belton pattern: a white base coat flecked or mottled with black, blue, orange, lemon, or liver markings. The ears are long and drooping, the muzzle is fairly long, and the tail is carried level or slightly raised with feathering.
212.guidelines: Classify as English setter when the dog has the setter’s refined, athletic outline, long feathered coat, and characteristic white speckled or ticked belton coloring. Distinguish it from spaniels by its leggier build and longer muzzle, and from pointers by its much longer, silkier feathering. Compared with the Irish setter, it is usually white with colored speckling rather than solid red; compared with the Gordon setter, it lacks the black-and-tan pattern. Avoid confusing heavily feathered black-and-white dogs with border collies: English setters have drooping ears, a setter head shape, and a more evenly speckled coat.

name: Irish Setter
Canis lupus familiaris
213.description: A tall, elegant sporting dog with a lean athletic build, a long narrow head, and long pendant ears. The coat is rich chestnut to mahogany red, medium-long, silky, and often lightly wavy, with clear feathering on the ears, chest, belly, legs, and tail.
213.guidelines: Classify as Irish Setter when the dog has a solid deep red coat and the refined, leggy setter build with long silky feathering. Distinguish it from the English Setter by the lack of white speckling or belton pattern, from the Gordon Setter by the absence of black-and-tan coloring, and from red-coated spaniels or retrievers by its taller, slimmer body, longer muzzle, and more pronounced setter-type feathered ears and tail.

name: Gordon Setter
Canis lupus familiaris
214.description: A large, sturdy setter with a silky, moderately long feathered coat that is glossy black with rich tan markings on the muzzle, eyebrows, chest, legs, and under the tail. It has long, low-set pendant ears, a long muzzle, a deep chest, and feathering on the ears, chest, belly, legs, and tail.
214.guidelines: Classify as Gordon Setter when the dog is a black-and-tan setter with a long, silky feathered coat and long drooping ears. Distinguish it from the Irish Setter, which is solid reddish chestnut, and the English Setter, which is typically white with speckling or patches. It can resemble black-and-tan spaniels, but Gordon Setters are larger, longer-legged, and more setter-like in build, with a longer muzzle and less compact body.

name: Brittany
Canis lupus familiaris
215.description: A compact, athletic gun dog with a lightly built body, long legs, drop ears, and a characteristically very short or absent tail. The coat is usually white with orange or liver patches, often with ticking or roaning, and the face commonly has a narrow white blaze.
215.guidelines: Classify as Brittany when the dog is a small-to-medium, leggy spaniel-type hunting dog with a short tail and orange-and-white or liver-and-white coat, often speckled. Distinguish it from springer spaniels and cocker spaniels by its lighter build, longer legs, and much shorter tail; from setters by its shorter coat and more compact body; and from pointers by its softer spaniel-like head, drop ears, and feathering.

name: Clumber Spaniel
Canis lupus familiaris
216.description: A low-set, heavy-boned spaniel with a long body, broad head, deep muzzle, droopy eyes, and long pendant ears. The coat is dense and mostly white, typically with lemon or orange markings on the ears, face, or body.
216.guidelines: Classify as Clumber Spaniel when the dog is a solid, substantial spaniel with a predominantly white coat and pale lemon or orange patches, especially on the ears and around the face. Distinguish it from English Springer Spaniels and Cocker Spaniels, which are usually lighter-built, leggier, and less massive in the head and body; and from setters, which are taller, slimmer, and more feathered.

name: English Springer Spaniel
Canis lupus familiaris
217.description: A medium-sized, leggy spaniel with a compact but athletic build, long drooping feathered ears, and a soft wavy coat with feathering on the legs, chest, and tail. Typical coloring includes liver and white, black and white, or tricolor, often with a white blaze and freckling on the muzzle or legs.
217.guidelines: Classify as English Springer Spaniel when the dog is a sporting spaniel with longer legs and a taller, less low-slung build than cocker spaniels, plus long pendant ears and moderate feathering. Common look-alikes include the English Cocker Spaniel, which is smaller, shorter-legged, and rounder-headed, and the Welsh Springer Spaniel, which is characteristically red-and-white rather than black/white or liver/white. Do not confuse with Brittany dogs, which usually have shorter ears and less spaniel feathering.

name: Welsh Springer Spaniel
Canis lupus familiaris
218.description: A medium-sized, compact spaniel with a sturdy build, long pendant ears, and a silky coat with moderate feathering on the chest, legs, and tail. The coat is characteristically red and white, often with a rich chestnut-red color and clear white areas, sometimes with light ticking or freckling on the muzzle or legs.
218.guidelines: Classify as Welsh Springer Spaniel when the dog is a red-and-white spaniel with a balanced, slightly rectangular build and moderate feathering. Do not confuse with the English Springer Spaniel, which is often black-and-white or liver-and-white and usually shows a more variable pattern; or the Brittany, which typically has shorter ears, less coat feathering, and a more lightly built sporting-dog outline. Also distinguish from the Cavalier King Charles Spaniel, which is smaller, toy-sized, and shorter-legged.

name: English Cocker Spaniel
Canis lupus familiaris
219.description: A small to medium-sized, compact spaniel with a rounded head, medium-length muzzle, large dark eyes, and long, pendulous feathered ears. The coat is silky and may be solid black, golden, liver, cream, or particolor/roan, often with feathering on the legs, chest, and underside.
219.guidelines: Classify as English Cocker Spaniel when the dog is a compact sporting spaniel with long low-set feathered ears, a moderately long silky coat, and a softer, less exaggerated build than showier toy spaniels. Distinguish it from the American Cocker Spaniel by its longer muzzle, less domed skull, and less profuse coat; from Springer Spaniels by its smaller size and shorter body; and from Cavalier King Charles Spaniels by its sturdier sporting build and longer muzzle.

name: Sussex Spaniel
Canis lupus familiaris
220.description: A low-set, heavy-boned spaniel with a long body, short legs, and a solid liver-brown coat. It has long, feathered ears, a broad head with a serious expression, and moderate feathering on the chest, legs, and tail.
220.guidelines: Classify as Sussex Spaniel when the dog is distinctly long and low with a uniform rich brown/liver coat and spaniel ears. Distinguish it from Cocker Spaniels and Springer Spaniels, which are leggier and often have parti-color patterns; from Clumber Spaniels, which are usually white with lemon or orange markings and heavier-faced; and from Field Spaniels, which are taller, less low-slung, and typically have a sleeker outline.

name: Irish water spaniel
Canis lupus familiaris
221.description: A medium-to-large spaniel with a dense, tightly curled liver-brown coat, a long narrow muzzle, and long curly hanging ears. It has a distinctive topknot of looser curls on the head, a bearded face, and a sturdy athletic build. The tail is characteristically long, tapering, and much less curly than the body, giving a smooth 'rat tail' appearance.
221.guidelines: Classify as Irish water spaniel when the dog shows the classic dark brown curly coat, spaniel head and ears, and especially the smooth or sparsely coated tapering tail. Do not confuse with poodles, which usually have a squarer muzzle, different grooming, and a fully coated tail; or curly-coated retrievers, which have shorter ear curls, a less pronounced topknot, and a more retriever-like head. Also distinguish from other spaniels by the much tighter curls and solid liver color.

name: Great Pyrenees
Canis lupus familiaris
222.description: Large, heavily built white dog with a dense double coat that is long, thick, and slightly wavy to straight. The body is sturdy and muscular, with a broad head, drop ears, dark eyes and nose, a full neck ruff, and a plumed tail. Most examples are solid white, sometimes with faint cream shading.
222.guidelines: Classify as Great Pyrenees when the dog is a large all-white livestock-guardian type with a broad head, drop ears, and a very full, fluffy coat. Do not confuse it with the Kuvasz, which is usually leaner and more square-headed with a more distinctly wavy coat and a less massive overall build. Also distinguish it from white retrievers or other large white dogs by the heavier guardian-dog frame, thicker neck ruff, and more imposing, shaggy appearance.

name: Schipperke
Canis lupus familiaris
223.description: A small, compact spitz-type dog with a thick solid-black coat, upright pointed ears, and a wedge-shaped, foxlike face. The body is short and sturdy, often with a pronounced neck ruff and a fluffy tail or tailless rear silhouette.
223.guidelines: Classify as Schipperke when the dog is distinctly small, black, and fox-faced with erect ears and a dense coat. Do not confuse it with the larger Belgian Sheepdog/Groenendael, which is much taller and longer-legged, or with black Pomeranians, which are fluffier, rounder-faced, and more toy-like. Also avoid confusing it with general black mixed-breed spitz dogs; Schipperkes are compact, fine-muzzled, and characteristically all black.

name: Groenendael
Canis lupus familiaris
224.description: A Groenendael is a variety of Belgian Shepherd: a medium-to-large, elegant herding dog with a solid black, long-haired coat, a narrow wedge-shaped head, and upright pointed ears. The coat is full and straight to slightly wavy, with a pronounced neck ruff, feathering on the legs, and a plumed tail.
224.guidelines: Classify as Groenendael when the dog is a black long-coated Belgian Shepherd with erect ears and a refined, athletic build. Distinguish it from the Belgian Malinois, which is short-haired and usually fawn with a black mask; from the German Shepherd, which is heavier-bodied and commonly tan-and-black with a broader head and sloping back; and from other black spitz or shepherd-type dogs by the Groenendael’s solid black color, long flowing coat, and distinctly Belgian Shepherd head shape.

name: Belgian Malinois
Canis lupus familiaris
225.description: A medium-large herding dog with a lean, athletic build, short straight coat, and a fawn to mahogany body paired with a distinct black mask. The ears are erect, the muzzle is long and wedge-shaped, and the coat is usually fairly uniform in color rather than strongly patterned, sometimes with slight dark overlay on the back.
225.guidelines: Classify as Belgian Malinois when the dog has a short coat, tan/fawn body, black face mask, and upright ears in a sleek shepherd-like build. Do not confuse it with the German Shepherd, which is usually heavier-bodied with a longer, fuller coat and a black saddle pattern; or the Dutch Shepherd, which is typically brindled. Also distinguish it from longer-haired Belgian shepherd varieties such as the Tervuren, which have a noticeably fuller coat.

name: Briard
Canis lupus familiaris
226.description: A large, long-coated herding dog with a shaggy, wavy coat, heavy facial hair forming a beard and mustache, and long hair that often partly covers the eyes. Coat colors are commonly tawny, fawn, gray, or black. The body is sturdy and rectangular, and when visible the tail is long with a distinct hook or J-shaped curve at the tip.
226.guidelines: Classify as Briard only when the dog shows the breed’s characteristic shaggy coat, bearded face, and usually a long tail ending in a hooked J-shape. Do not confuse with the Bearded Collie, which is typically lighter-built with a flatter, more parted coat and white markings, or the Berger Picard, which has a harsher shorter coat and clearly erect ears. Also distinguish from other long-haired shepherd dogs by the Briard’s dense full-body coat, heavily furnished face, and curved tail tip.

name: Australian Kelpie
Canis lupus familiaris
227.description: A medium-sized herding dog resembling a small, short-coated Border Collie. It has a lean, athletic build, erect pointed ears, a wedge-shaped head, and a smooth short coat most often in black, red, chocolate, or fawn, sometimes with tan markings or a small white chest patch.
227.guidelines: Classify as Australian Kelpie when the dog is a compact, agile herding type with upright ears and a short sleek coat. Do not confuse it with the Border Collie, which is usually fluffier and longer-coated, or with the Australian Cattle Dog, which is stockier and commonly blue or red speckled/roan. Also distinguish it from mixed-breed pinscher-type dogs by the Kelpie’s balanced herding-dog proportions, wedge head, and typical solid black/red/chocolate/fawn coloring.

name: Komondor
Canis lupus familiaris
228.description: A large, powerfully built white livestock-guardian dog with a distinctive corded coat that hangs in long, heavy tassels like a mop or dreadlocks, often covering the face and legs. Some individuals, especially younger or less fully corded dogs, may appear fluffier or woollier rather than fully corded.
228.guidelines: Classify as Komondor when the dog is large and white with a naturally corded or woolly coat, especially long rope-like cords over the whole body. Do not confuse with the Puli, which is smaller and lighter-built and commonly black or other colors, or with the Bergamasco Shepherd, whose coat forms flatter felted mats and is usually gray or multicolored rather than solid white. Also distinguish from fluffy white breeds such as the Old English Sheepdog or South Russian Ovcharka, which lack the Komondor’s long mop-like cords.

name: Old English Sheepdog
Canis lupus familiaris
229.description: A large, sturdy herding dog with a very thick, long, shaggy double coat that often covers the eyes and much of the face. The coat is typically white with gray, blue, or black patches, especially over the body and ears, giving a fluffy, rounded outline. Many have a naturally short or docked tail.
229.guidelines: Classify as Old English Sheepdog when the dog is heavily built and covered in a dense, tousled shaggy coat, usually white combined with gray or blue. Distinguish it from the Bearded Collie, which is leaner with a flatter, more parted coat and a longer visible muzzle; from the Polish Lowland Sheepdog, which is smaller and less massive; and from poodle-coated or doodle-type dogs, which have curlier rather than shaggy, sheepdog-like fur. The characteristic bulky body, profuse coat over the eyes, and white-and-gray bobtail appearance are key cues.

name: Shetland Sheepdog
Canis lupus familiaris
230.description: A small, long-haired herding dog that resembles a miniature Rough Collie, with a refined wedge-shaped head, relatively short muzzle, erect tipped ears, and a very full double coat with a heavy mane and frill. Common colors include sable and white, black and white, blue merle, and tricolor.
230.guidelines: Classify as Shetland Sheepdog when the dog is small and elegant with a profuse coat, prominent neck ruff, collie-like face, and semi-erect ears that tip forward. Distinguish it from the Rough Collie by its much smaller size, shorter head and muzzle, and more compact proportions. Distinguish it from Border Collies and Australian Shepherds by the fuller mane, more foxlike collie head, and less athletic, less workmanlike build.

name: Rough Collie
Canis lupus familiaris
231.description: A medium-to-large herding dog with a long, abundant coat, a prominent white mane or ruff around the neck, a long narrow muzzle, and a wedge-shaped head. The ears are small and partly tipped forward, and the coat is commonly sable-and-white, tricolor, blue merle, or similar collie patterns.
231.guidelines: Classify as Rough Collie when the dog has a distinctly long coat, heavy neck ruff, elegant narrow head, and long pointed muzzle. Do not confuse it with the smaller Shetland Sheepdog, which is usually more compact with a shorter muzzle and lighter build, or with the Smooth Collie, which has the same general head shape but a short coat. Also distinguish it from Border Collies and Australian Shepherds, which typically have broader heads, different ear carriage, and less of the classic full collie mane.

name: Border Collie
Canis lupus familiaris
232.description: A medium-sized herding dog with an athletic build, a medium or short coat, and coloration commonly in black and white, brown and white, or blue merle. Most have a distinct white blaze running up the muzzle and forehead, often with white on the chest, legs, and tail tip.
232.guidelines: Classify as Border Collie when the dog shows the breed’s lean, agile herding-dog build, alert expression, and typical white facial blaze with black, brown, or merle coloring. Do not confuse it with the Australian Shepherd, which is usually stockier with a heavier coat and often a bobbed tail, or the Shetland Sheepdog, which is smaller with a fuller mane and a narrower, more refined face. Also distinguish it from rough collies, which have a much longer muzzle and a fuller, more luxuriant coat.

name: Bouvier des Flandres
Canis lupus familiaris
233.description: A large, sturdy herding dog with a rough, shaggy, unkempt-looking double coat, most often black but also seen in gray, brindle, or fawn tones. It has a broad, powerful body, heavy legs, a large head, and a distinctive facial furnishing with pronounced moustache, beard, and bushy eyebrows that partly cover the eyes.
233.guidelines: Classify as Bouvier des Flandres when the dog is a heavy, compact, rough-coated working dog with a dark shaggy coat and strong beard/moustache. Do not confuse it with giant schnauzers, which are usually cleaner-outlined, more uniformly trimmed, and have a harsher wiry coat with a more defined schnauzer silhouette; or with black Russian terriers, which are often glossier black, more terrier-like in outline, and commonly show fuller dropped furnishings. Also distinguish it from Briards and bearded collies, which are longer-bodied with a more flowing coat, and from Old English sheepdogs, which are much fuller-coated and typically gray-and-white.

name: Rottweiler
Canis lupus familiaris
234.description: A large, powerful, muscular dog with a short, dense black coat and sharply defined rust-to-tan markings above the eyes, on the muzzle, chest, lower legs, and under the tail. The head is broad with a strong muzzle, the body is compact and substantial, and the ears are medium-sized and folded. The tail may be docked or naturally long.
234.guidelines: Classify as Rottweiler when the dog has the classic black-and-tan pattern combined with a heavy, robust build and broad head. Distinguish it from Dobermans, which are slimmer, leggier, and more wedge-headed; from black-and-tan coonhounds, which have longer ears and a lighter hound build; and from mixed black-and-tan dogs, which usually lack the Rottweiler’s stocky body, broad chest, and characteristic rust markings placement.

name: German Shepherd
Canis lupus familiaris
235.description: A large, athletic dog breed with a long wedge-shaped muzzle, erect pointed ears, and a long bushy tail. The coat is typically medium to long and most often black and tan with a dark saddle and mask, though it can also be sable, solid black, or gray-toned.
235.guidelines: Classify as German Shepherd when the dog has the breed’s classic shepherd build: upright ears, elongated muzzle, sloping back, and black-and-tan or sable shepherd coat. Do not confuse with Belgian Malinois, which is usually slimmer, shorter-coated, and more uniformly fawn with a black mask; or with wolfdog/husky types, which often have curlier tails, lighter facial markings, or thicker spitz-like coats. Exclude mixed-breed shepherds if the overall appearance is not clearly German Shepherd.

name: Dobermann
Canis lupus familiaris
236.description: A sleek, athletic dog breed with a lean muscular body, deep chest, long legs, and a short smooth coat. Most examples are black-and-rust or red-and-rust, with tan markings on the muzzle, chest, legs, and above the eyes. The head is long and wedge-shaped, and the ears may be naturally floppy or cropped erect.
236.guidelines: Classify as Dobermann when the dog has the breed’s slender but powerful build, short close coat, and characteristic rust points on a black or red body. Do not require pointed ears, since many Dobermanns have natural uncropped ears. Distinguish from Rottweiler by the lighter, taller, more elegant frame and narrower head; from Miniature Pinscher by the much larger size and stronger build; and from black-and-tan coonhounds or similar hounds by the cleaner outline, shorter coat, and more square, working-dog proportions.

name: Miniature Pinscher
Canis lupus familiaris
237.description: A very small, fine-boned toy dog with a short, smooth coat, a compact square body, long slender legs, and a narrow wedge-shaped head. The ears are often large and erect or cropped to stand sharply upright. Common colors include black-and-tan, red, and chocolate-and-tan, typically with crisp tan points on the muzzle, chest, and legs.
237.guidelines: Classify as Miniature Pinscher when the dog is tiny, sleek, and deer-like, with a short coat, slender build, and prominent upright ears. Do not confuse it with a Chihuahua, which usually has a rounder apple-shaped head, shorter muzzle, and softer overall proportions, or with a Manchester Terrier, which is typically larger and less toy-like. Also distinguish it from toy terriers with longer coats or heavier bodies; the Miniature Pinscher should look smooth-coated, elegant, and narrowly built.

name: Greater Swiss Mountain Dog
Canis lupus familiaris
238.description: A large, heavily built mountain dog with a short, dense tricolor coat: mostly black with rich rust markings on the cheeks, above the eyes, and legs, plus white on the muzzle, chest, and often a blaze up the face. It has a broad head, medium drop ears, a strong straight back, and a sturdy, muscular body.
238.guidelines: Classify as Greater Swiss Mountain Dog when the dog is a large, robust, short-haired Swiss tricolor with a broad head and clear black-rust-white pattern. Distinguish it from the Bernese Mountain Dog by its short coat rather than long, fluffy fur; from the Entlebucher Mountain Dog by its much larger, heavier build; and from the Appenzeller Sennenhund by its larger size, broader head, and typically less tightly curled tail.

name: Bernese Mountain Dog
Canis lupus familiaris
239.description: A large, sturdy dog with a long, slightly wavy tricolor coat: mostly black with a broad white chest blaze, white muzzle and facial blaze, and rich rust markings above the eyes, on the cheeks, and on the legs.
239.guidelines: Classify as Bernese Mountain Dog when the dog is a heavy-built, long-haired tri-colored mountain dog with the classic black-white-rust pattern and prominent white chest. Distinguish it from the Greater Swiss Mountain Dog, which has a similar color pattern but a short coat; from the Saint Bernard, which is bulkier and usually red-and-white or brown-and-white rather than crisply tricolored; and from Australian Shepherds or Border Collies, which are lighter-built and less massive, with different head shape and coat patterning.

name: Appenzeller Sennenhund
Canis lupus familiaris
240.description: A medium-sized, sturdy mountain dog with a short, smooth tricolor coat: black or occasionally brown as the base color, with symmetrical white markings on the blaze, muzzle, chest, feet, and tail tip, plus tan points above the eyes, on the cheeks, and legs. It has a broad head, drop ears, and a characteristic high-set tail that often curls over the back.
240.guidelines: Classify as Appenzeller Sennenhund when the dog is a compact, athletic Swiss mountain dog with a short tricolor coat and a tightly curled or carried-high tail. Distinguish it from the Greater Swiss Mountain Dog, which is larger, heavier, and usually has a straight tail; from the Bernese Mountain Dog, which has a much longer, fluffier coat; and from the Entlebucher Mountain Dog, which is generally lower, longer-bodied, and often has a less prominently curled tail.

name: Entlebucher Mountain Dog
Canis lupus familiaris
241.description: A medium-small, compact mountain dog with a sturdy build, short smooth coat, and distinct tricolor pattern: black body, tan markings on the face and legs, and white on the muzzle, chest, and feet. The head is broad with drop ears, and the tail is very short, naturally bobbed, or carried low.
241.guidelines: Classify as Entlebucher Mountain Dog when the dog is a compact, short-haired tricolor Swiss mountain dog with a black base coat, clear white chest blaze and muzzle, tan points, and a notably short or bobbed tail. Distinguish it from the larger Bernese Mountain Dog and Greater Swiss Mountain Dog by its smaller size and shorter coat, and from the Appenzeller Sennenhund by the Appenzeller’s more curled tail and lighter, less compact build. Do not confuse with generic tricolor hounds or mixed-breed dogs, which typically lack the characteristic Swiss mountain dog proportions and markings.

name: Boxer
Canis lupus familiaris
242.description: A medium-to-large, muscular dog breed with a deep chest, strong legs, and a compact, athletic build. The head is distinctive: broad and square with a short muzzle, pronounced stop, dark mask, and often a white blaze or chest markings. The coat is short and smooth, most commonly fawn or brindle with possible white markings.
242.guidelines: Classify as boxer when the dog has the breed’s square head, short broad muzzle, athletic body, and typical fawn or brindle short coat, often with a black mask and white chest or feet. Distinguish it from bulldogs by the boxer’s taller, leaner, more athletic build and longer legs; from bullmastiffs and mastiffs by its less massive body and shorter, squarer muzzle; and from pit bull–type dogs by the boxer’s more brachycephalic face, heavier jowls, and characteristic black mask.

name: Bullmastiff
Canis lupus familiaris
243.description: A large, powerfully built mastiff-type dog with a broad deep chest, thick neck, and muscular body. The head is large and square with a short dark muzzle, dropped ears, loose jowls, and a moderately wrinkled forehead. The coat is short and dense, commonly fawn, red, or brindle, often with a black mask.
243.guidelines: Classify as Bullmastiff when the dog is a heavy, compact mastiff with a broad square head, short muzzle, black mask, and moderate facial wrinkling. Do not confuse with Boxer, which is leaner, more athletic, and has a more upturned muzzle; English Mastiff, which is usually taller, heavier, and looser-skinned; or Boerboel/Cane Corso types, which tend to have less characteristic Bullmastiff head shape and expression.

name: Tibetan Mastiff
Canis lupus familiaris
244.description: A very large, heavily built dog with a dense double coat and a pronounced lion-like mane around the neck and shoulders. Typical coloration is black, black and tan, or gold, often with tan points and occasional white markings on the chest or feet. The head is broad, the muzzle is strong, the ears are pendant, and the tail is thick and usually carried curled over the back.
244.guidelines: Classify as Tibetan Mastiff when the dog is a giant, long-haired mastiff-type with a heavy frame, abundant coat, and especially a thick mane-like ruff. Distinguish it from Newfoundland by the more mastiff-like head, curled tail, and frequent tan-point patterning; from Leonberger by its less elongated muzzle and heavier, more compact build; and from Bernese Mountain Dog by its fuller mane, heavier body, and less regular tricolor pattern. Do not confuse it with other mountain or livestock guardian dogs that lack the dense mane and massive mastiff proportions.

name: French Bulldog
Canis lupus familiaris
245.description: A small, compact, muscular dog with a broad chest, short legs, a short smooth coat, and a flat, wrinkled face. It has a square, heavy head and very large upright bat-like ears. Common coat colors include brindle, fawn, black, cream, and white, often with piebald markings.
245.guidelines: Classify as French Bulldog when the dog has the breed’s hallmark oversized upright ears, short muzzle, compact stocky body, and smooth coat. Do not confuse with Boston Terrier, which is usually leggier with a more tuxedo-like black-and-white pattern and a less heavy build, or with Pug, which has small folded ears and a tightly curled tail. Also distinguish from English Bulldog, which is much larger, lower, and heavier with broader shoulders and smaller rose-shaped ears.

name: Great Dane
Canis lupus familiaris
246.description: A giant dog breed with a very tall, long-legged body, deep chest, long neck, and short smooth coat. The head is large and rectangular with a long muzzle; ears may be natural and floppy or cropped upright. Common coat colors include fawn with a black mask, brindle, harlequin white with black patches, mantle black-and-white, solid black, blue, and merle.
246.guidelines: Classify as Great Dane when the dog is notably giant and leggy, with a short coat, deep chest, and long rectangular head. Do not confuse with Mastiffs, which are heavier, broader, and shorter-legged with a more massive head and looser skin; Greyhounds or other sighthounds, which are slimmer and narrower-headed; or German Shorthaired Pointers and similar spotted breeds, which are much smaller and less massive. Harlequin and mantle Great Danes can resemble other black-and-white dogs, but their exceptional height, heavy bone, and large head distinguish them.

name: Saint Bernard
Canis lupus familiaris
247.description: A giant, heavily built dog with a broad head, short muzzle, drooping jowls, and soft droopy eyes. The coat is thick and dense, usually white with large red, mahogany, brown, or brindle patches and often a dark facial mask; ears are medium-sized and pendant, and the tail is long and bushy.
247.guidelines: Classify as Saint Bernard when the dog is very large and heavy-boned, with the characteristic white-and-reddish patched coat, broad face, and loose expression. Distinguish it from the Bernese Mountain Dog, which is slimmer and consistently black-rust-white; from the Newfoundland, which is usually solid black or dark brown with a different head shape; and from the Great Pyrenees, which is mostly white and less blocky-faced. Do not rely on rescue-barrel accessories, which are optional and not defining.

name: husky
Canis lupus familiaris
248.description: A medium-sized spitz-type dog with an athletic build, erect triangular ears, a wedge-shaped head, almond-shaped eyes, and a thick double coat. Common coat patterns include black-and-white, gray-and-white, red-and-white, sable, or solid white, often with a distinct facial mask. The tail is bushy, and the overall look is wolf-like but compact and domesticated.
248.guidelines: Classify as husky when the dog shows the typical northern spitz build, erect ears, dense coat, bushy tail, and common husky facial mask or coloring. Do not require only black-and-white coloration: white, gray, red, and sable huskies also belong. Distinguish from Alaskan malamute by the husky’s lighter build, narrower head, and less bulky body; from Samoyed by the lack of the Samoyed’s consistently fluffy pure-white coat and rounder face; from German shepherd or wolfdog by the thicker spitz coat, more compact proportions, and curled or plume-like tail.

name: Alaskan Malamute
Canis lupus familiaris
249.description: A large, powerfully built spitz-type dog with a broad head, erect triangular ears, almond-shaped eyes, and a very thick double coat. The coat is heavier and fluffier than a Siberian Husky’s, commonly in gray-and-white, black-and-white, sable, red, or seal patterns, often with a white face mask, chest, legs, and underside. It has a deep chest, sturdy legs, and a full bushy tail carried over the back.
249.guidelines: Classify as Alaskan Malamute when the dog appears large-boned, strong, and heavily coated, with a broad wolf-like face and dense plush fur. Distinguish it from the Siberian Husky by its bulkier build, broader head, smaller-looking ears relative to the head, and thicker coat; Huskies are usually lighter, leggier, and more refined. Also avoid confusing it with wolfdogs or wolves: Malamutes have a more domestic dog expression, fuller coat, and typical pet-dog proportions and markings.

name: husky
Canis lupus familiaris
250.description: A medium-sized spitz-type dog with erect triangular ears, almond-shaped eyes that may be blue, brown, or mismatched, and a thick double coat. Most have a gray-and-white, black-and-white, red-and-white, or all-white coat with a pale face, distinct mask pattern, and bushy tail often carried in a curve. The build is athletic and fairly lean rather than heavy, with a wolf-like head and overall sled-dog appearance.
250.guidelines: Classify as husky when the dog has the familiar sled-dog look: erect ears, dense coat, facial mask, light or contrasting markings, and a medium, agile build. Do not confuse with Alaskan malamute, which is larger, heavier-boned, and broader-headed; Samoyed or American Eskimo Dog, which are usually fluffier and more uniformly white without the typical husky mask; or wolfdogs/wolves, which tend to have longer muzzles, less distinct pet-dog mask patterns, and a less compact domestic-dog appearance.

name: Dalmatian
Canis lupus familiaris
251.description: Medium-sized dog breed with a short, smooth white coat covered in distinct round black or liver-colored spots. The body is lean and athletic, with a deep chest, long legs, a narrow muzzle, and drop ears; puppies may have fewer visible spots that develop with age.
251.guidelines: Classify as Dalmatian when the dog has the breed’s signature spotted white coat and athletic hound-like build. Do not confuse it with English setter or pointer breeds, which may also be white with dark markings but usually have larger patches, ticking, feathered fur, or a less uniformly spotted pattern. Exclude merle-coated dogs, whose mottling is marbled rather than crisp round spots.

name: Affenpinscher
Canis lupus familiaris
252.description: A very small, sturdy toy dog with a rough, shaggy black or dark coat, a short muzzle, and a distinctive monkey-like face. It has a rounded head, prominent beard and eyebrows, small folded ears, and a tail often carried high over the back.
252.guidelines: Classify as Affenpinscher when the dog is a tiny wiry-coated toy breed with a short snout and a scruffy, bearded, monkey-like expression. Do not confuse it with the Brussels Griffon, which usually has a rounder face and often a red or smoother coat; or the Miniature Schnauzer, which is larger with a longer muzzle and clearer schnauzer patterning. Also distinguish it from small terriers by the Affenpinscher's shorter face, more compact toy build, and characteristic shaggy facial furnishings.

name: Basenji
Canis lupus familiaris
253.description: A small, lightly built dog breed with a short smooth coat, erect pointed ears, a wedge-shaped head, long legs, and a tightly curled tail. Common colors include red and white, black and white, tricolor, or brindle, often with white on the chest, feet, and tail tip.
253.guidelines: Classify as Basenji when the dog shows the breed’s compact but elegant build, very short coat, upright ears, and especially the tightly curled tail. Do not confuse it with small terriers or sighthounds: Basenjis have a curled tail and a distinctive clean wedge-shaped head, unlike rat terriers or toy fox terriers, which often have a straight tail, or whippets, which have folded ears and a longer, lower silhouette.

name: pug
Canis lupus familiaris
254.description: A small, compact toy dog with a short, square body, a broad round head, a very short wrinkled muzzle, large prominent eyes, small folded ears, and a tightly curled tail. The coat is short and smooth, most often fawn with a black mask or solid black.
254.guidelines: Classify as pug when the dog has a distinctly flat, wrinkled face, large round eyes, a compact build, and a tightly curled tail. Do not confuse with French bulldog or Boston terrier, which have erect bat-like ears and less tightly curled tails; with bulldogs, which are much heavier and broader; or with puggle and other mixes, which usually have a longer muzzle, less facial wrinkling, and a less compact toy-dog shape.

name: Leonberger
Canis lupus familiaris
255.description: A giant, powerfully built dog with a long, thick double coat, usually golden-brown to reddish-brown or lion-colored, often with darker shading on the back and a distinct black facial mask. It has a broad head, dropped ears, a full mane-like ruff around the neck and chest, heavy bone, and a bushy tail.
255.guidelines: Classify this as a Leonberger when the dog is very large and lion-like, with a black mask and a long tawny or golden-brown coat. Distinguish it from the Newfoundland, which is usually solid black or black-and-white and more heavily coated; the Saint Bernard, which is typically white with red-brown patches and less uniformly lion-colored; and long-haired mastiff types such as the Tibetan Mastiff, which are stockier, often have a shorter muzzle, and usually lack the Leonberger’s characteristic black-mask-on-golden-coat look.

name: Newfoundland
Canis lupus familiaris
256.description: A giant, heavy-boned dog with a massive body, broad head, short square muzzle, and small pendant ears. It has a very thick, dense, water-resistant double coat that is usually solid black, but can also be brown, gray, or black-and-white. The coat is long and shaggy rather than sleek, and the overall build is powerful but gentle-looking.
256.guidelines: Classify as Newfoundland when the dog is very large and sturdy with a broad head, short muzzle, and dense shaggy coat, often black or black-and-white. Do not confuse with Landseer, which is specifically the black-and-white color variety often treated separately in dog labeling; if the category must cover all examples here, include both solid and black-and-white Newfoundlands. Distinguish from Flat-coated Retriever or Labrador Retriever by the Newfoundland's much heavier build, larger head, shorter muzzle, and far thicker coat. Distinguish from Leonberger by the Newfoundland's broader head, darker common coloration, and less leonine tan-and-black patterning.

name: Great Pyrenees
Canis lupus familiaris
257.description: A very large, heavily built dog with a thick, long white or mostly white fluffy double coat. It has a broad head, dark eyes and nose, small drop ears, a full plumed tail, and a sturdy, calm-looking stance.
257.guidelines: Classify as Great Pyrenees when the dog is giant-sized and covered in a dense white coat, often with slight cream, tan, gray, or badger markings around the ears or face. Distinguish it from the Kuvasz by the Great Pyrenees' heavier build, broader head, and longer shaggier coat; from white Golden Retrievers or Labradors by its much thicker coat, larger guardian-dog frame, and smaller ears; and from Samoyeds by its drop ears rather than erect ears and its less fox-like face.

name: Samoyed
Canis lupus familiaris
258.description: A medium-to-large spitz-type dog with a thick, very fluffy white coat, a dense ruff around the neck, small upright triangular ears, dark eyes and nose, and a plumed tail usually curled over the back. The body looks sturdy but elegant, with a broad smiling face and a soft, cloudlike outline.
258.guidelines: Classify as Samoyed when the dog is an all-white, long-haired spitz with a heavy double coat, erect ears, and a full curled tail. Do not confuse it with the American Eskimo Dog or Japanese Spitz, which are usually smaller and finer-boned, or with white Huskies and other sled dogs, which have a leaner build, less voluminous coat, and typically lack the characteristic fluffy 'smiling' Samoyed appearance.

name: Pomeranian
Canis lupus familiaris
259.description: A very small toy spitz dog with a compact body, abundant long double coat, full ruff around the neck, plume-like tail carried over the back, and a short pointed foxlike face with small upright ears. Common colors include orange, cream, white, black, sable, and particolor.
259.guidelines: Classify as Pomeranian when the dog is tiny and distinctly fluffy, with a rounded puffball outline, erect ears, foxlike muzzle, and a heavily plumed tail over the back. Do not confuse with German Spitz or other spitz breeds, which are usually larger and less compact; Chihuahua, which has a much shorter coat or larger ears relative to the head; or Papillon, which has a finer coat and large fringed ears rather than a dense all-over spitz coat.

name: Chow Chow
Canis lupus familiaris
260.description: A sturdy, compact spitz-type dog with a very dense double coat, a broad lion-like ruff around the neck, small triangular upright ears, deep-set eyes, and a tightly curled tail carried over the back. The coat is usually red, cream, black, blue, or cinnamon, and the breed is especially known for its blue-black tongue.
260.guidelines: Classify as Chow Chow when the dog has a heavy fluffy coat, a mane-like ruff, a square compact build, small erect ears, and the characteristic blue-black tongue if visible. Do not confuse with Samoyed, which is usually pure white with a lighter, smiling expression and longer muzzle; Eurasier, which is less heavily coated with a softer, less massive head; or Pomeranian, which is much smaller and finer-boned. Shar Pei may share a broad head but has short wrinkled skin rather than a dense plush coat.

name: Keeshond
Canis lupus familiaris
261.description: A small to medium spitz-type dog with a very thick double coat, usually gray, silver, and black with a lighter cream undercoat. It has a foxlike face, small pointed upright ears, dark facial shading that often forms a mask or “spectacles,” a dense neck ruff, and a heavily plumed tail curled over the back.
261.guidelines: Classify as Keeshond when the dog is a compact, fluffy spitz with a gray-silver-and-black coat, dark facial mask, and curled plume tail. Do not confuse it with Pomeranian, which is much smaller and rounder-faced; Samoyed, which is larger and predominantly white; Norwegian elkhound, which is leaner with a less profuse coat and less pronounced facial spectacles; or Eurasier/German spitz types, which can look similar but often lack the Keeshond’s characteristic gray-black shading and distinct face markings.

name: Brussels Griffon
Canis lupus familiaris
262.description: Toy-sized companion dog with a compact, square body, a large rounded head, very short muzzle, and prominent dark eyes that create an expressive almost human-like face. The coat may be smooth or rough, and common colors include red, black, black-and-tan, and belge; the rough-coated form often has a beard and eyebrows, while the smooth-coated form has a sleek, close coat.
262.guidelines: Classify as Brussels Griffon when the dog is very small and compact with a brachycephalic face, short nose, large round eyes, and griffon-like expression. Distinguish it from a pug by its less wrinkled face, lighter finer build, and often less tightly curled tail; from an Affenpinscher by the much shorter muzzle and rounder eyes; and from other toy brachycephalic dogs such as Chihuahua or French Bulldog by the characteristic griffon head shape, square body, and either rough bearded coat or smooth griffon coat.

name: Pembroke Welsh Corgi
Canis lupus familiaris
263.description: A small herding dog with a long, low body, short legs, a foxlike face, and large upright pointed ears. The coat is usually red, sable, fawn, or black and tan with common white markings on the chest, muzzle, neck, and legs. Compared with the Cardigan, the tail is very short or absent, and the build is compact but sturdy.
263.guidelines: Classify as Pembroke Welsh Corgi when the dog shows the classic low-slung corgi build, erect oversized ears, and especially a naturally very short tail or docked-looking tail. Distinguish it from the Cardigan Welsh Corgi, which usually has a longer foxlike tail, rounder larger ears, and often a slightly longer body. Also avoid confusion with dachshunds or short-legged mixed breeds: Pembrokes have a broader herding-dog head, thicker double coat, and upright ears rather than the dachshund's long muzzle and drop ears.

name: Cardigan Welsh Corgi
Canis lupus familiaris
264.description: A small herding dog with a long, low body, short legs, a deep chest, and very large upright ears. It has a foxlike face and, unlike the Pembroke, a full long tail. The coat is medium-length and comes in varied colors and patterns, including brindle, black-and-white, red-and-white, sable, blue merle, and tricolor.
264.guidelines: Classify as Cardigan Welsh Corgi when the dog has the corgi build but clearly shows a long tail, large rounded upright ears, and a slightly heavier, longer-bodied frame. The main look-alike is the Pembroke Welsh Corgi, which usually has no visible tail or a very short docked tail and often a lighter, more compact look. Do not rely on coat color alone, since Cardigans occur in many colors, including merle, that Pembrokes usually do not.

name: toy poodle
Canis lupus familiaris
265.description: A very small poodle with a compact, delicate build, long dropped ears, and a dense curly or fluffy coat. The coat is often solid white, cream, apricot, brown, gray, or black, and the face has a narrow muzzle with dark round eyes.
265.guidelines: Classify as toy poodle when the dog is clearly poodle-like and tiny, with a fine-boned body and tightly curled or groomed fluffy coat. Distinguish it from miniature or standard poodles by its much smaller size, from bichon frisés by the longer muzzle and more poodle-shaped outline, and from Maltese or other toy breeds by the characteristic curly poodle coat rather than straight or silky hair.

name: Miniature Poodle
Canis lupus familiaris
266.description: A small, lightly built poodle with a refined outline, long narrow muzzle, dark oval eyes, and drop ears. The coat is dense and curly or fluffy, often clipped, and commonly appears in white, black, apricot, cream, brown, or parti-color.
266.guidelines: Classify as Miniature Poodle when the dog is clearly a small poodle-type with a fine-boned body, narrow muzzle, and characteristically curly coat. Include both pet trims and fuller puppy coats. Do not confuse with Toy Poodle, which is usually even smaller and more delicate, or Standard Poodle, which is much larger and longer-legged. Distinguish from Bichon Frise and Maltese by the poodle’s longer muzzle, less round head, and tighter curl pattern; distinguish from doodle mixes by the more refined poodle build and more consistently poodle-like face and coat.

name: Standard poodle
Canis lupus familiaris
267.description: A large poodle with a tall, elegant build, long straight muzzle, and a dense curly or corded coat. The coat is often clipped in characteristic poodle trims and appears in solid colors such as white, black, brown, gray, or apricot.
267.guidelines: Classify as standard poodle when the dog shows the large poodle form: long legs, refined proportions, narrow muzzle, and a dense curly coat. Distinguish it from miniature and toy poodles mainly by larger size and taller build. Avoid confusing it with bichon frise or other small white curly dogs, which are much smaller and rounder-faced, and with doodle-type mixes, which usually have a less refined head shape and a looser, less uniform coat.

name: Xoloitzcuintli
Canis lupus familiaris
268.description: A nearly hairless dog breed with smooth bare skin, usually dark gray, black, slate, or brown, sometimes with small white markings and a short tuft of hair on the head, tail, or feet. It has a lean elegant build, long legs, a narrow muzzle, and very large upright ears.
268.guidelines: Classify as Xoloitzcuintli when the dog is mostly hairless and has the characteristic slim body, wedge-shaped head, and oversized erect ears. Do not confuse it with the Chinese Crested, which is usually smaller and has obvious long silky hair on the head, tail, and feet, or with other small hairless dogs that have shorter legs or a less refined outline. The key cues are the almost entirely bare skin, elegant sighthound-like proportions, and large bat-like ears.

name: gray wolf
Canis lupus
269.description: A large wild canid with a long-legged, athletic build, broad muzzle, erect triangular ears, and a thick bushy tail usually carried low. The coat is dense and variable but most often gray mixed with black, brown, buff, or white, often with paler cheeks, throat, and underparts and a darker back or saddle.
269.guidelines: Classify as gray wolf when the animal has the robust build, broad head, relatively large paws, and full mottled gray-brown coat typical of wild wolves. Do not confuse with domestic dogs such as huskies or German shepherds, which often have more breed-specific markings, different tail carriage, or a less uniformly wild canid build. Distinguish from coyotes by the wolf’s larger size, broader muzzle, heavier neck and chest, shorter-looking ears relative to the head, and thicker fur; coyotes are slimmer, narrower-faced, and leggier-looking.

name: Arctic wolf
Canis lupus arctos
270.description: A large wolf with a thick, fluffy coat that is predominantly white to creamy white, sometimes with faint pale gray or buff shading. It has a broad head, pointed upright ears, a long muzzle, long legs, and a bushy tail; the dense fur gives the body and neck a fuller, more rounded appearance than many gray wolves.
270.guidelines: Classify as Arctic wolf when the animal is clearly a wolf with an almost entirely white coat and heavy northern-type fur. Do not confuse it with gray wolf varieties that are tan, brown, or strongly gray, or with domestic dogs such as Samoyeds or white huskies, which usually have shorter muzzles, different body proportions, curlier tails, or a more pet-dog appearance. Also distinguish it from foxes by the wolf’s much larger size, broader muzzle, and less delicate build.

name: maned wolf
Chrysocyon brachyurus
271.description: A tall, long-legged canid with a shaggy reddish-orange coat, very large upright ears, a dark muzzle, black lower legs, and often a black mane along the neck and shoulders. The body is slim and foxlike, with a pale throat and a bushy tail that may show a lighter tip.
271.guidelines: Classify as maned wolf when the animal has strikingly long black legs, a lean high-shouldered build, oversized ears, and a reddish coat. Do not confuse it with the red wolf or gray wolf, which are heavier-bodied and proportionally shorter-legged, or with foxes and coyotes, which are smaller and lack the maned wolf’s stilt-like legs and distinctive black stockings.

name: coyote
Canis latrans
272.description: A medium-sized wild canid with a lean build, narrow muzzle, large pointed ears, long legs, and a bushy tail usually carried low. The coat is typically grayish tan to buff or reddish gray, often with black-tipped guard hairs, paler underparts, and a somewhat scruffy appearance.
272.guidelines: Classify as coyote when the animal is a slim, foxlike canid with a long narrow snout, upright ears, and a low-carried bushy tail. Distinguish it from wolves by its smaller size, lighter build, narrower face, and proportionally larger ears; from red foxes by its larger size, longer legs, less fluffy coat, and lack of a white tail tip; and from domestic dogs by its more consistent wild canid proportions, especially the narrow chest, pointed muzzle, and straight, low tail carriage.

name: dhole
Cuon alpinus
274.description: A medium-sized wild dog with a compact, foxlike build, a rusty red to reddish-brown coat, paler white or cream fur on the throat, chest, and underside, relatively short muzzle, and broad rounded ears. The tail is bushy and usually darker toward the tip, often blackish. Compared with similar canids, it looks stockier and more thick-furred.
274.guidelines: Classify as dhole when the animal shows the characteristic reddish coat, rounded ears, compact body, and bushy dark-tipped tail. Do not confuse it with the red fox, which has a narrower muzzle, more pointed ears, and a longer, lower-slung body; or with wolves, coyotes, and jackals, which are generally grayer or sandier, longer-legged, and have sharper, more triangular heads. Dholes also tend to have a more uniform red coat and less contrasting facial markings than foxes.

name: African wild dog
Lycaon pictus
275.description: A lean, long-legged wild canid with very large rounded ears, a narrow dark muzzle, and an irregular mottled coat of black, tan, white, and brown. The body is lightly built with a sloping back, long legs, and a bushy tail often tipped in white.
275.guidelines: Classify as African wild dog when the animal shows the distinctive patchy multicolored coat and oversized rounded ears. Do not confuse it with hyenas, which have shorter rounded ears, heavier front quarters, and lack the crisp black-tan-white patchwork; or with wolves, jackals, and domestic dogs, which usually have more uniform coats and more pointed ears. The combination of very large ears, slender build, and blotchy painted coat is the key cue.

name: hyena
Hyaenidae
276.description: A dog-like carnivore with a heavy forequarters, sloping back, large rounded ears, a broad muzzle, and a coarse coat that is usually spotted or striped depending on the species. Colors range from sandy or grayish to brown, often with darker markings and a shorter mane along the neck and back.
276.guidelines: Classify as hyena when the animal has the characteristic hyena build: powerful front end, lower hindquarters, big rounded ears, and a coarse spotted or striped coat. Do not confuse it with African wild dogs, which are leggier with larger pointed ears and patchy multicolor coats, or with wolves and other dogs, which have a more level back and narrower head. Spotted hyenas are stockier with dark spots; striped hyenas have vertical body stripes and a shaggier mane, but both belong in this category.

name: red fox
Vulpes vulpes
277.description: A medium-sized fox with a slender body, long bushy tail, pointed muzzle, and large upright ears. Typical coat is reddish orange to rusty red, often with a white throat, chest, or tail tip and darker blackish legs or ear backs. Some individuals appear paler, browner, or more grayish, but the overall shape remains lean and sharp-faced.
277.guidelines: Classify as red fox when the animal shows the classic fox form: narrow pointed face, large triangular ears, slim legs, and a long very bushy tail, usually with reddish coat and often dark legs.
