Use the overall lanky proportions and small narrow face as the key cues.

name: mantled guereza
Colobus guereza
375.description: A black-and-white colobus monkey with a black face framed by white cheek and brow hair, a glossy black body, long silky white mantle hair along the sides, and a long tail ending in a large white tuft. The body is slender, with long limbs and a small head topped by a dark cap.
375.guidelines: Classify as mantled guereza when the monkey is distinctly black and white, especially with a white facial fringe, long white side mantle, and a long tail with a prominent white plume. Do not confuse it with other colobus monkeys such as the Angolan colobus, which often has heavier white facial and shoulder markings, or with langurs and guenons, which may be black-and-white but lack the flowing white mantle and large white tail tuft typical of guerezas.

name: proboscis monkey
Nasalis larvatus
376.description: A large, long-limbed monkey with a pot-bellied body, reddish-brown upperparts, pale underparts, grayish limbs, and an exceptionally large, fleshy, downward-hanging nose, especially in adult males. It has a long tail and often shows a pale face with a chestnut crown.
376.guidelines: Classify as proboscis monkey when the monkey has the distinctive oversized pendulous nose, pot belly, reddish back, pale belly, and gray limbs. Do not confuse it with macaques, langurs, or snub-nosed monkeys: macaques usually have shorter muzzles and no large hanging nose; langurs are typically slimmer with smaller noses and different coat patterns; snub-nosed monkeys have short upturned noses rather than a long drooping one. Females and juveniles may have smaller noses, but still show the same general reddish-and-pale coloration and long-tailed, pot-bellied build.

name: callitrichid
Callitrichidae
377.description: Very small New World monkey with a compact body, short muzzle, large forward-facing eyes, and a long tail. Coat color varies widely across species—gray, brown, black, white, or golden—and many have distinctive ear tufts, a fluffy mane, or a contrasting face.
377.guidelines: Classify as callitrichid when the animal is a tiny monkey with a small rounded face, very large eyes, and often ear tufts or a lion-like mane; this includes both marmosets and tamarins. Do not confuse with squirrel monkeys or capuchins, which are larger and longer-limbed with less tufted faces, or with tarsiers, galagos, and lemurs, which have much larger eyes relative to the head and a more non-monkey facial shape.

name: white-headed capuchin
Cebus capucinus
378.description: A small to medium capuchin monkey with a creamy white to pale yellow face, throat, chest, and shoulders, contrasting with a darker black or dark brown crown, back, arms, legs, and long tail. The face is bare and pinkish to gray, and the body is slender with a strongly curved tail often carried in a loop.
378.guidelines: Classify this as a white-headed capuchin when the monkey shows the characteristic pale head and front with a sharply contrasting dark cap and dark limbs. Do not confuse it with black capuchins or tufted capuchins, which are darker overall and lack the strongly white face and chest, or with squirrel monkeys, which are smaller, more delicate, and have a different facial mask. The key cue is the bold black-and-white capuchin pattern: pale head/chest plus dark body and tail.

name: mantled howler
Alouatta palliata
379.description: A large, long-limbed howler monkey with shaggy fur, a heavy body, and a broad jaw and throat. Most individuals are mostly black, often with brownish or golden fur along the sides or back, and they have a long prehensile tail, a dark face, and a bearded look.
379.guidelines: Classify as mantled howler when the monkey is robust, shaggy, and mostly black with possible golden-brown side fur, plus a broad muzzle and long grasping tail. Do not confuse it with spider monkeys, which are slimmer with smaller heads and much longer, more delicate limbs, or with capuchins and other monkeys that are smaller, less shaggy, and lack the howler’s heavy jaw and throat.

name: titi monkey
Callicebinae
380.description: Small arboreal monkey with a compact body, a rounded teddy-bear-like face, short muzzle, and dense fluffy fur. Most examples show reddish-brown, chestnut, or gray-brown coats, a darker face, and a long bushy tail that is not prehensile.
380.guidelines: Classify as a titi monkey when the animal is a small, fluffy New World monkey with a round face and very long bushy tail, usually seen sitting or moving in trees. Do not confuse it with squirrel monkeys or capuchins, which have less fluffy coats and more slender, alert faces, or with tamarins and marmosets, which are smaller and often have ear tufts or sharply patterned faces. Also distinguish it from woolly monkeys and howler monkeys, which are much larger and heavier-bodied.

name: spider monkey
Ateles
381.description: A very slender, long-limbed New World monkey with a small head, lean body, and an extremely long, flexible prehensile tail that is often held curled or used like a fifth limb. The arms and legs are notably elongated, and the fur is usually dark brown, black, golden, or reddish, sometimes with a paler face or underside. It is commonly seen hanging, climbing, or moving through trees with its tail supporting much of its weight.
381.guidelines: Classify as spider monkey when the monkey has a distinctly lightweight build, very long limbs, and an exceptionally long grasping tail used for suspending or balancing in the canopy. Do not confuse with howler monkeys, which are heavier-bodied with shorter-looking limbs and a bulkier head; woolly monkeys, which are stockier and fluffier; or capuchins and other smaller monkeys, which have shorter limbs and less dramatically elongated tails. The overall silhouette of a spider monkey is especially lanky and arboreal.

name: common squirrel monkey
Saimiri sciureus
382.description: A small, slender arboreal monkey with a gray-olive back, bright yellow to orange forearms and lower legs, a long tail, and a distinct white facial mask around the eyes and muzzle. The crown is darker, and the eyes appear large and dark in the pale face.
382.guidelines: Classify as common squirrel monkey when the animal is a small monkey with yellow limbs, a white mask-like face, and a dark cap. Distinguish it from capuchin monkeys, which are bulkier with shorter-looking faces and lack the crisp white mask, and from tamarins or marmosets, which are much smaller and often have ear tufts or longer facial hair. Do not rely on pose or habitat alone; the key cues are the white facial mask, dark crown, slender build, and yellow-orange limbs.

name: ring-tailed lemur
Lemur catta
383.description: A slender gray lemur with a pointed muzzle, white face, dark triangular eye patches, large amber to yellow eyes, and a very long tail marked with bold black-and-white rings.
383.guidelines: Classify as ring-tailed lemur when the animal shows the distinctive striped tail plus the white face with dark eye patches and gray body. Do not confuse with other lemurs such as ruffed lemurs or sifakas, which lack the sharply ringed tail, or with raccoons and coatis, which may have ringed tails but have different body shape, fur texture, and face pattern.

name: indri
Indri indri
384.description: A large black-and-white lemur with a round, furry face, bright yellow to orange-yellow eyes, small rounded ears, and dense plush fur. The body is stout and upright-clinging, with long hind limbs, a mostly black face, and strongly contrasting black-and-white coat patches; unlike most lemurs, the tail is extremely short and often barely visible.
384.guidelines: Classify this as an indri when the animal is a large arboreal lemur with a teddy-bear-like face, bright eyes, thick black-and-white fur, and especially a very short tail. Do not confuse it with sifakas, which are similarly black and white but usually have a long, obvious tail and a slimmer look. It also differs from ruffed lemurs, which have a longer muzzle, bushier long tail, and more fox-like proportions.

name: Indian elephant
Elephas maximus indicus
385.description: A large gray elephant with a domed head, relatively small fan-shaped ears, a long muscular trunk, thick wrinkled skin, and a broad heavy body. The back is gently arched or level rather than strongly sloped, and tusks may be short or absent, especially in females.
385.guidelines: Classify as Indian elephant when the animal is an Asian elephant with noticeably smaller ears than African elephants and a more rounded head profile. Do not confuse with African bush elephant or African forest elephant, which have much larger ears; the bush elephant is larger with broader ears and a more concave back, while the forest elephant is smaller and differently proportioned. If the image only shows a generic elephant but the small ears and Asian-elephant head shape are clear, it fits this category.

name: African bush elephant
Loxodonta africana
386.description: A very large gray elephant with extremely large, fan-shaped ears, a long muscular trunk, wrinkled skin, pillar-like legs, and often prominent curved ivory tusks. The back is generally slightly concave, and both males and many females may have tusks.
386.guidelines: Classify as African bush elephant when the animal has very large ears that extend well below and behind the head, giving a broad triangular or fan-like outline. Distinguish it from the Asian elephant, which has much smaller rounded ears, a more domed head, and smoother-looking proportions. Also avoid confusing it with the African forest elephant, which is typically smaller, darker, and more compact with rounder ears and straighter, thinner tusks.

name: northern pike
Esox lucius
389.description: A long, torpedo-shaped freshwater fish with a broad duck-bill snout, large mouth, and body patterned with pale oval spots or bars on an olive to gray-green background. The fins, especially the tail and lower rear fins, are rounded and often yellowish to orange-red, sometimes with darker markings.
389.guidelines: Classify as northern pike when the fish has the classic Esox shape: elongated body, very long flattened snout, dorsal and anal fins set far back near the tail, and a pale-spotted body. Do not confuse with barracuda or snoek, which are marine fish that are more silvery and lack the olive spotted pike pattern. Also distinguish from muskellunge, which usually has a slimmer body and darker markings on a lighter background rather than pale spots on a darker body, and from walleye/zander, which are deeper-bodied and perch-like rather than duck-billed.

name: moray eel
Muraenidae
390.description: A long, snake-like eel with a thick, muscular body, smooth leathery scaleless skin, and a continuous fleshy dorsal fin that starts just behind the head and runs along the back. The head is blunt to pointed with a large mouth, strong jaws, and distinctive tubular nostrils on the snout. Coloration varies widely—yellow, green, brown, gray, black, white, or boldly mottled and spotted—but many show high-contrast patterns. Moray eels are often seen with only the head protruding from a crevice, burrow, pipe, or coral hole.
390.guidelines: Classify as a moray eel when the eel has a stout body, obvious tube-like nostrils, a high continuous fin fold beginning near the head, and the typical thick-skinned reef- or burrow-dwelling appearance. Do not confuse with true freshwater eels or conger eels, which are usually smoother-headed, less heavy-bodied, and lack the prominent tubular nostrils; snake eels, which often have more pointed tails and different head shape; or garden eels, which are much thinner and usually stand upright from sandy burrows. The visible tubular nostrils and robust moray head are the best cues.

name: coho salmon
Oncorhynchus kisutch
391.description: A medium to large salmon with a streamlined silver body, darker blue-green to gray back, and small black spots mainly on the back and upper lobe of the tail. Adults at sea are bright and silvery; spawning adults often turn maroon to reddish with a darker gray head and develop a hooked upper jaw. The eye sits roughly centered between the snout tip and gill cover. Juveniles are slimmer, with relatively large eyes, distinct vertical oval parr marks, and noticeable white leading edges on the fins, especially the anal fin.
391.guidelines: Classify as coho salmon when the fish has a bright silver body with spotting concentrated on the upper back and tail, or when spawning adults show the typical maroon body and dark head. Juveniles should show oval parr marks and white fin edges. Distinguish from chinook salmon by the coho's whiter gums and less extensive spotting on the tail, from sockeye salmon by the presence of spots and the darker head rather than a bright red body with green head, and from Atlantic salmon by the heavier spotting pattern on the upper body and the overall Pacific salmon shape and coloration.

name: rock beauty
Holacanthus tricolor
392.description: A deep-bodied marine angelfish with a bright yellow head, chest, and rear margins, and a large black patch covering most of the midbody, creating a bold black-and-yellow pattern. The body is tall and laterally compressed, often appearing somewhat rectangular or arrowhead-shaped. The dorsal and anal fins are long and taper to pointed rear tips, the tail is yellow, the lips are thick and dark, and a sharp backward-pointing spine is visible at the gill cover. The eye may show a faint bluish ring. Juveniles are mostly yellow with a distinct black spot or saddle on the side.
392.guidelines: Classify as rock beauty when the fish is a yellow-and-black angelfish with a yellow head and tail but a single large black midbody patch, plus the typical angelfish shape with pointed dorsal and anal fin ends. Distinguish it from French angelfish and gray angelfish, which are darker overall with many pale scale markings rather than one solid black field. Distinguish it from bicolor angelfish and related dwarf angelfish, which are smaller, rounder, and lack the pronounced Holacanthus body shape and gill-cover spine. Ignore lighting shifts that make the black area look brownish or bluish; the key cue is the strong yellow front and rear framing one large dark central patch.

name: anemonefish
Amphiprioninae
393.description: Small, laterally compressed reef fish usually seen living among sea anemone tentacles. Body colors are bold and high-contrast—often orange, red, yellow, black, or brown—with rounded fins, a blunt snout, and one or more broad white markings, commonly vertical head/body bars edged in black or a pale stripe along the back. Many images show the fish partly sheltered within an anemone.
393.guidelines: Classify as anemonefish when the fish has the typical clownfish shape, bold contrasting white bars or patches, and is closely associated with a sea anemone. Do not restrict the class to the familiar orange three-banded clownfish: black, yellow, red, and single-stripe forms also belong here. Distinguish from damselfish and other reef fish by the thicker white bars, rounder body, blunt face, and frequent anemone habitat. Distinguish from butterflyfish and angelfish by the lack of a strongly elongated, disk-like body and by the characteristic clownfish-style bars rather than thin lines or eye stripes.

name: white sturgeon
Acipenser transmontanus
394.description: A very large, elongated fish with a long pointed snout, four barbels hanging beneath the snout, and a small underside mouth. The body is armored with five rows of prominent bony scutes rather than regular scales, including a raised ridge along the back. It has broad, horizontally held pectoral fins and a strongly asymmetrical, shark-like tail with a longer upper lobe. Color is usually gray to brown or olive above and paler below.
394.guidelines: Classify as white sturgeon when the fish has the classic sturgeon body plan: long snout, barbels under the snout, rows of bony scutes, large paddle-like pectoral fins, and a heterocercal tail. Do not confuse it with sharks, which lack barbels and scute rows, or catfish, which have whiskers around the mouth but no armored scutes or shark-like tail. Compared with paddlefish, white sturgeon have a pointed snout rather than a broad paddle-shaped one. Use the heavy armored body and five scute rows to distinguish it from salmon or other large freshwater fish.

name: gar
Lepisosteidae
395.description: Large, elongated freshwater fish with a cylindrical body, a long narrow snout to broad alligator-like snout depending on species, and a covering of hard, diamond-shaped interlocking ganoid scales that give an armored look. Color is usually olive, brown, or gray above with a paler underside; some species show dark spots on the body and fins.
395.guidelines: Classify as gar when the fish has a very long torpedo-shaped body, a beaklike snout, and especially thick rhomboid armor-like scales. This category includes long-snouted forms such as longnose gar, medium-snouted spotted gar, and broad-snouted alligator gar. Avoid confusing it with needlefish or halfbeaks, which are much slimmer and lack heavy diamond armor; sturgeon, which have rows of scutes rather than full-body rhomboid scales; and pike or barracuda, which have ordinary scales and a less armored appearance.

name: lionfish
Pterois
396.description: A striking reef fish with bold zebra-like vertical stripes, a laterally compressed body, very long venomous dorsal spines, broad fanlike pectoral fins, and small fleshy tentacles above the eyes. Coloration is usually red, reddish-brown, cream, or white, often with banded fins and spotted fin membranes.
396.guidelines: Classify as lionfish when the fish shows both strong contrasting stripes and dramatic radiating spines with large winglike pectoral fins. Do not confuse it with scorpionfish or stonefish, which are stockier, rougher, and lack the long showy fin rays; or with turkeyfish/firefish labels, which are often common names for the same Pterois group. The combination of zebra striping, eye tassels, and long separated fin spines is the key cue.

name: blowfish
397.description: A small to medium fish with a short, rounded body, blunt face, large prominent eyes, and a small beak-like mouth. Members of this class can inflate their bodies into a ball. Appearance ranges from smooth or finely granular-skinned pufferfish to porcupinefish with conspicuous long spines even when not inflated. Coloration is highly variable, often mottled, spotted, reticulated, or pale with dark dots.
397.guidelines: Classify both true pufferfish (family Tetraodontidae) and porcupinefish (family Diodontidae) here. Key cues are the rounded body, large eyes, small fins, beak-like mouth, and the ability to inflate. Porcupinefish are distinguished within this class by obvious external spines and especially large eyes; smoother fish with tiny skin prickles are typical pufferfish. Do not confuse with boxfish or cowfish, which have a rigid boxy body and cannot balloon into a sphere, or with spiny burrfish-like reef fish that lack the characteristic puffer shape and facial structure.

name: abacus
398.description: A counting frame used for arithmetic, consisting of a rectangular frame with parallel rods or wires holding rows of sliding beads. It may be oriented horizontally or vertically, and the beads are often wood or plastic in natural, dark, or brightly colored finishes.
398.guidelines: Classify as an abacus when the object is a bead-based counting frame with multiple parallel rods or wires inside a frame. Include traditional wooden suanpan-style abaci and toy or educational versions. Do not confuse with bead mazes or bead-coaster toys, which have curved looping wires rather than straight parallel counting rows, or with decorative bead panels that are not arranged as a calculation device.

name: abaya
399.description: A loose, full-length outer garment worn over clothing, usually dark-colored—especially black—and cut in a simple robe-like or cloak-like shape that falls from the shoulders to the ankles or feet. It typically has long sleeves or wide draped openings and a modest, flowing silhouette, though some examples include embroidery, trim, pleated cuffs, colored piping, or decorative panels. It may be worn with a headscarf or face veil, but the defining item is the long overgarment itself.
399.guidelines: Classify as abaya when the main object is a long, loose, modest overgarment covering most of the body in a robe-like form. Do not require face covering: many abayas are worn with only a hijab, while others are paired with a niqab. Distinguish from a jilbab, which is often used more broadly for various loose Islamic outer garments; use abaya when the garment has the characteristic robe/cloak look common in Gulf-style dress. Distinguish from hijab, which is only the headscarf; niqab, which is only the face veil; chador, which is usually an open semicircular wrap held closed rather than a sleeved robe; and burqa, which fully covers the face with a mesh eye screen. Focus on the full-length flowing outer robe, not the head covering alone.

name: academic dress
400.description: Formal academic attire worn at universities, typically consisting of a long loose black or dark gown or robe, often with colored trim, velvet panels, sleeve bars, or a separate hood draped over the shoulders. It is frequently paired with a mortarboard or soft academic cap and may vary by degree, field, or institution.
400.guidelines: Classify images here when the defining item is university ceremonial clothing: a gown or robe used for graduation, commencement, or faculty academic ceremony, often with a hood and academic cap. Do not confuse it with a judge's robe, which is usually a plain judicial robe without academic hoods or degree-color trim, or with choir robes and clerical vestments, which are religious garments rather than university regalia. Graduation caps alone are not enough unless the academic gown or robe is clearly present.

name: accordion
401.description: A portable free-reed musical instrument with a bellows body held between both hands. It has pleated expanding bellows in the center and keyboards or rows of buttons on the two ends; one side often has piano-style keys while the other has bass or melody buttons. Commonly rectangular or slightly rounded, with metal, wood, or plastic panels and shoulder straps.
401.guidelines: Classify as accordion when the instrument has a hand-played bellows connecting two rigid ends, with piano keys or dense button arrays. Include both piano accordions and button accordions. Do not confuse with a concertina or bandoneon, which are smaller, usually hexagonal or boxy, and lack a long piano keyboard; or with a harmonium or organ, which are not handheld and do not have this squeeze-bellows form.

name: acoustic guitar
402.description: A hollow-bodied guitar with a waisted wooden body, round sound hole, flat top, long fretted neck, and a headstock with enclosed tuning machines. In the typical steel-string form shown here, the strings are metal and are anchored at the bridge with visible bridge pins.
402.guidelines: Classify as acoustic guitar when the instrument is a non-electric guitar with a resonant hollow body and visible sound hole, usually with steel strings, bridge pins, and closed tuning pegs. Do not confuse it with a classical guitar, which usually has nylon strings, a slotted headstock, and no bridge pins; or with electric and semi-acoustic guitars, which have pickups/electronics and are not defined mainly by an acoustic sound box. Ignore playing context, partial views, and decorative finishes as long as the guitar’s hollow acoustic body and steel-string hardware are visible.

name: aircraft carrier
403.description: A very large naval warship built as a floating airbase, with a long, flat full-length flight deck for launching and recovering aircraft. It typically has a tall island superstructure offset to one side, a broad rectangular hull, and an open deck lined with parked jets, helicopters, deck markings, and aircraft-handling equipment.
403.guidelines: Classify as an aircraft carrier when the ship’s dominant feature is a full-length flat flight deck used for aircraft operations. Distinguish it from amphibious assault ships or helicopter carriers by the carrier-style long unobstructed deck and naval air wing presence, often with fixed-wing jets. Do not confuse it with other warships such as destroyers, cruisers, or battleships, which have narrower decks, prominent guns or missile systems, and no continuous runway-like flight deck.

name: airliner
404.description: A large fixed-wing commercial airplane built to carry passengers and often cargo. It typically has a long cylindrical fuselage, swept wings, jet engines mounted under the wings or at the rear, a conventional tail, and airline livery; sizes range from regional jets to wide-body airliners.
404.guidelines: Classify as an airliner when the image shows a civilian commercial transport aircraft, whether in flight, landing, taxiing, parked, or seen partly from a window or close-up. Include both passenger and cargo airline-operated jets. Do not confuse with military aircraft, which often have tactical paint, visible weapons, refueling gear, or non-civil fuselage shapes; with private/business jets, which are much smaller and lack airliner proportions; or with small general-aviation planes and turboprops, which are usually smaller and less streamlined.

name: airship
405.description: A large lighter-than-air aircraft with an elongated cigar- or blimp-shaped gas envelope, usually flying high in the sky. It may have small tail fins, engine gondolas, and sometimes a passenger or advertising cabin suspended beneath the envelope.
405.guidelines: Classify as an airship when the object is a powered lighter-than-air craft with a long streamlined envelope and fins. Include both blimps and rigid or semi-rigid dirigibles. Do not confuse with a hot-air balloon, which has a rounded balloon shape with a hanging basket and no fins, or with an airplane/helicopter, which rely on wings or rotors rather than buoyant lift.

name: altar
406.description: A raised table, platform, or shrine-like structure used for worship and ritual, typically placed at the focal end of a sacred space. It is often symmetrical and decorated with cloths, candles, flowers, icons, statues, crosses, offerings, or other ceremonial objects, and may range from a simple table to an ornate built-in structure. Altars occur in Christian churches as well as other religious settings such as temples and household shrines.
406.guidelines: Classify as altar when the image centers on the sacred ritual focal structure itself—the table, platform, or shrine where offerings or rites are performed. Include both simple church communion tables and elaborate temple shrines. Do not confuse with a pulpit/lectern, which is a stand for reading or preaching; a pew, which is seating; an iconostasis or reredos, which is the decorative screen or backdrop behind the altar; or a general sanctuary interior where the altar is small or incidental. The key cue is a dedicated ritual surface or shrine, usually front-facing and centrally arranged for worship.

name: ambulance
407.description: A road vehicle specially outfitted for medical transport and emergency response, usually a van, truck, or large car with high-visibility markings, emergency lights, and often medical symbols such as a red cross or Star of Life.
407.guidelines: Classify as ambulance only when the vehicle is clearly equipped and marked for transporting sick or injured people. Typical cues are emergency light bars, medical insignia, high-visibility striping, and a van- or box-bodied patient compartment. Do not confuse with fire engines, police cars, rescue vans, hearses, or ordinary vans: ambulances are specifically marked and configured for medical care and patient transport.

name: amphibious vehicle
408.description: A vehicle designed to travel on both land and water, typically with a boat-like or sealed hull combined with wheels or tracks. It often has a blunt, boxy, or wedge-shaped body, raised sides, and propulsion or flotation features for water use, while still retaining normal road or off-road driving components.
408.guidelines: Classify as an amphibious vehicle when the vehicle is clearly built to operate in both water and on land. Look for a drivable wheeled or tracked chassis integrated with a hull-shaped body. Do not confuse with ordinary boats on trailers, hovercraft, or seaplanes: boats usually lack usable road wheels for self-driving on land, hovercraft ride on an air cushion rather than a hull in the water, and seaplanes are aircraft with wings. Also exclude standard trucks or armored vehicles unless they are visibly amphibious in design.

name: analog clock
409.description: A timekeeping device with a visible clock face and moving hands that indicate the time, typically including at least an hour hand and usually minute and sometimes second hands. The face is commonly circular but may be square or decorative, with numerals, tick marks, or Roman numerals around the dial.
409.guidelines: Classify as analog clock when the image shows a clock face with hands displaying time. Include wall clocks, desk clocks, alarm clocks, tower clocks, and decorative analog clocks. Do not confuse with digital clocks, which show time as numerals without hands; watches, which are wearable wrist or pocket timepieces; stopwatches or timers, which are specialized timing devices; or sundials, whose shadow-casting gnomon replaces mechanical hands.

name: beehive
410.description: A beehive is a boxlike structure used to house honey bees, typically seen as stacked wooden hive boxes with removable frames. It often appears outdoors in groups in an apiary, and may be shown open with bees covering the frames or comb inside.
410.guidelines: Classify as beehive when the image centers on the hive structure itself: stacked wooden boxes, lids, entrances, or exposed frames/comb used for managed bees. Include open hives being inspected by beekeepers. Do not confuse with honeycomb alone, which shows wax comb without the full hive box, or with an apiary scene where the emphasis is the whole field or site rather than a specific hive. Also exclude natural nests in trees or under roofs unless the managed hive box is the main subject.

name: apron
411.description: A sleeveless protective garment worn over the front of the body, typically tied at the waist or neck. It is usually made of cloth or plastic and may be full-length, waist-length, or bib-style, often with pockets, ruffles, or decorative prints.
411.guidelines: Classify as apron when the item is specifically designed to cover the front of clothing during cooking, cleaning, crafts, or similar work. Common forms include bib aprons with a neck loop and waist ties, and half aprons tied around the waist. Do not confuse with dresses, pinafores, or skirts: aprons are worn over other clothing and are open or tied at the back rather than fully constructed garments. Also distinguish from smocks or uniforms, which usually have sleeves or fuller body coverage.

name: trash can
412.description: A container for collecting waste, typically an open-top or lidded bin made of plastic or metal. It may be cylindrical, rectangular, or tapered, and can appear indoors or outdoors as a small household wastebasket, a wheeled curbside bin, or a public rubbish receptacle.
412.guidelines: Classify as trash can when the main object is a bin or receptacle specifically used for holding trash or refuse. Include household garbage cans, office wastebaskets, street litter bins, and similar public or private waste containers. Do not confuse with dumpsters (much larger bulk waste containers), recycling bins when clearly designated only for recyclables, storage tubs or buckets not used as waste receptacles, or ashtrays/cigarette bins that are primarily for cigarette disposal.

name: assault rifle
413.description: A shoulder-fired military-style rifle of medium length with a long barrel, prominent receiver, detachable box magazine, and a full stock, folding stock, or pistol grip. It is designed for rapid semiautomatic or automatic fire and often has accessory rails, sights, flash suppressors, or foregrips.
413.guidelines: Classify as assault rifle when the image shows a rifle-sized firearm built for shoulder firing and rapid fire, typically with a detachable magazine and military configuration. Do not confuse with submachine guns, which are usually shorter and more compact and fire pistol ammunition; battle rifles, which are often larger and heavier with full-power rifle proportions; or light machine guns, which are bulkier and often belt-fed or have heavier barrels and bipods. Exclude generic civilian sporting rifles or shotguns unless the weapon clearly matches the military assault-rifle form.

name: backpack
414.description: A soft portable bag carried on the back, typically with two shoulder straps and a zippered main compartment. It may be small or large, structured or soft-sided, and often includes front or side pockets, handles, buckles, or compression straps.
414.guidelines: Classify as backpack when the bag is designed to be worn on the back with shoulder straps. Include school backpacks, hiking daypacks, hydration packs, and rucksacks. Exclude other bags such as messenger bags, duffel bags, suitcases, tote bags, and sling bags worn over one shoulder. To distinguish from luggage or handbags, look for a back-worn form factor and visible shoulder straps rather than wheels, rigid suitcase shells, or hand-carry handles as the primary feature.

name: bakery
415.description: A bakery is a shop or display associated with baked goods such as bread, rolls, cakes, cupcakes, cookies, pastries, and similar sweet or savory items. Images may show the storefront or sign of the shop, interior bread or pastry displays, or baked goods presented as typical bakery products.
415.guidelines: Classify as bakery when the image shows a bakery shop, bakery signage, a bakery display case, or baked goods presented in a general bakery context. Do not confuse with a restaurant, which emphasizes prepared meals and dining service rather than baked goods. Also avoid labeling single specific products as bakery when a narrower class is more appropriate, such as cake, cupcake, bread loaf, donut, or pastry, unless the image clearly represents the broader bakery/shop context.

name: balance beam
416.description: A balance beam is a long, very narrow, padded horizontal bar raised above the floor on supports, used in artistic gymnastics. It appears as a slim beam just wide enough for a gymnast’s foot, typically tan or light colored, with a suede-like surface and metal legs or bases.
416.guidelines: Classify this as a balance beam when the image centers on the narrow elevated gymnastics apparatus itself or a gymnast performing on it. Do not confuse it with the pommel horse or vaulting horse, which are wider padded bodies rather than a thin beam; the uneven bars or horizontal bar, which are metal bars; or a generic bench or rail, which lacks the standard gymnastics apparatus design.

name: hot air balloon
417.description: A large lighter-than-air aircraft with a bulbous fabric envelope and a small basket or gondola suspended beneath it. In these images it is specifically a hot air balloon: the envelope is inflated by heated air, usually rounded or teardrop-shaped, often brightly colored or patterned, and sometimes made in special character shapes.
417.guidelines: Classify as hot air balloon when the image shows a full-size crewed balloon aircraft with a large fabric envelope and a basket underneath, typically flying in the sky or being inflated on the ground. Do not confuse it with party balloons or toy balloons, which are small, handheld, and lack a basket; blimps or dirigibles, which are elongated airships with fins or engines; or parachutes/paragliders, which have open canopies rather than a sealed balloon envelope.

name: ballpoint pen
418.description: A pen with a small rolling metal ball at the tip that dispenses ink. It typically has a slim cylindrical plastic or metal barrel, a pointed conical tip, and may be capped, retractable, transparent, or decorated, but the defining feature is the ball-bearing writing tip used with paste-like ink.
418.guidelines: Classify as ballpoint pen when the object is clearly a pen with a ball-tip writing point, including capped novelty and retractable forms. Do not confuse with gel pens or rollerball pens, which often look similar but usually have a wetter ink flow and different tip construction; with felt-tip or marker pens, which have a fiber tip rather than a metal ball; or with mechanical pencils, which show exposed graphite lead instead of a ballpoint tip.

name: adhesive bandage
419.description: A small ready-made wound dressing consisting of a narrow strip of adhesive material, usually fabric or plastic, with a padded absorbent center placed over a minor cut, blister, or puncture. It is typically flesh-colored, white, clear, or brightly colored and is commonly applied to fingers, toes, arms, legs, or the face.
419.guidelines: Classify images as adhesive bandage when they show a single self-adhesive strip bandage or several such bandages, either on skin or off the body. The key cues are the adhesive tabs and the distinct central pad or protected dressing area. Do not confuse it with medical tape, which is a plain strip without a central pad; gauze pads or larger dressings, which are broader and usually require tape; wraps or bandages, which wind around a body part; or adhesive strips used only for wound closure, which are thin closure tapes rather than padded bandages.

name: banjo
420.description: A banjo is a stringed instrument with a circular, drum-like body made from a taut membrane stretched over a rim, plus a long fretted neck and usually four to six strings. Most examples show the common five-string banjo, recognizable by the short fifth string with its tuning peg mounted partway up the neck.
420.guidelines: Classify as banjo when the instrument has a round drum-head body and a long neck with strings. The clearest cue for a five-string banjo is the extra short fifth string whose tuning peg sits halfway up the neck. Do not confuse it with a guitar, mandolin, or ukulele, which have wooden box bodies rather than a membrane head, or with a tambourine/frame drum, which lacks a long fretted neck and full string setup.

name: railing
421.description: A railing is a linear barrier or support structure, typically running along stairs, landings, balconies, ramps, or edges. It usually consists of a handrail supported by vertical posts, balusters, glass panels, or metal bars, and is designed to be grasped for support and to prevent falls.
421.guidelines: Classify as railing when the prominent object is the protective or graspable barrier along a stairway, balcony, walkway, or edge. Include metal, wood, glass, or stone railings and balustrades. Do not confuse with the stairs or escalator themselves: the railing is the side support, not the steps. A handrail alone may qualify if it is clearly the main support rail; balusters are the vertical elements within a railing, not a separate class here.

name: barbell
422.description: A barbell is a long straight metal weightlifting bar, usually steel, with sleeve ends that hold round weight plates secured by collars or clamps. It is used for exercises such as the bench press, squat, deadlift, overhead press, and similar lifts. The defining form is a single rigid bar designed to be gripped with both hands, typically loaded symmetrically on both ends.
422.guidelines: Classify as barbell when the main object is a long two-handed lifting bar, usually with weight plates mounted on both ends. Include unloaded barbells if the straight weighted bar itself is clearly shown. Do not confuse with dumbbells, which are short one-handed weights; EZ curl bars, which have a bent or zigzag shaft; or weight machines and Smith machines, where the bar is attached to a frame or rails unless the barbell itself is the clear subject. Exclude loose weight plates by themselves and exercise scenes where the barbell is too small or incidental.

name: barber chair
423.description: A heavy padded chair used for hair cutting and grooming, typically with a broad seat and backrest, upholstered armrests, a metal pedestal base, and a footrest. It often swivels and reclines, and many examples have a hydraulic height-adjustment column and attached headrest.
423.guidelines: Classify as barber chair only when the chair is the specialized salon/barbershop type with a pedestal base, footrest, and robust reclining or height-adjustable structure. Do not confuse with a salon styling chair, which is often simpler and lacks the prominent footrest and reclining mechanism, or with a dentist's chair, which is bulkier and more medical-looking with leg support and attached equipment. Also exclude ordinary armchairs or office chairs that do not have the characteristic barbershop pedestal and footrest.

name: barbershop
424.description: A barbershop is a small hair-cutting business or storefront for grooming, especially men’s hair and shaving. It often appears as a street-level shop with signage reading “barber shop” or similar, traditional barber poles with red-white-blue stripes, large front windows, barber chairs, mirrors, clippers, and customers receiving haircuts or shaves.
424.guidelines: Classify as barbershop when the image shows a barbering business, its interior, or its storefront signage. Common cues are barber chairs, mirrors, haircutting in progress, shaving scenes, and barber-pole stripes. Do not confuse with a beauty salon or hair salon, which more often emphasizes women’s hairstyling, wash stations, dryers, manicure services, or more general salon branding. Also exclude generic storefronts or signs unless they clearly indicate barber services.

name: barn
425.description: A barn is a large rural farm building, usually a simple rectangular structure with a tall broad mass, a pitched gambrel or gabled roof, and wide doors for animals, hay, or equipment. It is commonly made of wood or metal siding and often painted red, brown, or left weathered gray.
425.guidelines: Classify as barn when the image shows a substantial farm outbuilding used for storage or livestock, typically freestanding in a field or farmyard and larger than a shed. Common look-alikes include sheds, stables, warehouses, and houses. Barns are usually bulkier and taller than sheds, less residential than houses, and more plainly agricultural than warehouses. Silos may appear nearby but are not themselves barns; fences, fields, and large loft-style doors are helpful cues.

name: barometer
426.description: An instrument for measuring atmospheric pressure, most often shown as a round analog dial with a pointer and a calibrated scale. The face commonly includes weather words such as “stormy,” “rain,” “change,” “fair,” or “dry,” and may be mounted in brass, wood, or a wall plaque; some examples are part of multi-instrument weather stations with thermometer or hygrometer dials alongside it.
426.guidelines: Classify as a barometer when the main object is an atmospheric-pressure gauge, typically with a circular pointer dial and pressure/weather labels. Do not confuse it with a thermometer (single temperature scale, often a tube or °C/°F dial), hygrometer (humidity scale marked %), clock (hour numerals and time hands), or compass (direction labels N/E/S/W). Multi-instrument weather stations still count if the barometer dial is the primary component or clearly present.

name: barrel
427.description: A large cylindrical container with a bulging middle and narrower ends, made either of wooden staves bound by metal hoops or of metal sheet. It is typically upright or stored on its side and used to hold or age liquids, especially alcoholic beverages, though similar forms are also used for oil and other bulk liquids.
427.guidelines: Classify as barrel when the object is the familiar cask/drum-shaped storage container with rounded sides and flat circular ends, in wood or metal. Include wine and whiskey casks and metal barrels/oil drums when the category is used broadly. Do not confuse with a bucket or tub, which are open-topped and usually smaller; a keg, which is typically smaller and more standardized for beer; or a tank or vat, which are much larger and usually lack the classic barrel profile with hoops and curved sides.

name: wheelbarrow
428.description: A wheelbarrow is a small hand-propelled cart with a shallow open tray or tub, two long handles at the rear, and usually a single wheel centered at the front. It is commonly made of metal or plastic and used to carry soil, plants, tools, rubble, or other loads.
428.guidelines: Classify as wheelbarrow when the object is a push cart with one front wheel and two rear handles supporting an open load tray. Include typical garden and construction wheelbarrows, whether metal, plastic, old, decorative, or loaded. Do not confuse with a garden cart or lawn cart, which usually has two or four wheels and is pulled rather than lifted and pushed; a hand truck/dolly, which has a vertical frame instead of a tray; or a wagon, which has multiple wheels and a deeper box-like body.

name: baseball
baseball
429.description: A small hard ball used in baseball, typically white or off-white and covered in leather or synthetic leather, with two curved seams stitched in red that form a distinctive figure-eight pattern around the surface. It is usually spherical, palm-sized, and may appear clean, scuffed, or dirt-stained from play.
429.guidelines: Classify as a baseball when the object is the ball itself, identified by its compact spherical shape and characteristic red stitched curved seams on a white cover. Do not confuse it with a softball, which is noticeably larger and often yellow; a cricket ball, which is usually solid red or white with a raised straight seam; a tennis ball, which is fuzzy and fluorescent; or a golf ball, which has dimples instead of stitched seams. Ignore surrounding bats, gloves, or field context unless the ball’s seam pattern matches a baseball.

name: basketball
430.description: A basketball is a large, round inflatable ball used in the sport of basketball, typically orange or tan with black channel lines dividing the surface into panels. It has a pebbled rubber, leather, or composite texture and is commonly shown being dribbled, passed, shot, or held on an indoor court or near a hoop.
430.guidelines: Classify as basketball when the central object is the distinctive basketball ball itself: a spherical ball with dark seam lines and a textured surface, usually orange. Do not confuse it with other sports balls such as volleyballs, soccer balls, or playground balls, which differ in panel pattern, color scheme, and surface texture. Ignore surrounding players, hoops, or courts; the category is the ball, not the sport scene.

name: bassinet
431.description: A bassinet is a small, lightweight bed for a newborn, typically with a padded oval or rectangular sleeping basket, high fabric-lined sides, and a compact frame or stand. Many are wicker, fabric, or mesh, and are designed to hold an infant lying flat during the first few months of life.
431.guidelines: Classify as a bassinet when the image shows a freestanding newborn bed that is smaller and lighter than a crib, often basket-like and sometimes raised on legs, wheels, or a folding stand. Do not confuse it with a crib, which is larger, deeper, and built with rigid slatted sides for older infants; a cradle, which is usually a sturdier rocking bed; or a stroller/pram, which has clear transport features such as large wheels and a push handle. Bassinets are primarily indoor infant sleep baskets rather than full-size nursery beds or wheeled carriers.

name: bassoon
432.description: A bassoon is a long, folded double-reed woodwind with a reddish-brown wooden body, many silver-colored keys, and a narrow curved metal bocal leading to the reed. Its tubing doubles back on itself into a tall U-shaped form, with a flared bell at the top and a long vertical overall profile.
432.guidelines: Classify as a bassoon when the instrument is a large folded wooden woodwind with extensive keywork and a curved metal bocal. Do not confuse it with an oboe or English horn, which are much smaller and mostly straight, or with a saxophone, which is metal-bodied. It can resemble a contrabassoon, but a contrabassoon is much larger, more heavily folded, and usually has more looping tubing.

name: swim cap
433.description: A close-fitting cap worn over the hair for swimming, typically made of smooth rubber, latex, silicone, or similar waterproof material. It covers most or all of the scalp and fits tightly to the head, often in solid bright colors, sometimes with logos or printed designs.
433.guidelines: Classify as swim cap when the main object is a tight, head-hugging cap specifically for use in swimming. Common look-alikes include shower caps, winter beanies, and wetsuit hoods. Swim caps are smooth and sleek rather than loose or puffy like shower caps, knitted like beanies, or extended to cover the neck and shoulders like hoods. Ignore surrounding swim goggles or swimsuits unless the cap itself is clearly visible.

name: bath towel
434.description: A bath towel is a large rectangular towel made of absorbent fabric, usually terry cloth or similar woven cotton, often thick, soft, and plush. It may be plain, striped, embroidered, or patterned, and is typically shown folded, rolled, hanging, or wrapped around the body after bathing.
434.guidelines: Classify as bath towel when the item is a full-size body towel intended for drying after a bath or shower. Common appearances include thick cotton towels hanging in bathrooms, stacked towels, or towels wrapped around a person’s body or hair. Do not confuse with hand towels or washcloths, which are much smaller; beach towels, which are often larger and more vividly printed; bathrobes, which are wearable garments with sleeves; or blankets and sheets, which are larger bedding textiles and usually less towel-like in texture.

name: bathing tub
435.description: A large open tub or basin meant for a person to sit or recline in while bathing. It is typically oval, rectangular, or rounded-rectangular, with high sides, a smooth waterproof interior, and a drain and faucet; many are porcelain, fiberglass, metal, wood, or acrylic. Examples include standard indoor bathtubs, freestanding clawfoot tubs, built-in tubs, and spa-style hot tubs or jacuzzis.
435.guidelines: Classify any image whose main object is a human-sized immersion tub for bathing, whether indoors or outdoors, empty or occupied, and including hot tubs/jacuzzis. Do not confuse with a sink or washbasin, which is smaller and meant mainly for hands or face; a swimming pool, which is much larger and built into the ground; a toilet bowl, which is deeper and has a seat and tank; or animal troughs and utility containers, which lack bathroom/spa fixtures and human-bathing form.

name: station wagon
estate car
436.description: A passenger car with a long roofline that extends straight back over an enlarged rear cargo area, ending in a rear hatch or tailgate. It typically has four side doors, large rear side windows, and a two-box profile that combines a sedan-like front with a longer, boxier rear body for luggage or goods.
436.guidelines: Classify as a station wagon (estate car) when the car has a continuous roof to the rear and a full-height rear cargo compartment accessed by a hatch or tailgate. Do not confuse it with a sedan, which has a separate enclosed trunk; a hatchback, which is usually shorter and more compact with a steeper rear; an SUV or crossover, which sits taller with higher ground clearance and a bulkier body; or a minivan, which is taller and more van-like with a one-box profile. The key cue is a car-based body with an elongated roof and wagon-style rear cargo area.

name: lighthouse
437.description: A lighthouse is a tall navigational tower or coastal building structure, usually standing alone on a shore, pier, breakwater, reef, or rocky island. It commonly has a cylindrical, tapered, square, or polygonal tower body with a lantern room and light at the top, often with a gallery or railing below the lantern. Typical colors are white, red, black, or striped daymark patterns, and many are attached to or accompanied by low keeper’s buildings.
437.guidelines: Classify as a lighthouse when the structure is a purpose-built navigational light tower with a prominent lantern room at the top and a coastal or harbor setting. Include both large shore lighthouses and smaller pierhead or offshore light towers. Do not confuse with water towers, chimneys, minarets, church steeples, observation towers, or decorative garden lanterns: those lack the characteristic lantern room, gallery, and marine navigational context. Also distinguish from generic beacons or buoys, which are much smaller marker structures rather than substantial lighthouse towers.

name: beaker
438.description: A beaker is a simple cylindrical laboratory container, usually made of thin glass or clear plastic, with a flat bottom, straight or slightly flared sides, a wide open top, and typically a small pouring spout. Many examples have printed volume graduations, but it is mainly a general-purpose lab vessel rather than a precision measuring container.
438.guidelines: Classify as a beaker when the vessel is broad, open-topped, and roughly cylindrical with a pour lip. Do not confuse it with a graduated cylinder, which is much taller and narrower; an Erlenmeyer flask, which has a conical body and narrow neck; a volumetric flask, which has a round bulb and long neck; or a cup/mug/measuring cup, which typically has a handle or kitchen-style form.

name: bearskin
bearskin cap
439.description: A tall, cylindrical military fur hat made of dense black fur, usually worn upright and covering much of the head and forehead. In these images it is most often seen as the ceremonial headgear of British guards, paired with red tunics or dark dress uniforms; some examples include a small colored plume or side ornament.
439.guidelines: Classify this as a bearskin when the hat is very tall, black, furry, and vertically cylindrical with a rounded top. Do not confuse it with a shako, which is a stiff cloth or leather military hat with a structured, non-furry surface, or with a busby, which is generally shorter and often has a distinct colored cloth bag hanging from the side. The key cue here is the large full fur body of the hat.

name: beer bottle
440.description: A beer bottle is a narrow-necked glass bottle made for beer, usually brown, green, or clear, with a long or short cylindrical body, sloped shoulders, and a crown cap, swing-top, or similar closure. Labels and branding are common, and the bottle may be shown full, empty, upright, lying down, chilled, or grouped with other bottles.
440.guidelines: Classify as beer bottle when the image shows a glass bottle specifically intended for beer packaging. Typical cues are amber or green glass, a capped narrow neck, brewery labeling, and the standard beer-bottle silhouette. Do not confuse with wine bottles, which are usually taller with broader bodies and longer necks; liquor bottles, which often have heavier glass and more varied shapes; or soda bottles, which are commonly plastic or have softer-drink branding. Exclude generic bottles unless beer branding or the characteristic beer-bottle form is clear.

name: beer glass
441.description: A drinking glass made for serving beer, typically clear glass and sized larger than a standard drinking glass. It may be cylindrical, slightly tapered, flared, footed, or mug-shaped, and often holds pale golden to dark amber beer with a foamy head. Many examples have brewery logos or pub branding.
441.guidelines: Classify as beer glass when the item is a glass vessel specifically intended for beer service, whether empty or filled. Include pint glasses, pilsner glasses, beer mugs, and similar branded pub glasses. Do not confuse with wine glasses, champagne flutes, cocktail coupes, or generic tumblers: beer glasses are usually sturdier, wider-mouthed, and associated with beer presentation, often showing foam head, amber liquid, handles, or brewery markings.

name: bell cote
442.description: A bell cote is a small bell housing attached to the top of a roof, gable, or wall rather than a full tower. It is usually a simple open arch, pair of arches, or small turret holding one or more visible bells, often capped by a short pitched roof, triangular gable, or plain masonry top, and sometimes topped with a cross or finial. It lacks the height and mass of a true bell tower and usually has no large dome or substantial spire.
442.guidelines: Classify as bell cote when the main feature is a small open bell structure perched on a church roofline, facade, or gable. Look for one or more bells suspended in open archways with only a minimal housing around them. Do not confuse with a bell tower or steeple, which is a larger vertically extended tower; a cupola or lantern, which is typically enclosed or windowed; or a spire, which is a tall pointed roof rather than an open bell opening. If the bell is housed in a modest rooftop arch or tiny turret rather than a full tower, it is a bell cote.

name: baby bib
443.description: A baby bib is a small protective cloth or waterproof panel worn on an infant’s or toddler’s chest, hanging from the neck and covering the front of the shirt. It is usually rounded or U-shaped with a neck opening or ties/snaps, and is made from absorbent fabric, plastic-coated material, or both. Many have decorative prints, embroidery, or appliqué.
443.guidelines: Classify as baby bib when the item is specifically a neck-worn feeding or drool protector for babies, covering the upper chest. Typical cues are a bib-like rounded shape, neck opening, and soft or wipe-clean material. Do not confuse with an apron, which is larger and covers more of the torso, or with a burp cloth, towel, or washcloth, which lack a neck opening and are not worn. Also exclude full baby smocks or sleeved feeding garments that function more like protective clothing than a simple bib.

name: tandem bicycle
444.description: A bicycle built for two or more riders, with an elongated frame carrying multiple saddles, handlebar positions, and pedal sets arranged one behind another. Most examples have two wheels and two rider positions in line, though frame style, handlebar shape, and wheel size can vary.
444.guidelines: Classify as a tandem bicycle when the bike is clearly designed for multiple riders sharing one extended frame, typically with two seats and two pedal stations. Do not confuse with a standard bicycle, which has only one rider position, or with side-by-side or four-wheeled multi-person cycles such as surreys or quadracycles. The key cue is the long in-line frame with repeated rider components.

name: bikini
445.description: A bikini is a women’s two-piece swimsuit consisting of a separate top and bottom, typically revealing the midriff. It appears in many cuts and styles, but the defining visual trait is that the upper and lower garments are separate pieces worn for swimming or sunbathing.
445.guidelines: Classify as bikini when the swimwear clearly has two separate pieces: a bikini top and bikini bottoms. Do not confuse with a one-piece swimsuit or monokini, which forms a single connected garment, or with underwear/lingerie, which may look similar but is usually styled for indoor wear rather than swimming. Ignore variations in coverage, color, ties, straps, or decorative design as long as it remains a two-piece swimsuit.

name: ring binder
446.description: A ring binder is a hard or flexible cover folder fitted with a metal ring mechanism inside the spine, used to hold loose-leaf paper or punched plastic sleeves. It is typically rectangular like a book or portfolio and may appear as an office binder, presentation binder, or planner-style organizer.
446.guidelines: Classify as ring binder when the object’s defining feature is the internal metal rings or ring mechanism for securing punched pages. Include closed binders if the ring-binder form is clear from the spine, covers, or context. Do not confuse with clipboards, folders, notebooks, or spiral-bound books: those lack the hinged metal rings mounted inside the binder. Also exclude lever-arch files and box files unless they are clearly ring binders with exposed ring hardware.

name: binoculars
447.description: A handheld or mounted optical viewing device with two parallel tubes or eyepieces for both eyes, used to magnify distant objects. It typically has a pair of side-by-side objective lenses and eyepieces joined by a central bridge, and may appear as compact opera glasses, standard field binoculars, or fixed public viewing binoculars.
447.guidelines: Classify as binoculars when the device is a dual-eye viewer with two eyepieces used simultaneously. This includes handheld field glasses, opera glasses, and pedestal-mounted viewing binoculars. Do not confuse with a telescope or spyglass, which usually has a single viewing tube and one eyepiece, or with cameras/VR headsets, which may have two lenses but are not primarily optical viewers for direct distant viewing.

name: birdhouse
448.description: A birdhouse is a small shelter or nesting box for birds, usually made of wood and shaped like a miniature house or simple box. It typically has one or more round entry holes on the front, often a pitched roof, and may be mounted on a post, hung from a branch, or attached to a tree or wall. Designs range from plain functional nest boxes to decorative house-like forms.
448.guidelines: Classify as birdhouse when the object is a bird nesting shelter with an enclosed cavity and a small entrance hole. Common look-alikes include bird feeders, which are open or have trays/ports for accessible food rather than an enclosed nest cavity; doghouses, which are much larger with open doorways; and decorative miniature houses not intended for birds. The key cues are small scale, outdoor mounting, enclosed box structure, and one or more small bird-sized entrance holes.

name: boathouse
449.description: A boathouse is a small to medium building built on the edge of, over, or partly in the water for storing boats. It typically has a simple shed- or house-like form, often with large waterfront doors or an open bay at water level so boats can be moved directly in and out. Common materials include wood siding and pitched roofs; some stand on pilings or stilts above the water.
449.guidelines: Classify as boathouse when the structure is primarily a waterside building for housing boats, usually with direct boat access from the water. Do not confuse with a dock or pier, which is an open platform rather than an enclosed building; a houseboat, which is itself a floating dwelling or vessel; a stilt house or overwater house, which is meant for living rather than boat storage; or a marina building, which is part of a larger harbor facility and not specifically a boat-storage shed.

name: bobsled
450.description: A long, narrow, streamlined racing sled used in bobsleigh, typically with a rounded aerodynamic nose, enclosed body shell, and metal runners underneath. It is built for ice tracks and often appears as a two-person or four-person sled, with athletes pushing or riding inside or partly visible from the cockpit.
450.guidelines: Classify as bobsled only when the image shows the enclosed aerodynamic sled used in the sport of bobsleigh. Key cues are the bullet-shaped body, multiple-person cockpit, and use on an iced bobsleigh track. Do not confuse it with a luge sled or skeleton sled, which are much smaller, flatter, and ridden by a single athlete without a large enclosing shell; or with ordinary toboggans and snow sleds, which lack the heavy streamlined racing body and metal running gear.

name: bolo tie
451.description: A necktie made from a cord or braided leather string fastened with a decorative sliding clasp or ornament, usually worn under a shirt collar. It typically has two hanging cord ends below the clasp, often tipped with metal points, and the central slide may feature stone, metalwork, enamel, or carved designs.
451.guidelines: Classify as a bolo tie when the item is a cord necktie with an adjustable central slide and two dangling ends. Common look-alikes include necklaces, pendants, medallions, and lariats: unlike those, a bolo tie is worn like a necktie and has a pair of cords hanging below the front clasp. Also distinguish it from a regular necktie or bow tie, which are made of fabric rather than cord.

name: bonnet
452.description: A soft hat with a close-fitting crown and ties or ribbons under the chin, often worn by babies, children, or in old-fashioned styles. It typically frames the face, covers the top and sides of the head, and may have a brim, flared front, ruffles, or a pointed pixie-like shape. Common materials include fabric, knit, or crochet, often in pastel colors, prints, or decorative trims.
452.guidelines: Classify as a bonnet when the headwear is a soft cap or hat tied under the chin and fitted around the head, usually framing the face. Include baby bonnets, sun bonnets, and poke bonnets. Do not confuse with beanies or knit caps, which usually lack chin ties and a face-framing brim; hoods, which are attached to a garment; or broad-brimmed sun hats, which have a full circular brim rather than a fitted tied cap.

name: bookcase
453.description: A tall or medium-height piece of furniture with multiple horizontal shelves arranged in a vertical frame for storing and displaying books. Usually made of wood, metal, or laminate, it may be open-fronted or have sides, backing, doors, or decorative trim; shelves are typically straight, evenly spaced, and sized to hold rows of books upright or stacked.
453.guidelines: Classify as bookcase when the main object is a shelving unit intended for books, typically a vertical furniture piece with several shelves. Include both filled and empty bookcases, and built-in or freestanding examples. Do not confuse with a generic shelf or storage rack: bookcases are usually taller, furniture-like, and proportioned for books. Exclude cabinets, dressers, cupboards, and display cases whose primary form is enclosed storage, as well as library room interiors where no single bookcase is the main object.

name: library
bookstore
454.description: Indoor or street-front spaces organized around books, with tall shelving, bookcases, display tables, stacked volumes, and browsing aisles. Images may show public-library reading stacks or service desks, or retail bookshops and bookstalls with featured displays, storefront signs, and books for sale.
454.guidelines: Classify as this category when the scene is clearly a library or a bookstore/bookstall: books dominate the space and are arranged on shelves or display tables for browsing, reading, borrowing, or purchase. Include both interiors and storefront exteriors. Do not confuse with a generic shop, newsstand, office, classroom, or archive: this category is defined by a dedicated book-focused environment. Libraries often have uniform shelving, reading/study areas, and circulation desks; bookstores more often have front-window displays, merchandising tables, price signage, and commercial storefront branding.

name: metal bottle cap
455.description: A small round metal cap used to seal glass beverage bottles, typically with a flat printed top and crimped, ridged edges that grip the bottle neck. It is usually made of thin painted or printed metal and often shows brand logos, colors, or decorative designs.
455.guidelines: Classify as metal bottle cap only when the object is a crown-style metal closure with a circular top and corrugated edge. It may appear loose, attached to a bottle, flattened, rusted, or reused in crafts, but the cap itself should remain identifiable. Do not confuse it with plastic bottle caps, jar lids, can tops, pull tabs, or the bottle itself. The key cues are the shallow circular shape and the distinct crimped metal rim.

name: bow
456.description: A bow is a handheld archery weapon or sporting implement made of a flexible curved stave with a string stretched between its ends, used to launch arrows. It may be simple or highly engineered, including longbows, recurve bows, and compound bows with cams and accessories. We annotate the bow itself even when no arrow is present.
456.guidelines: Classify images showing an archery bow: a curved frame with a taut string, whether being held, used, displayed, or shown alone. Include traditional wooden bows, modern recurve bows, compound bows, and toy bows if the object is clearly a bow. Do not confuse it with a crossbow, which has a horizontal bow mounted on a stock; a violin bow, which is a straight stick with hair; or unrelated curved tools and poles. The key cue is a flexible bow body with a string for shooting arrows.

name: bow tie
457.description: A bow tie is a short necktie tied into a compact, symmetrical bow at the collar. It consists of two side loops and two pointed or rounded ends meeting in a central knot, and may be solid-colored, patterned, or made from satin, silk, cotton, or similar fabric.
457.guidelines: Classify images as bow ties when the neckwear forms a distinct bow shape centered at the neck or appears as an untied bow-tie garment. Include both worn and standalone bow ties. Do not confuse with a standard necktie or cravat, which hangs down in a long strip, or with a ribbon bow used for decoration rather than neckwear. The key cue is the small, horizontal bow form at the collar.

name: commemorative plaque
458.description: A flat inscribed tablet mounted on a wall, stone, pedestal, or stand, typically made of metal or stone and bearing engraved or raised text, dates, names, and sometimes emblems or decorative borders to commemorate a person, place, group, or event.
458.guidelines: Classify as a commemorative plaque when the image centers on a permanent inscribed tablet or plate installed as a marker or memorial. It may be bronze, brass, stone, or another durable material, and is usually mounted to masonry, rock, or a monument base. Do not confuse it with a gravestone or headstone, which marks a grave and is usually a larger upright or horizontal burial marker; a sign, which mainly gives directions or information rather than commemoration; or a monument/obelisk, where the main object is the larger structure rather than the attached inscribed tablet.

name: bra
459.description: A bra is a close-fitting undergarment for the upper torso, designed to cover and support the breasts. It typically has two shaped cups, a band around the chest, and shoulder straps; common materials include knit fabric, satin, lace, or foam-padded textiles.
459.guidelines: Classify as bra when the image shows the breast-supporting undergarment itself, whether worn, displayed flat, on a mannequin, or in advertising. Key cues are two distinct cups, a chest band, and usually shoulder straps. Do not confuse with a bikini top or swimsuit top, which are swimwear and often appear in beach or pool contexts with matching bottoms and swim fabric; a sports bra, which is a bra subtype but typically has a simpler, more compressive athletic design; or a camisole, bustier, corset, or bralette-style top that extends farther down the torso. If the item is specifically a standard breast-supporting undergarment, label it as bra.

name: breakwater
460.description: A long, massive barrier of concrete, stone, timber, or steel built out from the shore or along the water’s edge to reduce wave action and protect a harbor, channel, or shoreline. It typically appears as a low linear wall, rock embankment, or pile of interlocking blocks projecting into open water or running parallel to shore.
460.guidelines: Classify structures whose main purpose is coastal or harbor protection from waves: rock or concrete sea barriers, harbor moles, groynes, and similar seawalls. Do not confuse with a pier, dock, or quay, which are mainly for berthing boats and usually have decks, pilings, railings, or clear access for people and vehicles. Also exclude boats, ships, and ordinary shoreline views where the protective barrier is not the subject.

name: cuirass
461.description: A rigid torso armor piece made of plate or molded material, covering the chest, back, or both. It is usually a solid shell rather than a flexible garment, and may appear as a breastplate alone, a backplate, or a full body cuirass, in metal, leather, or modern protective materials.
461.guidelines: Classify as cuirass when the main object is a single rigid torso defense covering the front, back, or both. Include historical breastplates and modern molded chest armor if they are plate-like and torso-covering. Do not confuse with chain mail, which is flexible and mesh-like; with full suits of armor when the whole suit is the subject rather than the torso plate; or with shoulder guards, helmets, and other separate armor parts. The key cue is a solid, one-piece or paired rigid torso shell.

name: broom
462.description: A broom is a cleaning tool with a long handle and a head made of bundled straw, twigs, reeds, corn fibers, or synthetic bristles tied or fixed together at one end. The sweeping end is typically fan-shaped, cylindrical, or slightly flared, and is used for sweeping floors, ground, or outdoor surfaces.
462.guidelines: Classify as broom when the object is a handled sweeping tool with bundled fibers or twigs forming the main head. Include traditional straw brooms, twig brooms, and synthetic household brooms. Do not confuse with a mop, which has loose absorbent strands for wet cleaning; a brush, which usually has a smaller rigid block or compact bristle base; a rake, which has separated tines rather than a fiber bundle; or a whisk broom/hand broom, which lacks the long handle typical of a broom.

name: bucket
463.description: A bucket is a portable open-top container, usually roughly cylindrical or slightly tapered, with a flat or rounded bottom and a wire, metal, or plastic handle for carrying. It may be made of plastic, metal, or wood and comes in many sizes, from small decorative pails to large utility buckets.
463.guidelines: Classify as bucket when the object is a simple handled open container meant for carrying or holding water, sand, paint, food scraps, or similar contents. Include both utility buckets and pails in varied materials and shapes. Do not confuse with tubs, basins, or bowls, which are typically wider and lack a single carrying handle; flower pots or planters, which are usually meant for plants and often have no handle; trash cans, which are larger and usually stand alone; or watering cans, which have a spout.

name: buckle
464.description: A buckle is a fastening device, usually metal but sometimes plastic, attached to a belt, strap, shoe, bag, or garment. It typically has a rigid frame and a method of closure such as a prong, bar, clasp, or snap, and may be plain, polished, or highly decorative.
464.guidelines: Classify images as buckles when the fastening hardware itself is the main subject: a framed clasp or closure used to secure a strap, belt, or similar item. Include belt buckles, shoe buckles, bag buckles, and decorative garment buckles. Do not confuse with the whole belt, strap, collar, harness, or sandal when the hardware is not the focus. Distinguish from buttons, zippers, brooches, and jewelry by the presence of a functional strap-fastening mechanism rather than a simple ornament or sewn closure.

name: bulletproof vest
465.description: A sleeveless protective torso garment worn over clothing, typically covering the chest and back. It is usually thick, padded, and boxy, with broad shoulder straps and a close-fitting vest shape. Common colors are black, navy, olive, tan, or camouflage, and many examples have panel seams, external pockets, webbing, or plate-carrier-style sections.
465.guidelines: Classify as bulletproof vest when the main object is a ballistic protective vest designed to stop or reduce gunfire injury. Include soft armor vests, tactical body armor, and plate carriers worn by police, military, or security personnel. Do not confuse with life jackets or flotation vests, which are bulkier and buoyant-looking; fashion vests, which are thinner and tailored; load-bearing or fishing vests, which have many pockets but little armor padding; or motocross/chest protectors, which use hard molded plastic shells rather than ballistic panels.

name: bullet train
466.description: A streamlined high-speed passenger train with a long, pointed aerodynamic nose, smooth rounded body, and sleek modern cars, typically seen on electrified rail lines and station platforms. Most examples are white, silver, or light gray, often with blue, green, or orange accent stripes.
466.guidelines: Classify as bullet train when the image shows a very fast, streamlined high-speed train with a distinct aerodynamic nose and sleek continuous body profile. Do not confuse it with ordinary passenger trains, commuter rail, or locomotives, which have boxier fronts and less extreme streamlining; or with metro/subway trains, which are shorter, squarer, and built for urban platforms. High-speed trains with blunt or non-bullet-shaped noses may still belong if they clearly match the modern dedicated high-speed rail style.

name: butcher shop
meat market
467.description: A retail stall or shop displaying raw or cured meat for sale, often with hanging carcasses or large cuts, butcher counters, chopping blocks, scales, refrigerated cases, sausages, and trays of pork, beef, lamb, or other meat products.
467.guidelines: Classify as butcher shop or meat market when the image shows a place primarily devoted to selling meat, especially with butcher counters, hanging cuts, carcasses, or meat displays. Do not confuse with a general grocery store or supermarket, which has mixed food sections; a delicatessen, which emphasizes prepared foods and sliced cold cuts; or a fish market, which mainly shows seafood. The key cue is that the scene is centered on fresh or cured meat being butchered, displayed, or sold.

name: taxicab
468.description: A passenger car used as a taxi, typically marked for hire with a roof light or illuminated TAXI sign, company markings, license numbers, or a distinctive livery such as yellow paint, checker stripes, or other city-specific taxi colors.
468.guidelines: Classify as taxicab when the vehicle is clearly identifiable as a for-hire taxi by taxi signage, roof lights, fare markings, medallion or company text, or a well-known taxi livery. Include sedans, vans, SUVs, and older classic taxi models if they are visibly functioning as taxis. Do not confuse with ordinary cars painted yellow, police cars, ride-share vehicles, limousines, or buses; the key cues are explicit taxi identifiers rather than just vehicle shape or color.

name: cauldron
469.description: A cauldron is a large deep cooking vessel with a wide open top, rounded bowl-like body, and thick metal walls, traditionally cast iron or copper. It typically has a black or dark metallic finish, often stands on three short legs or a rounded base, and may have side handles or a swinging bail handle for hanging over a fire. It is commonly shown holding soups, stews, or boiling liquid.
