469.guidelines: Classify as a cauldron when the vessel is a heavy, deep, wide-mouthed pot with a rounded belly, associated with boiling or cooking over an open fire. It may have legs, a bail handle, or a distinctly old-fashioned cast-metal look. Do not confuse with a stockpot or Dutch oven, which usually have straighter sides, flatter bottoms, tighter-fitting lids, and are made for stovetops; a kettle, which has a spout and narrower opening; or a wok, which is broad and shallow. Exclude decorative bowls, planters, and cakes merely shaped like cauldrons unless the object itself is clearly a cauldron.

name: candle
470.description: A candle is a wax or similar fuel body with an embedded wick that burns with a small steady flame. It may be cylindrical, tapered, molded, or contained in a cup or glass holder, and is often white or colored. Melted wax, dripping sides, and a glowing wick are common visual features.
470.guidelines: Classify as candle when the main object is a wax light source with a wick, whether freestanding, tapered, pillar-shaped, tea light, votive, birthday candle, or in a holder. Do not confuse with oil lamps, electric candles, lanterns, or decorative light fixtures: candles have visible wax and a wick. Candleholders or candelabras may appear, but the category should center on the candle itself rather than the stand.

name: cannon
471.description: A cannon is a large, heavy artillery gun with a long thick barrel, usually made of metal, often mounted on a carriage, base, fortification, or ship. It is typically cylindrical with a prominent muzzle opening, and may appear on wheels, naval mounts, or fixed supports.
471.guidelines: Classify as cannon when the image shows a large mounted artillery piece with a single substantial barrel, especially historical or fortress/naval guns. Do not confuse it with a howitzer or field gun, which often have more modern split-trail carriages and shorter proportions, or with tank guns and naval turrets where the vehicle or turret system is the main subject. Smaller handheld firearms, machine guns, and decorative pipes are not cannons.

name: kayak
472.description: A small, narrow watercraft with a pointed bow and stern, low profile, and one or more seated paddlers. It is typically propelled with a double-bladed paddle, and may be a closed-deck or sit-on-top design made of rigid plastic or inflatable material.
472.guidelines: Classify as kayak when the boat is slim, low to the water, and used with a double-bladed paddle. Include both solo and tandem kayaks, including sit-on-top recreational models. Do not confuse with a canoe, which is usually more open on top, rides higher, and is typically paddled with a single-bladed paddle. Also exclude rowboats or dinghies, which use oars attached to the boat rather than a handheld double paddle.

name: can opener
473.description: A handheld kitchen tool for opening metal cans, typically with two squeeze handles or a turning knob, a clamping wheel, and a small cutting blade that bites into the can lid and travels around the rim. Most examples are metal with plastic or rubber grips and have a compact plier-like or crank-like form.
473.guidelines: Classify as can opener when the tool is specifically designed to cut open metal cans by gripping the rim with a cutting wheel/blade and gear or lever mechanism. It may be manual with twin handles, a side-cut style, or a mounted crank style. Do not confuse with bottle openers, which only hook under caps; corkscrews, which have a spiral worm; nutcrackers or pliers, which lack a can-cutting wheel; or jar openers, which grip lids without cutting them.

name: cardigan
474.description: A cardigan is a knitted sweater that opens down the front, usually fastened with buttons or sometimes left open. It is typically waist- to hip-length, with long or short sleeves, and may have a V-neck, round neck, ribbed edges, cable knit, or other sweater textures and patterns.
474.guidelines: Classify as a cardigan when the garment is a knit sweater with a full front opening. Distinguish it from a pullover sweater or jumper, which has no full front opening; from a jacket or blazer, which is usually woven and more structured rather than knitted; and from a hoodie or zip-up sweatshirt, which is usually made of sweatshirt fabric and often has a hood or zipper instead of a knit sweater construction.

name: side-view mirror
475.description: A mirror mounted on the outside of a car door or front side panel, usually in a black or body-colored housing. It typically has a rounded rectangular or oval reflective surface and shows the road, nearby vehicles, sky, or the side of the car; many examples include the warning text "Objects in mirror are closer than they appear."
475.guidelines: Classify as side-view mirror when the image centers on an exterior mirror attached to the side of a vehicle. Do not confuse it with a rear-view mirror, which is mounted inside the cabin at the top of the windshield, or with a generic mirror not attached to a car. Reflections of scenery or people are common, but the key cue is the mirror housing fixed to the vehicle exterior.

name: carousel
476.description: An amusement ride with a circular rotating platform carrying fixed seats, most commonly carved horses or other animals mounted on vertical poles, often with ornate painted panels, mirrors, canopies, and rows of lights. Riders sit on the figures or in benches as the whole structure turns around a central axis.
476.guidelines: Classify as carousel when the image shows a rotating round ride with mounted animals or bench seats arranged around a center, typically under a decorated canopy. Do not confuse it with swing rides, where chairs hang from chains; Ferris wheels, which are large vertical wheels; spinning flat rides such as teacups, which lack the characteristic carousel animals and poles; or playground roundabouts, which are simple small rotating platforms without ornate fairground decoration.

name: tool kit
477.description: A collection of multiple hand tools or small repair implements presented together in a case, box, pouch, roll, or tray. Typical kits include combinations of wrenches, screwdrivers, pliers, sockets, drill bits, hex keys, or similar tools arranged as a set rather than shown as a single loose tool.
477.guidelines: Classify as this category when the image shows a grouped set of tools sold, stored, or organized together as one kit. The container may be open or closed, but multiple tools should clearly belong to one set. Do not use this class for a single tool such as one hammer, wrench, drill, or screwdriver, even if photographed closely. Also exclude toolboxes, cabinets, or workshop scenes unless the emphasis is specifically on the organized multi-tool set itself.

name: carton
478.description: A carton is a paperboard or corrugated-paper box of any size, typically rectangular, with folded panels, flaps, and printed or plain exterior surfaces. It may appear as a fully assembled box, an open container, or a flat disassembled blank ready to be folded into shape.
478.guidelines: Classify as carton when the main object is a paper-based box or box blank made from folded cardboard, paperboard, or corrugated fiberboard. This includes packaging cartons, shipping boxes, folding cartons, and flattened box forms. Do not confuse with crates, plastic storage bins, wooden boxes, or rigid cases made of metal or fabric. The key cues are paper/cardboard material, fold lines, flaps, and packaging-box construction.

name: car wheel
479.description: A wheel from a passenger automobile, typically shown as a circular rubber tire mounted around a metal wheel with a central hub, lug nuts, and often a hubcap or alloy spokes. It may appear alone or attached to the side of a car, and can range from plain steel wheels to decorative chrome or multi-spoke rims.
479.guidelines: Classify images as car wheel when the main subject is the wheel assembly of a passenger car. Include wheels with visible tire, rim, hubcap, spokes, or center cap, whether mounted on the car or shown separately. Do not confuse with just a tire by itself, a bare rim without the full wheel context, or close-ups dominated by brake discs. Exclude motorcycle or bicycle wheels, which are much thinner and often show spokes, and exclude truck or bus wheels, which are usually larger, heavier-duty, and associated with commercial vehicles.

name: ATM
automated teller machine
480.description: A self-service banking terminal with a screen, numeric keypad, card slot, cash dispenser, and often receipt slot or side buttons, typically built into a wall or housed in a freestanding kiosk. It is usually a boxy metal machine branded by a bank or ATM network and used for withdrawing cash and performing basic banking transactions.
480.guidelines: Classify as an ATM when the machine is clearly a bank cash machine or teller terminal with a card reader, keypad, display, and cash-dispensing area. Include both wall-mounted and freestanding units. Do not confuse with payment kiosks, ticket machines, vending machines, parking meters, gas pumps, or self-checkout terminals: ATMs specifically have banking-oriented controls and cash/card transaction hardware, often with bank branding or labels such as ATM, cash machine, or teller. Exclude close-ups that show only a generic screen unless the ATM hardware or context is still evident.

name: Compact Cassette
481.description: A Compact Cassette is a small rectangular analog audio tape cartridge with a hard plastic shell, two visible reel hubs, and magnetic tape running between them behind a central window. It typically has label areas on the front, small holes and notches along the top and bottom edges, and comes in clear, black, white, or brightly colored plastic.
481.guidelines: Classify only standard Compact Cassettes used for audio recording/playback. Exclude larger VHS videocassettes, smaller DAT tapes, 8-track cartridges, and microcassettes. The key cues are the palm-sized rectangular shell, exactly two visible spools, exposed tape window, and the familiar Philips-style cassette shape with edge holes/notches.

name: cassette player
482.description: An audio device designed to play cassette tapes, typically with a rectangular body and a visible cassette compartment or slot sized for a compact cassette. It may appear as a portable Walkman-style unit, a tabletop cassette deck, a boombox, an integrated stereo component, or a small recorder, often with transport controls such as play, stop, rewind, fast-forward, and eject.
482.guidelines: Classify as cassette player when the main object is a machine for playing a compact cassette, whether portable or home audio equipment. Include cassette decks, boomboxes, portable cassette recorders, and Walkman-type players. Do not confuse with a cassette tape by itself, which is just the small plastic media cartridge; with VCRs or tape players for larger video cassettes; or with reel-to-reel tape machines, which use exposed tape reels instead of enclosed cassettes. If the object’s defining feature is a cassette bay or inserted compact cassette plus playback controls, it belongs here.

name: castle
483.description: A castle is a large fortified building or castle complex built for defense, typically with thick masonry walls, battlements, towers or keeps, gatehouses, and relatively small window openings. Castles are often elevated on hills, cliffs, or surrounded by water or defensive walls, and some castle grounds may also contain palace-like residential buildings.
483.guidelines: Classify as castle when the main subject is a fortified historic residence or stronghold with clear defensive architecture such as towers, crenellated walls, keeps, curtain walls, moats, or fortified gates. Include castle complexes even if part of the visible structure looks palace-like, as long as the overall site is a recognized fortified castle. Do not confuse with palaces or manor houses, which are grand residences but usually lack substantial defensive walls and towers; forts, which are primarily military defensive works without a residential castle form; churches or monasteries, which may be large stone buildings but lack battlements and fortified keeps; and ordinary towers or city walls shown without a castle complex.

name: catamaran
484.description: A catamaran is a boat or yacht with two usually parallel hulls joined by a deck or frame. It is commonly sail-powered, with a wide stance, open or bridged space between the hulls, and either one central mast or a low cabin spanning the twin hulls; some examples are motor catamarans.
484.guidelines: Classify as catamaran when the vessel clearly has two separate side-by-side hulls connected above the water. Do not confuse it with a monohull sailboat, which has a single central hull, or with a trimaran, which has one main hull plus two smaller outriggers. Exclude simple outrigger canoes unless the category explicitly includes outrigger craft; the defining cue here is the twin-hull layout.

name: compact disc player
485.description: An audio playback device with a slot- or tray-loading mechanism for compact discs, typically shown as a standalone hi-fi component, shelf stereo, boombox, car-style unit, or integrated media system. It usually has a flat front panel with a disc tray or disc slot, playback buttons, and often a display screen; top-loading models open to reveal a circular disc spindle.
485.guidelines: Classify devices whose defining function is playing compact discs, including standalone CD decks and stereos/boomboxes with a built-in CD player. Do not require the disc itself to be visible. Exclude DVD or Blu-ray players when they are primarily video devices, turntables that play vinyl records, cassette decks, and generic amplifiers/receivers or speakers with no CD mechanism. The key cue is a visible CD tray, slot, or top-loading disc compartment associated with audio playback controls.

name: cello
Violoncello
486.description: A large bowed string instrument with a hollow wooden hourglass-shaped body, flat front, arched back, two f-holes, four strings over a long fingerboard, and a scroll at the top. It is played upright, typically between the knees, and supported on the floor by a metal endpin; sizes can vary.
486.guidelines: Classify as cello when the instrument is a medium-large upright bowed string instrument with a rounded upper body and endpin, usually played seated between the knees. Do not confuse with double bass, which is much larger and has a taller, more droplet-shaped body with sloping shoulders; or with violin/viola, which are much smaller and played under the chin.

name: mobile phone
487.description: A handheld telephone designed for use on a cellular network. It is typically a small pocket-sized electronic device with a screen, buttons or a touchscreen, and a compact rectangular, flip, or slider form. Examples include candybar phones, clamshell phones, sliders, and early smartphones.
487.guidelines: Classify as a mobile phone when the device is a portable cellular handset meant for voice or data communication over a mobile network. It may have a numeric keypad, QWERTY keyboard, touchscreen, camera, or hinged/sliding body. Do not confuse with cordless landline phones, walkie-talkies, pagers, remote controls, media players, or tablets. Unlike cordless phones, mobile phones are self-contained pocket devices without a base station; unlike pagers and media players, they are built as telephones with calling controls, keypad/dial interface, earpiece, and microphone.

name: chain
488.description: A chain is a flexible series of connected links, usually metal, forming a linear loop or length. It may appear as heavy industrial hardware, a hanging or restraining chain, or a fine decorative or jewelry chain worn alone or supporting a pendant or pocket watch.
488.guidelines: Classify images as chain when the linked structure itself is the main subject, whether coarse or delicate. Include utility chains, anchor or restraint chains, and jewelry chains. Do not confuse with necklaces where beads, gems, charms, or pendants dominate the appearance; with ropes or cords, which are fibrous rather than made of interlocking links; or with mesh, nets, and chain-link fencing, which form broad woven patterns instead of a single linked strand.

name: chain-link fence
489.description: A fence made from interwoven steel wire forming a regular diamond-shaped mesh, usually supported by metal posts and often topped with a horizontal rail or barbed wire. It is typically silver galvanized metal, though it may also be painted or vinyl-coated black, green, or other colors.
489.guidelines: Classify as chain-link fence when the defining feature is the open diamond wire mesh used as fencing or enclosure. Include close-up views of the mesh, fence lines, gates, and chain-link barriers around yards, lots, courts, cages, or industrial sites. Do not confuse with welded wire or hardware cloth, which have square or rectangular grids; barbed wire, which is only strands with barbs and no mesh; wrought-iron or picket fences, which use vertical bars or boards; or netting, which is rope or plastic rather than metal wire mesh.

name: chain mail
490.description: Protective clothing made from many small interlinked metal rings, forming a flexible mesh. It is usually silver or steel-gray and can appear as a hood, shirt, coif, glove, sleeve, or full garment worn alone or with plate armor. The key visual trait is the clearly visible ring-linked pattern across the surface.
490.guidelines: Classify as chain mail when the object itself is armor clothing constructed from linked metal rings. Include garments such as mail coifs, hauberks, shirts, mittens, and sleeves. Do not classify plain metal mesh material by itself unless it is clearly a wearable armor piece. Distinguish from plate armor, which has large solid metal plates; scale armor, which uses overlapping scales rather than linked rings; and modern fabric or knit hoods, which lack the metallic ring pattern.

name: chainsaw
491.description: A handheld power saw with a motorized chain of cutting teeth running around a guide bar. It typically has a bulky engine or motor housing, front and rear handles, and a long narrow bar projecting forward; common colors include orange, red, yellow, black, or white.
491.guidelines: Classify as a chainsaw when the image shows the distinctive toothed chain moving around a straight guide bar attached to a handheld motor unit. Include gas, electric, and battery-powered models, whether in use or at rest. Do not confuse with a regular circular saw or handsaw, which lack the chain-and-bar cutting assembly, or with a hedge trimmer/pole saw, which has reciprocating blades or a long extension shaft rather than a standard handheld chainsaw body.

name: storage chest
492.description: A storage chest is a rigid boxlike container or piece of furniture with a hinged lid that opens from the top. It is usually wider than tall and made of wood, metal, leather, or other sturdy materials. Common forms include rectangular or domed tops, reinforced corners, handles, latches, decorative panels, or carved surfaces.
492.guidelines: Classify as a storage chest when the object is a freestanding lidded container meant for storing items, especially with a top-opening hinged lid and substantial, trunk-like construction. Do not confuse it with a suitcase or briefcase, which are portable travel cases with slimmer proportions and carrying-focused design; a cabinet or cupboard, which has doors on the front; a dresser or chest of drawers, which has multiple pull-out drawers; or a small jewelry box or casket, which is much smaller and more delicate. Include both plain utility chests and ornate treasure-chest or trunk-like forms if they are top-opening storage chests.

name: commode
493.description: A commode is a freestanding storage cabinet, usually made of wood, with multiple drawers stacked vertically. It may be low and wide or tall and narrow, and some examples also include lower doors or enclosed compartments beneath or beside the drawers. Typical examples have a flat top, rectangular body, and drawer pulls or knobs, often in painted, polished, or carved finishes.
493.guidelines: Classify as commode when the furniture piece is primarily a drawer-based storage cabinet with several drawers arranged one above another, sometimes combined with a small cabinet section. Do not confuse it with a wardrobe or armoire, which is dominated by full-height doors for hanging clothes, or with a nightstand, which is smaller and usually meant to sit beside a bed. Also exclude sideboards and buffets, which are generally wider dining-room cabinets with doors and serving surfaces, and desks or vanities, which have knee space or a work surface rather than mainly stacked drawers.

name: bell
494.description: A bell: a hollow, usually metal object with a flared cup shape, suspended from above and rung by a clapper, striker, or pull rope. It is typically bronze, brass, iron, or painted metal, with a wide open rim and a loop, yoke, or frame at the top for mounting.
494.guidelines: Classify as bell when the object is a single cup-shaped ringing body with an open mouth and usually an internal or external striker. Do not confuse with a gong, which is typically a flat or slightly domed circular disk, or with tubular chimes/carillon pipes, which are long tubes rather than cup-shaped bells. Exclude generic 'chime' sets unless the image clearly centers on an individual bell.

name: china cabinet
495.description: A tall household display cabinet for dishes and glassware, typically with glass-front upper doors or sides, shelves for visible storage, and a lower section of drawers or closed cupboards. It is usually made of wood and is designed to showcase china, stemware, or decorative tableware.
495.guidelines: Classify as a china cabinet when the furniture is specifically a freestanding cabinet for displaying dishes behind glass. Common look-alikes include bookcases, curio cabinets, hutches, and built-in cupboards. Unlike a bookcase, it usually has glass doors and is intended for tableware display; unlike a curio cabinet, it is broader and more dining-room oriented; unlike a hutch, it is usually treated as a single display cabinet rather than a desk-top upper unit; unlike built-in cabinetry, it is a standalone furniture piece.

name: Christmas stocking
496.description: A decorative stocking-shaped holiday container, usually larger than a normal sock and made of fabric, felt, knit, or plush material. It typically has a wide cuff for hanging and a boot-like shape with a heel and toe, and is often red, green, white, or patterned with Christmas motifs, names, embroidery, or appliqué figures such as Santa, snowmen, or elves.
496.guidelines: Classify as Christmas stocking when the item is a stocking-shaped Christmas decoration or gift holder meant to be hung, filled, or displayed for the holiday. Include handmade, knitted, novelty, and miniature decorative versions. Do not confuse with ordinary socks, baby booties, mittens, or stockings worn as clothing. The key cue is holiday use and presentation: a hanging decorative boot-shaped pouch, often with a cuff, loop, festive colors, or Christmas imagery.

name: church
497.description: A church is a building used for Christian worship. It may be shown from the outside or as an interior space, and typically includes features such as a steeple, bell tower, cross, nave, altar, arched doors or windows, stained glass, pews, icons, or other Christian religious ornament.
497.guidelines: Classify images as church when they show a Christian worship building or its interior. Include exterior views of chapels, parish churches, and cathedral-like church buildings, as well as interior views centered on the nave, altar, sanctuary, or chapel space. Do not confuse with a mosque, which typically has minarets, domes, mihrabs, and Islamic decoration rather than crosses, altars, pews, or Christian iconography. Also avoid labeling isolated religious objects such as crucifixes, statues, altars, or doors as church unless the image clearly depicts the church building or interior space itself.

name: movie theater
498.description: A movie theater is a building or venue for showing films, typically identified by a marquee, box office, poster displays, neon or vertical signs, and an auditorium with a large projection screen and rows of seats. Exteriors often feature illuminated theater signage and showtimes, while interiors show lobby corridors or screening rooms.
498.guidelines: Classify as movie theater when the image shows a cinema facade, marquee, ticket area, theater entrance, or an interior screening auditorium with a large movie screen and theater seating. Do not confuse it with live-performance theaters or opera houses, which more often emphasize a stage with curtains and proscenium rather than a projection screen, or with generic commercial buildings that only have posters or signs. A true movie theater usually has film posters, showtime marquees, cinema signage, or a screen-based auditorium.

name: cleaver
499.description: A heavy kitchen or butcher’s knife with a broad, rectangular metal blade and a straight cutting edge, usually taller and thicker than an ordinary chef’s knife. It typically has a short handle attached to one corner of the blade, giving it a blocky, hatchet-like profile.
499.guidelines: Classify as cleaver when the tool has the distinctive wide, rectangular blade made for chopping. Do not confuse it with a chef’s knife or carving knife, which have longer, narrower, pointed blades, or with an axe/hatchet, which usually has a more wedge-shaped head and a tool-like rather than kitchen-knife form. Chinese chef’s knives can look similar, but if the object is the broad rectangular kitchen chopper form shown here, it still belongs in this category.

name: cliff dwelling
500.description: Ancient stone or adobe habitations built into shallow caves, rock alcoves, or directly beneath overhanging cliffs. They typically appear as tan to reddish masonry rooms, walls, towers, and door or window openings embedded in a natural rock face, often weathered or partially ruined.
500.guidelines: Classify as cliff dwelling when the structure is clearly a built human habitation sheltered by a cliff, cave, or rock overhang. The key cue is masonry or constructed rooms integrated into the rock recess. Do not confuse with natural caves without built walls, rock-cut tombs or temples carved into solid rock, freestanding ruins not under an overhang, or modern houses built near cliffs.

name: cloak
501.description: A loose outer garment that hangs from the shoulders and drapes over the body, typically long and flowing, often with a hood and little or no sleeve structure. It usually forms a broad, smooth silhouette and may fasten at the neck or front.
501.guidelines: Classify as cloak when the garment is a draped outer covering worn over other clothes, especially if it is long, hooded, and hangs freely from the shoulders. Do not confuse with a cape, which is usually shorter and often lacks a hood; a robe or gown, which has sleeves and a more fitted body; or a poncho/blanket wrap, which is typically a single sheet with a head opening rather than an opened front or neck fastening.

name: clog
502.description: A clog is a slip-on shoe with a rigid, often thick sole and a simple upper that leaves much of the foot uncovered or is open at the back. It may be carved from wood as a single piece, built with a wooden sole and strap, or made from leather, rubber, or foam; common forms include traditional wooden clogs, Dutch-style sabots, and modern molded clogs.
502.guidelines: Classify as clog when the footwear has the characteristic clog structure: a stiff or chunky sole, easy slip-on form, and often an open back or simplified upper. Include wooden sabots, platform wooden clogs, geta-like clog forms, and molded foam clogs such as Crocs. Do not confuse with slippers or mules, which usually have softer, flatter construction; sandals or flip-flops, which are more open and strap-based; or rain boots, which fully enclose the foot and ankle.

name: cocktail shaker
503.description: A cocktail shaker is a hand-held bar vessel used for mixing drinks, typically made of polished metal such as stainless steel, though some are glass or plastic. It usually has a tall cup-shaped body with a fitted top; many examples are two- or three-piece shakers with a cap and built-in strainer, while others are plain metal tins used with a separate mixing tin or strainer.
503.guidelines: Classify as a cocktail shaker when the object is a bar-mixing vessel with a shaker body and fitted top, often metallic and cylindrical, tapered, or slightly bulbous. Do not confuse it with a thermos or vacuum flask, which is meant for storage and usually has a screw cap but no shaker form; a cocktail mixing glass, which is open at the top and not sealed for shaking; or a martini shaker set with separate accessories, where the shaker itself is still the target object. Coffee pots, teapots, and pitchers usually have a spout and handle, while cocktail shakers typically do not, except in some novelty designs.

name: mug
504.description: A mug is a sturdy drinking vessel with a wide cylindrical or slightly tapered body, a single side handle, and relatively thick walls. It is typically deeper and heavier than a teacup, and may be made of ceramic, glass, or metal; many examples are used for coffee or other hot drinks.
504.guidelines: Classify as mug when the object is a handled, thick-walled everyday drinking cup with a broad body and substantial capacity. Include coffee mugs, novelty mugs, and glass or ceramic mugs. Do not confuse with teacups or espresso cups, which are usually smaller, lighter, and paired with saucers; tankards or beer steins, which are often larger and more specialized; or tumblers, which usually lack a handle. The key cues are the single handle, robust construction, and mug-like cup shape.

name: coffee pot
505.description: A coffee pot is a vessel associated with coffee, either for brewing or for holding and serving it. Across examples it appears in several forms: tall cylindrical metal pots, faceted stovetop moka pots with a lower chamber and small upper pot, glass drip-coffee carafes, and long-spouted metal coffee pots such as Arabic dallahs. Common cues are a handled body, a pouring spout, and a lid or top piece; many are metal, though ceramic and glass versions also occur.
505.guidelines: Classify as coffee pot when the object is clearly a pot or carafe intended for coffee brewing or serving, including moka pots, percolators, drip coffee carafes, and traditional long-spouted coffee pots. Do not confuse with a teapot: teapots are usually rounder or squat and associated with tea service rather than coffee. Do not confuse with a kettle, which is mainly for boiling water and usually lacks coffee-specific brewing structure, or with a pitcher/carafe that has no lid, spout shape, or coffee-making role. Faceted octagonal stovetop bodies suggest moka pots; glass handled vessels with coffee-machine styling suggest drip coffee pots; tall narrow metal pots with long curved spouts suggest Arabic coffee pots.

name: spiral
506.description: A spiral or spiral-like form in which a line, tube, edge, or structure winds around a central axis or center point. It may appear as a flat whorl or volute, or as a three-dimensional coil or helix such as a spring, spiral staircase, shell, or twisted sculpture.
506.guidelines: Classify images here when the defining visual feature is a clearly winding, coiling, or helically turning shape. This includes flat spirals and 3D coils/helixes. Do not confuse with simple circles, rings, loops, or concentric patterns that do not continuously wind inward or upward. Also exclude generic zigzags, waves, or corkscrew-like twists if the spiral/coiled structure is not the main recognizable form.

name: combination lock
507.description: A lock opened by entering a numeric code rather than using a key. It typically has rotating number dials, a numbered turning dial, or push-button inputs on a padlock, cable lock, safe, door lock, or built-in locking mechanism.
507.guidelines: Classify as combination lock when the defining feature is a code-entry mechanism with numbers—especially multiple rotating digit wheels or a numbered dial. Include padlock, cable, safe, and door-mounted forms if they are combination-operated. Exclude keyed locks, plain padlocks without visible code dials, electronic keypad locks that are primarily button panels, and safes or doors where the lock itself is not clearly shown as combination-based.

name: computer keyboard
508.description: A computer input device made of many labeled keys arranged in rows on a flat rectangular board or built into a laptop. It typically includes letter keys, number keys, modifier keys such as Shift/Ctrl/Alt, and often function or navigation keys. Keys are usually square or rectangular plastic caps, commonly black, gray, or white, with printed characters or symbols.
508.guidelines: Classify as computer keyboard when the image shows a keyboard for typing on a computer, whether standalone or integrated into a laptop. Include close-ups of keycaps as well as full keyboards. Do not confuse with a numeric keypad, calculator keypad, telephone keypad, piano keyboard, or remote-control buttons. The key cue is a QWERTY-style typing layout with alphabetic keys and computer-specific modifiers like Enter, Shift, Ctrl, Alt, Command, or function keys.

name: candy store
509.description: A retail shop devoted mainly to sweets, with shelves, bins, jars, or display cases filled with candies, chocolates, gummies, hard sweets, or other confectionery. Typical scenes show colorful packaged or loose treats arranged in bulk containers, glass jars, counters, and wall displays.
509.guidelines: Classify as candy store when the image shows the shop environment itself: aisles, counters, bulk candy bins, glass jars, shelving, or storefront displays centered on sweets. Do not use this class for close-up photos of candy alone, chocolate boxes, or a single dessert without visible store context. It can be confused with a bakery, dessert shop, or supermarket aisle; unlike those, a candy store is dominated by packaged or loose confectionery rather than breads, pastries, cakes, or general groceries.

name: container ship
510.description: A large cargo ship built to carry standardized shipping containers stacked in neat rectangular rows on the deck and often in the hold. It typically has a long, boxy hull, a high freeboard, and a bridge/superstructure near the stern, with multicolored containers dominating its appearance.
510.guidelines: Classify as a container ship when the vessel is primarily carrying intermodal freight containers visible as stacked box-like units. Distinguish it from bulk carriers and tankers, which have open holds or smooth decks without container stacks; from roll-on/roll-off ships and ferries, which have enclosed vehicle decks rather than exposed containers; and from general cargo or crane ships, which may carry mixed cargo or have prominent loading gear but not dense container stacks over most of the ship.

name: convertible
511.description: A passenger car with a retractable or removable roof, shown either open or closed. This category includes cabriolets, roadsters, and soft-top or hardtop convertibles in many body styles, from classic full-size cars to modern compact and sports models.
511.guidelines: Classify as convertible when the vehicle is defined by an openable roof over the passenger compartment, even if the roof is currently up. Include cabriolets and roadsters. Do not require a sports-car shape: many examples are ordinary sedans or cruisers with convertible bodies. Distinguish from coupe, sedan, and hatchback by the folding/removable roof; from sunroof/moonroof cars by the fact that only a roof panel opens on those; and from fixed-roof sports cars by the absence of a permanent full roof structure. If the image only shows the interior or partial rear/side view, look for signs of a soft top, roof storage area, or open cabin.

name: corkscrew
512.description: A hand tool for removing corks from bottles, typically built around a pointed metal spiral worm that twists into the cork. Common forms include simple T-handled corkscrews, folding pocket corkscrews, waiter’s friends, winged lever types, and multi-tools that combine the spiral with a bottle opener, foil cutter, or small knife.
512.guidelines: Classify as corkscrew when the defining feature is a metal spiral worm used to extract a cork. It may appear alone or as part of a wine opener multi-tool. Do not confuse with a bottle opener, which lifts crown caps but lacks the corkscrew spiral, or with a Swiss Army knife / multitool where the spiral is only a secondary attachment and the object is not primarily a corkscrew. Also exclude augers, drill bits, and hooks that have a spiral shape but are not bottle-opening tools.

name: trumpet
513.description: A trumpet is a brass instrument with a long, mostly straight cylindrical tube that ends in a flared bell and is played through a cup-shaped mouthpiece. It typically has three piston valves on top, a compact hand-held form, and a bright metallic finish, often brass, silver, or lacquered gold.
513.guidelines: Classify as trumpet when the instrument has a straight, narrow body, a forward-facing flared bell, and three piston valves. Do not confuse it with a cornet, which is shorter and more compact with more conical tubing; a flugelhorn, which has a wider conical body and larger mellower bell; or larger brass instruments such as euphonium, baritone horn, trombone, or tuba, which have much more tubing or a slide instead of valves. Exclude bugles if there are no valves.

name: cowboy boot
514.description: A tall leather boot with a high shaft, angled heel, and a pointed to rounded toe. Typical examples show decorative stitching or inlays on the shaft, pull straps or pull holes near the top, and a firm structured shape associated with Western-style boots.
514.guidelines: Classify as cowboy boot when the footwear has the classic Western boot silhouette: mid-calf to knee-high shaft, slanted Cuban-style heel, and a pointed or slightly rounded toe, often with embroidered or stitched decoration. Do not confuse with riding boots or fashion knee boots, which usually have straighter heels, simpler shafts, and often zippers; or with work boots and Wellington boots, which are bulkier, plainer, and lack the distinctive angled heel and Western styling.

name: cowboy hat
515.description: A cowboy hat is a Western-style hat with a broad, usually upturned brim and a tall, creased crown. It is commonly made of felt or straw and often has a hatband or decorative trim around the base of the crown.
515.guidelines: Classify as cowboy hat when the hat has the characteristic high crown and wide brim associated with Western wear. Include both felt and straw versions, including white or tan ranch-style hats and decorative fashion variants. Do not confuse with a fedora or trilby, which have narrower brims and a pinched front; a sombrero, which usually has a much wider circular brim and different crown shape; or an outback hat, which typically has a flatter crown and a more utilitarian look.

name: bassinet
516.description: A small infant bed for newborns, usually an oval or rectangular basket-like sleeping space with high padded sides, often mounted on a light stand or wheeled frame. It may have a hood, skirt, canopy, or soft fabric lining, and is sized for a very young baby.
516.guidelines: Classify as bassinet when the image shows a compact baby bed meant for newborns, typically smaller and more enclosed than a crib. Common look-alikes are cribs, cradles, and playpens. Cribs are larger with rigid slatted sides and room for older infants; playpens have mesh sides and a boxier portable structure. A cradle specifically emphasizes a rocking frame, while many examples here are stationary or wheeled bassinets. Use bassinet for the small, basket-like infant sleeper even if it has a canopy or stand.

name: crane
517.description: A crane is a large lifting machine with a tall vertical support or tower and a long boom or horizontal jib, usually built from open metal trusswork. It is used to raise, lower, and move heavy loads with cables, hooks, or hoists, and is commonly seen on construction sites, in ports, and in industrial yards.
517.guidelines: Classify images as crane when the main object is a heavy lifting machine with a boom or jib for suspending and moving loads. This category includes tower cranes, harbor cranes, and other industrial lifting cranes. Do not confuse it with excavators, cherry pickers, derricks, drilling rigs, or utility poles: cranes are defined by a lifting boom/jib and suspended hoist or hook rather than a digging bucket, work platform, or drilling apparatus.

name: motorcycle helmet
518.description: A protective riding helmet with a hard rounded shell, padded interior, and chin strap, made to cover the head for motorcycling. It appears in full-face, open-face, modular, and half-helmet styles, often with a clear or tinted visor, chin bar, smooth glossy finish, and painted graphics or stripes.
518.guidelines: Classify as motorcycle helmet when the helmet has a sturdy enclosed shell and motorcycle-style features such as a face shield, chin bar, ear coverage, or modular/open-face scooter design. Do not confuse it with a bicycle helmet, which is lighter and heavily vented; a hard hat, which has a brim and no chin-focused protection; or sports helmets such as football or hockey helmets, which have different cage/pad structures.

name: crate
519.description: A crate is a rigid storage or transport container, usually box-shaped with straight sides and an open top or a removable lid. In these images it is most often made of wood slats or planks, but may also be plastic or metal. Crates are typically sturdy, stackable, and built for carrying produce, bottles, tools, or other goods; many have hand holes, slatted sides, printed labels, or worn industrial surfaces.
519.guidelines: Classify as crate when the object is a rigid container meant for storage or shipping, especially wooden slatted produce crates or similar stackable boxes. Do not confuse with cardboard cartons or corrugated boxes, which have folded paperboard walls and should be labeled as carton. Exclude animal cages or pet crates with bars, wire mesh, or doors designed to confine animals. Also distinguish from pallets, which are flat load platforms without enclosing side walls, and from drawers, cabinets, or bins that are fixed parts of furniture rather than standalone transport containers.

name: crib
520.description: A crib is a larger, stationary bed for infants and toddlers, typically made of wood or metal and enclosed by high protective slats or bars on all sides. It usually has a rectangular shape, a raised mattress, and may include features such as a canopy, mobile, or decorative bedding.
520.guidelines: Classify as a crib when the image shows a stationary infant bed with tall slatted sides designed to keep a baby safely enclosed. Do not confuse it with a bassinet or cradle, which are smaller and often have solid woven sides or rocking supports; a playpen, which usually has mesh or fabric walls; or a toddler bed, which sits lower and is more open for independent access.

name: slow cooker
521.description: A slow cooker is a countertop electric cooking appliance with a round or oval outer housing, a removable deep ceramic or metal crock, and a fitted lid, often glass. It is typically pot-shaped, with side handles and simple heat controls or a digital front panel, and is used to cook food slowly over several hours.
521.guidelines: Classify as slow cooker when the image shows the full countertop appliance with an outer heated base and lidded crock insert. Common look-alikes include pressure cookers, rice cookers, stockpots, Dutch ovens, and buffet chafers. Unlike pressure cookers and Instant Pot-style multicookers, slow cookers usually have a simple non-locking lid and no pressure-sealing mechanism. Unlike rice cookers, they are typically deeper, more crock-like, and often oval. Do not label images that show only food in a generic pot unless the slow-cooker base or characteristic crock appliance is visible.

name: croquet ball
522.description: A croquet ball is a hard, smooth ball used in croquet, typically about the size of a grapefruit and shown in solid bright colors such as red, blue, yellow, black, or green. It is usually spherical with a plain or lightly striped painted surface and appears with croquet mallets, wickets, and lawn grass.
522.guidelines: Classify as croquet ball when the image centers on the colored ball used in the lawn game croquet, often near mallets and wire wickets. Do not confuse it with bocce or lawn bowls balls, which are usually larger and associated with bowling-style play, or with billiard balls, which are smaller and seen on tables. Exclude general toy balls or baseballs; croquet balls are hard, relatively large, and specifically tied to croquet equipment and grassy playing lawns.

name: crutch
523.description: A crutch is a mobility aid used under the arm or against the forearm to support walking. It typically has one or two long shafts made of metal or wood, a handgrip partway down, and a top support such as an underarm pad, forearm cuff, or platform. Most examples appear as a matched pair, often with rubber tips at the bottom and adjustable holes or telescoping sections.
523.guidelines: Classify as crutch when the object is a walking aid designed to transfer body weight through the arms, usually with a handgrip and an upper support or cuff. Include underarm crutches, forearm crutches, platform crutches, and decorative or customized crutches. Do not confuse with a cane or walking stick, which is usually a single straight support without an upper arm support; a walker, which is a larger freestanding frame; or trekking/ski poles, which are sport equipment rather than medical mobility aids.

name: cuirass
524.description: A rigid torso armor piece made of solid plates, typically metal or hardened leather, that covers the chest and often the back. It appears as a shaped breast-and-torso shell, sometimes as a front plate only and sometimes as front-and-back plates joined at the shoulders or sides; surfaces may be plain, embossed, muscled, or fitted with straps and pauldrons.
524.guidelines: Annotate this category when the main object is a rigid plate armor component for the torso: a breastplate alone or a matched front-and-back torso defense. Do not confuse it with chain mail or scale armor, which are flexible and made of many small linked pieces, or with a full suit of armor when the whole armored figure is the focus. If only the rigid chest/body plate is the salient item, it is a cuirass.

name: dam
525.description: A dam is a large man-made barrier built across a river or valley to hold back, control, or redirect water. It typically appears as a broad concrete, earth, or masonry wall spanning from one bank to the other, often with a reservoir on the upstream side and spillways, gates, or outlets where water flows over or through the structure.
525.guidelines: Classify as dam when the main subject is a substantial barrier impounding or regulating a body of water across a channel or valley. Common appearances include tall concrete walls, sloped embankments, gated spillways, and hydroelectric intake towers. Do not confuse with a dike or levee, which is usually a long embankment running alongside water rather than blocking it; a weir, which is typically a lower overflow barrier; a bridge, which carries traffic over water; or a lock, which is a navigational chamber rather than the main retaining wall.

name: desk
526.description: A desk is a piece of furniture with a flat horizontal work surface, usually sized for one person and often paired with a chair. It may be rectangular, L-shaped, or built into a cubicle or workstation, and can include drawers, shelves, or a keyboard tray. Desks are commonly made of wood, metal, laminate, or glass and are often shown with computers, monitors, keyboards, papers, or office supplies on top.
526.guidelines: Classify as desk when the main object is a work table intended for writing, studying, or computer use. Include office desks, student desks, home computer desks, cubicle desks, and similar workstation furniture. Do not confuse with a dining table or coffee table, which are usually more open and not designed as personal workstations; a counter or reception desk, which is larger and built for service; or a nightstand or side table, which is smaller and not meant for seated work. The key cue is a personal work surface with legroom and a setup suited for office or study tasks.

name: desktop computer
527.description: A desktop computer is a stationary personal computer setup typically consisting of a separate system unit (tower or small-form-factor case), or a monitor/CRT screen paired with a keyboard and often a mouse. It is usually arranged on or under a desk, with visible cables and separate components rather than a single portable device.
527.guidelines: Classify as desktop computer when the image shows a non-portable computer setup with a desktop PC tower, or a monitor/CRT clearly used with a keyboard and/or mouse as part of a desktop workstation. Include older CRT-based setups and modern flat-panel desktop arrangements. Do not confuse with laptops, which have screen and keyboard hinged together in one portable unit; with standalone monitors or TVs shown without clear computer context; or with servers, which are rackmounted or industrial and not typical personal desktop workstations. Exclude all-in-one computers unless the category explicitly includes them.

name: rotary telephone
528.description: A telephone with a handset and a circular rotary dial on the base or body, with numbered finger holes used to place calls by rotating the dial. Common forms include desk sets, wall phones, and antique candlestick styles, typically with a wired handset and a bulky plastic or metal housing.
528.guidelines: Classify as rotary telephone when the device is a telephone specifically using a round rotary dial rather than push buttons or a touchscreen. It may be vintage, toy-like, wall-mounted, or decorative, but the defining cue is the circular finger-wheel dial. Do not confuse with push-button landline phones, payphones, mobile phones, intercom handsets, or telephone parts shown without a full recognizable rotary phone.

name: diaper
529.description: An absorbent undergarment for infants or incontinent wearers, typically worn around the waist and between the legs. It is usually made of soft white or pastel padded material, often disposable with a thick crotch, elastic leg openings, and adhesive tabs, though reusable cloth versions also appear.
529.guidelines: Classify as diaper when the image shows the absorbent garment itself or a person/animal clearly wearing it. Common variants include disposable diapers and cloth diapers. Do not confuse with sanitary napkins or pads, which are smaller flat menstrual products and are not worn like underwear; bibs, which cover the chest; or training pants/underwear, which look more like regular briefs and are less bulky. The key cues are the bulky absorbent center, wraparound waist, and leg openings designed for babies or similar wearers.

name: digital clock
530.description: A clock or clock display that shows time as numerals rather than with analog hands, typically using LED, LCD, VFD, or segmented digits. It may appear as a standalone alarm clock, wall clock, appliance display, watch display, or built-in electronic time readout.
530.guidelines: Classify as digital clock when the main subject is a time display shown numerically. Include bedside alarm clocks, wall-mounted electronic clocks, watch or appliance clock readouts, and similar displays. Do not confuse with analog clocks, which use hands on a dial, or with other numeric displays such as timers, calculators, scoreboards, thermometers, radios, or microwaves when the display is not primarily showing the current time. The key cue is a recognizable clock time presented in digits, often with a colon and sometimes AM/PM or alarm indicators.

name: digital watch
531.description: A wristwatch that shows the time with numerals on an electronic display rather than with hands. Typical examples have an LCD or LED screen, often in a square, rectangular, or rounded case, with plastic, rubber, or metal straps and additional buttons for functions such as date, alarm, stopwatch, or backlight.
531.guidelines: Classify as a digital watch when the watch face is primarily a numeric electronic display worn on the wrist. Include both simple and rugged sports styles, calculator watches, and models with extra digital functions. Do not confuse with analog watches, which use hour and minute hands, or analog-digital watches, which combine hands with a digital subdisplay; those are not purely digital watches.

name: dining table
532.description: A table intended for eating meals, typically with a broad flat top and enough surface area to seat several people. It is usually made of wood, metal, glass, or similar furniture materials, and commonly appears with matching dining chairs around it. Shapes are often rectangular, but can also be round or square.
532.guidelines: Classify as a dining table when the main object is a table clearly meant for dining or meal seating, usually full-sized and paired with multiple chairs. Do not confuse it with a coffee table or side table, which are much lower and smaller, a desk, which is intended for work and often has drawers, or a kitchen island/counter, which is built-in rather than movable furniture. Ignore dishes, glasses, or other items placed on top if the furniture itself is the main subject.

name: dishcloth
533.description: A small reusable cloth, usually square or nearly square, made from knitted or crocheted yarn. It is typically thick, soft, and textured, with visible stitches, ridges, waffle, striped, geometric, or simple patterned surfaces; most examples are flat quadrilateral pads in cotton or similar yarn.
533.guidelines: Classify as dishcloth when the image shows a small handmade knitted or crocheted cleaning cloth or scrubber, usually a flat square used for washing dishes or wiping surfaces. Do not confuse it with larger blankets, afghans, towels, scarves, potholders, or garments: dishcloths are typically compact, single-layer, and plainly functional rather than wearable. Potholders may look similar but are often thicker, insulated, quilted, or explicitly shown for handling hot cookware. Washcloths can look nearly identical, so if no clear bathroom context is present, a generic dishcloth-style cleaning cloth is appropriate here.

name: dishwasher
534.description: A dishwasher is a household or commercial appliance for washing dishes, glassware, and utensils. It is typically a boxy front-opening machine installed under a countertop or used as a freestanding unit, with a hinged drop-down door, pull-out wire racks, and a control panel on the front edge or face. Interiors are metallic or plastic with spray arms, detergent compartments, and dish baskets.
534.guidelines: Classify as dishwasher when the image shows the appliance itself, either closed, open, built-in, freestanding, or showing its rack-filled interior. Common look-alikes include ovens, washing machines, clothes dryers, refrigerators, and dish racks. Unlike an oven, a dishwasher has sliding dish racks and a wash tub rather than cooking trays or heating elements. Unlike a washing machine or dryer, it is shorter, cabinet-like, front-loading with dish baskets instead of a drum. Do not confuse it with a countertop dish rack or drying cabinet; the key cue is an enclosed washing appliance designed for dishes.

name: disc brake
535.description: A disc brake is a wheel braking system built around a flat circular metal rotor attached to the wheel hub and a caliper that clamps brake pads onto both sides of the rotor. The rotor is usually steel and often drilled, slotted, or cut into a wavy outline; the caliper is a compact housing mounted near the rim or hub, connected by a hydraulic line or cable. In images, it typically appears as a prominent circular brake disc with a small clamp-like unit beside it on a bicycle, motorcycle, scooter, or car wheel.
535.guidelines: Classify images as disc brake when the defining feature is a visible circular brake rotor with a caliper pressing on it. Include bicycle, motorcycle, scooter, and automotive examples. Do not confuse with drum brakes, which have an enclosed cylindrical hub and no exposed rotor, or with wheel rims/hubs that may be circular but lack a caliper and braking surface. Also exclude brake discs shown alone only if they are not clearly identifiable as part of a disc brake assembly; the key cue is the rotor-and-caliper braking mechanism.

name: dock
536.description: A dock is a waterside structure or designated berthing area where boats and ships are moored, loaded, unloaded, or serviced. It typically appears as a pier, quay, marina berth, or dry-dock edge alongside the water, often with vessels tied up next to it and sometimes with railings, posts, gangways, cranes, or other harbor equipment.
536.guidelines: Classify as dock when the image centers on the boat-berthing structure or harbor-side mooring area rather than on a specific vessel. Common look-alikes include pier, wharf, marina, and harbor: use dock when the emphasis is the place where boats are stationed or serviced. Do not confuse it with a ship or boat itself, or with a boathouse/warehouse; the key cue is a built waterfront edge or platform used for mooring and access.

name: dogsled
537.description: A dogsled is a narrow, lightweight sled used for travel over snow, typically with long runners, a low platform or basket, and handles at the rear for the musher. In images it often appears attached by lines to a team of harnessed sled dogs pulling it across snow or ice.
537.guidelines: Classify as dogsled when the central object is the sled used in dog mushing, usually seen on snow with runners and towing lines connected to dogs. Do not confuse it with a generic sled, toboggan, or sleigh pulled by people, horses, or vehicles. The key cue is a snow-going sled specifically designed to be pulled by a dog team.

name: dome
538.description: A dome is a rounded architectural roof or ceiling, typically hemispherical, bulbous, or smoothly curved in profile. It appears as a circular or polygonal structure rising upward from a drum or base, and may be built of masonry, metal, glass, or patterned latticework. Domes are often seen both from the exterior as roof forms and from the interior as coffered, painted, or skylit vaulted ceilings, including domes carried on pendentives.
538.guidelines: Classify as dome when the defining feature is a prominent rounded roof or ceiling structure spanning a circular or polygonal space. Include exterior cupolas and large building domes, as well as interior views showing the curved vaulted ceiling. Do not confuse with arches or barrel vaults, which extend lengthwise rather than forming a centralized round cap; spires or towers, which taper vertically; or generic round roofs that are flat or conical rather than smoothly domed.

name: doormat
539.description: A small flat mat placed at a doorway or entry, usually rectangular or shaped, made of coir, rubber, fabric, or similar durable material. It lies on the floor just inside or outside a door and often has a textured surface, decorative pattern, logo, or printed words such as “Welcome.”
539.guidelines: Classify as doormat when the image shows a floor mat specifically positioned at an entrance or threshold. Include plain, decorative, novelty, indoor, and outdoor entry mats. Do not confuse with larger area rugs or carpets, which cover more floor space and are not entry-specific; bath mats, which are usually found in bathrooms; or stair treads and floor runners, which are longer and not meant as door-threshold mats.

name: offshore oil platform
540.description: A large industrial structure standing in open water on tall legs, columns, or a floating base, with a broad working deck carrying a drilling derrick, cranes, pipes, machinery, and often a helipad or flare boom. Many examples are jack-up rigs or production platforms with multiple lattice legs rising high above the sea.
540.guidelines: Classify as offshore oil platform when the image shows a sea-based drilling or oil-production structure fixed, elevated, or floating offshore. Key cues are the raised platform deck, drilling tower or production equipment, heavy support legs/columns, and open-water setting. Do not confuse with ships or barges, which have a conventional hull and bow/stern profile, or with ordinary harbor cranes and piers, which lack the self-contained drilling platform structure. Also distinguish from wind turbines and lighthouses, which are much simpler single-tower structures without a broad industrial deck.

name: drum
541.description: A percussion instrument with a hollow resonating body—usually round and often cylindrical or barrel-shaped—and a stretched membrane (drumhead) over one or both ends. It is typically played by striking the head with sticks, mallets, hands, or beaters.
541.guidelines: Classify as drum when the main object is a membranophone with a taut skin or synthetic head over a hollow shell. This includes hand drums, marching drums, bass drums, snare drums, toms, and similar forms. Do not confuse with timpani/kettledrums, which have a distinctive bowl-shaped metal body, or tambourines/frame drums, which are much shallower and often have jingles. Exclude non-membrane percussion such as cymbals, xylophones, and bells.

name: drumstick
542.description: A drumstick is a slender stick used to play percussion instruments, usually made of wood and sometimes other materials. It is typically straight or slightly tapered, with one playing end shaped into a rounded, oval, teardrop, barrel, acorn, or pointed tip; some pairs may differ in finish, thickness, or have coated grips or specialty heads.
542.guidelines: Classify as drumstick when the image shows one or more handheld percussion sticks intended for drums or cymbals—usually sold or used in matched pairs, long, narrow, and tapered with a shaped striking tip. Do not confuse with a baton or conducting stick, which is much thinner and lighter with a handle; a mallet, which usually has a distinct soft or large head; a baseball bat or club, which is much thicker and heavier; or chopsticks and dowels, which lack the characteristic taper, matched-pair presentation, and branded drumstick form.

name: dumbbell
543.description: A dumbbell is a hand weight with a short central handle and a weighted mass at each end. It may be a single solid piece or an adjustable design with round or polygonal plates attached to a short bar. Common materials include metal, rubber-coated metal, or vinyl, and dumbbells are usually shown singly or in pairs.
543.guidelines: Classify as dumbbell when the object is a one-handed free weight with a short handle and two weighted ends. Include fixed and adjustable dumbbells. Do not confuse with a barbell, which has a much longer bar intended for two-handed lifting, or with weight plates shown alone without the short handle. Also exclude kettlebells, which have a loop handle, and gym machines or benches that may appear alongside dumbbells.

name: Dutch oven
544.description: A Dutch oven is a thick-walled, heavy cooking pot with a tight-fitting lid, typically round and deep. It is usually made of cast iron, sometimes enamel-coated, and is designed for stovetop, oven, and often campfire cooking. Common examples show short side handles, a domed or flat lid, and a broad, sturdy body suited to slow cooking, braising, baking, and stewing.
544.guidelines: Classify as a Dutch oven when the image shows a heavy, lidded pot with thick walls and a robust cast-metal construction, often cast iron or enameled cast iron. It may appear indoors on a stove or in an oven, or outdoors with coals placed underneath and sometimes on top of the lid. Do not confuse it with a stockpot or saucepan, which usually have thinner walls and lighter construction, or with a slow cooker/crock pot, which is an electric countertop appliance. Also distinguish it from a casserole dish by the pot’s notably heavy build, fitted lid, and traditional cast-iron form.

name: electric fan
545.description: An electrically powered air-moving device with several rotating blades attached to a central hub and driven by a motor, usually behind a protective grille or inside a square, round, or cylindrical housing. It may appear as a desk fan, box fan, vehicle radiator fan, or computer cooling fan, but the defining visual element is the motorized bladed rotor designed to circulate air.
545.guidelines: Classify as electric fan when the object is a powered fan with visible blades or an enclosed bladed rotor for moving air. Include household fans, cooling fans, exhaust fans, and radiator/computer fans. Do not confuse with non-electric hand fans, airplane propellers, wind turbines, ventilation ducts without a visible fan unit, or leaf blowers/air blowers that are tool-shaped rather than bladed fan assemblies. The key cue is a motor-driven multi-blade rotor used for airflow.

name: electric guitar
546.description: A guitar with a solid or semi-hollow body and electromagnetic pickups, typically with 6 strings and sometimes up to 8. It usually has a narrow neck, metal strings, control knobs, a bridge/tailpiece, and is often seen connected to an amplifier. Bodies vary widely in shape and color, but the defining feature is the electric-guitar construction rather than an acoustic soundbox.
546.guidelines: Classify as electric guitar when the instrument is clearly a guitar built around magnetic pickups, usually with 6–8 strings. Include solid-body and semi-hollow electric guitars. Do not include bass guitars: they usually have a longer neck and commonly 4 or 5 thick strings, though some have 6. Do not include acoustic guitars or acoustic-electric guitars whose main body is a full acoustic soundbox with a round sound hole, even if they can be plugged in. To distinguish from bass guitar, check string count, neck length, and the heavier, wider strings on a bass.

name: entertainment center
548.description: A large furniture unit or integrated media setup designed to hold a television or projection screen together with audio/video equipment. It typically has a central space for the screen, with shelves, cabinets, drawers, or side compartments for speakers, receivers, CD or tape players, and other electronics; common materials are wood, laminate, metal, or glass.
548.guidelines: Classify as entertainment center when the image shows a dedicated media cabinet, wall unit, or stand organized around a TV or projection screen and related stereo/home-theater components. Include both full wall units and smaller TV stands if they clearly function as a unified media center. Do not confuse with a plain television, a single speaker, a bookshelf, desk, fireplace mantel, or generic living-room furniture; the key cue is furniture or built-in structure specifically arranged to house the display plus entertainment equipment.

name: envelope
549.description: A flat paper or card container for holding letters, cards, or documents, usually rectangular or square with a folded flap that closes one open side. It may be plain or decorative, and can be sealed, tucked closed, or left open.
549.guidelines: Classify as envelope when the main object is a mailer or paper sleeve with a closing flap designed to contain a letter, card, or document. Include standard mailing envelopes, invitation envelopes, and decorative stationery envelopes. Do not confuse with folded greeting cards or postcards, which lack a containing pocket; paper bags or pouches, which are deeper and more bag-like; or document folders and wallets, which are typically larger, thicker, or made for repeated storage rather than single-piece mailing.

name: espresso machine
550.description: An espresso machine is a powered countertop coffee appliance that brews coffee under pressure. It typically has a boxy metal or plastic body, a brew head or spout over a cup area, control buttons or knobs, and often a drip tray, steam wand, portafilter, or built-in bean/water containers. Designs range from compact home units to larger commercial machines, but all are dedicated machines for making espresso-style coffee rather than simple manual brewers.
550.guidelines: Classify as this category when the image shows an electric espresso-making appliance, including pump-driven home machines and superautomatic bean-to-cup models. Do not include manual stovetop moka pots, French presses, pour-over devices, percolators, or drip coffee makers. The key cue is a machine body with brewing hardware and cup placement area, often with a steam wand, portafilter, or integrated dispensing spout for espresso.

name: face powder
551.description: A cosmetic powder for the face, usually beige, ivory, pink, or translucent, sold in round jars or hinged compacts. It appears as pressed powder in a flat cake or pan, or as loose powder in a container, often with a puff, sponge, sifter, or mirror.
551.guidelines: Classify as face powder when the product is clearly a facial powder in a jar or compact, including pressed and loose powder formats. Do not confuse it with blush or bronzer, which are usually more strongly pink, peach, or brown and marketed for adding color; eye shadow, which comes in much smaller pans; or cream/liquid foundation, which is not powder. If the item is a makeup compact containing facial powder and applicator puff or sponge, it belongs here.

name: feather boa
552.description: A long, fluffy fashion accessory made of soft feathers, worn draped around the neck or shoulders. It appears as a thick, airy strand or garland with a feathery texture, often in bright solid colors such as pink, red, white, black, or purple, and sometimes multicolored.
552.guidelines: Classify as feather boa when the item is a decorative wearable strand of feathers wrapped around the neck, shoulders, or costume. Do not confuse it with a fur scarf, knitted scarf, lei, or feather trim on clothing. The key cues are loose plume-like feathers forming a long boa shape rather than a flat fabric strip or a garment covered in feathers.

name: filing cabinet
553.description: A filing cabinet is a freestanding storage cabinet with multiple stacked drawers, usually tall and rectangular, made of metal or wood. The drawers are broad and deep enough to hold paper files, and typically have pull handles, label holders, and sometimes locks. Common forms include vertical cabinets with narrow full-width drawers and lateral cabinets with wider side-by-side filing drawers.
553.guidelines: Classify as filing cabinet when the object is a cabinet specifically designed for storing documents in pull-out filing drawers. Look for several large, file-sized drawers with handles and label slots, often in office settings. Do not confuse with dressers or chests of drawers, which are usually bedroom furniture with more decorative styling and shallower clothing drawers; tool cabinets, which often have many smaller drawers or workshop context; card catalogs or apothecary cabinets, which have numerous small compartments; or lockers and cupboards, which use doors rather than filing drawers.

name: fireboat
554.description: A fireboat is a specialized vessel equipped with powerful water cannons for fighting fires on ships, waterfront structures, and in harbors or coastal waters. It is typically a compact to medium-sized workboat, often painted red or high-visibility colors, with a sturdy hull, wheelhouse, and one or more deck-mounted monitors that spray large arcing jets of water.
554.guidelines: Classify as fireboat when the vessel is clearly equipped for firefighting, especially with prominent water cannons or active high-volume spray displays. Do not confuse with tugboats, pilot boats, or patrol boats, which may have similar hulls but lack dedicated firefighting monitors and dramatic water jets. If the boat is mainly towing another vessel, prefer tugboat unless firefighting equipment is the defining feature.

name: fire engine
555.description: A large emergency response vehicle used by firefighters, typically painted red or another high-visibility color and fitted with a truck body carrying hoses, pumps, ladders, compartments, warning lights, and other firefighting equipment. Examples include both modern and older fire service vehicles, from pumpers to ladder trucks, but all are recognizable as firefighting apparatus.
555.guidelines: Classify as fire engine when the image shows a fire service vehicle clearly equipped for firefighting or rescue use, usually with hoses, ladders, pump panels, side compartments, or emergency fire department markings. Do not confuse with ambulances, police vehicles, utility trucks, buses, or generic red trucks. If it is specifically a firefighting vehicle—even an antique, airport crash tender, ladder truck, or rescue pumper—it belongs here.

name: fireplace screen
556.description: A fireplace screen is a freestanding or fitted protective barrier placed in front of a fireplace opening. It is usually made of metal mesh, wrought iron, brass, glass, or decorative panels, and may be flat, curved, folding, or framed with feet or side supports. Many examples are ornamental, with scrollwork, embossed metal, or patterned grilles, but the defining feature is that it covers the front of the hearth to block sparks while allowing the fire to be seen.
556.guidelines: Classify as a fireplace screen when the object is a screen or guard specifically meant to stand in front of a fireplace or hearth opening. Common look-alikes include fireplace doors, which are hinged doors permanently mounted to the fireplace surround; andirons, which sit inside the fire to support logs; and baby gates or room dividers, which are not hearth-specific. Screens may be mesh, glass-backed, folding, curved, or highly decorative, but they should function visually as a protective front barrier for a fireplace.

name: flagpole
557.description: A tall, slender vertical pole or mast designed to display a flag, usually made of metal and topped with a finial or pulley. It appears as a simple upright shaft rising from the ground or a building, often with one or more flags attached near the top.
557.guidelines: Classify this as a flagpole when the main object is the pole or mast that supports a flag. Include freestanding poles and poles mounted on buildings. Do not confuse it with the flag itself, a signpost, light pole, utility pole, radio mast, or antenna. The key cue is a plain vertical support specifically used for flying a flag, typically with a flag, halyard, or attachment hardware near the top.

name: transverse flute
558.description: A flute held horizontally to the side of the player, consisting of a long narrow tube with a blow hole near one end and a line of finger holes or metal keywork along the body. It may be silver-colored metal, bamboo, wood, or other materials, but it lacks the beaked mouthpiece of a recorder.
558.guidelines: Classify as transverse flute when the instrument is played sideways across the mouth and has a side-blown embouchure hole. Include concert flutes and side-blown folk flutes made of wood or bamboo. Do not confuse with recorder or tin whistle, which are end-blown and have a distinct mouthpiece; clarinet or oboe, which are also end-blown and usually have reeds; or panpipes, which are sets of multiple tubes rather than one long side-blown tube.

name: folding chair
559.description: A chair designed to fold flat for storage, usually with a hinged frame and a seat and backrest made of metal, wood, plastic, or fabric. Most examples have simple tubular or bar-like legs that pivot inward, and many are lightweight portable chairs used indoors, outdoors, or for events.
559.guidelines: Classify as a folding chair when the chair’s structure is clearly made to collapse via hinges or pivoting legs into a flatter form. Includes metal, wood, plastic, padded, and fabric sling versions as long as they are true fold-up chairs. Do not confuse with stackable banquet or conference chairs, which have fixed rigid frames and do not fold; deck chairs or recliners, which may adjust angle but are a different chair type unless they clearly fold as portable event-style seating; or stools and director’s chairs, which have different shapes and support structures.

name: American football helmet
560.description: A hard-shell protective helmet worn for American football, typically rounded and close-fitting with ear coverage, a front face mask or cage, chin-strap attachments, and team colors, stripes, numbers, or logos. It is bulkier and more enclosed than many other sports helmets.
560.guidelines: Classify as an American football helmet when the helmet has a rigid shell plus a prominent front face mask and the overall design used in gridiron football. Do not confuse it with motorcycle or auto-racing helmets, which usually have a full visor and no open football-style cage; baseball or hockey helmets, which have different face protection and shell shapes; or rugby scrum caps, which are soft and lack a hard shell and face mask.

name: forklift
561.description: A compact industrial lift truck used to raise and move materials, characterized by a vertical mast and a pair of metal forks projecting from the front that slide under pallets or other loads. Most examples have an operator seat or standing compartment, small to medium wheels, and a counterweighted rear; colors and exact body style vary across warehouse, outdoor, and rough-terrain models.
561.guidelines: Classify as a forklift when the vehicle’s main load-handling feature is a front-mounted fork carriage on a vertical mast for lifting pallets or similar loads. Include common variants such as counterbalance forklifts, reach trucks, and rough-terrain forklifts. Do not confuse with telehandlers, which have a long extending boom; pallet jacks, which are much smaller walk-behind or ride-on devices without a tall mast; front loaders or tractors, which use buckets instead of forks as the primary design; or cranes, which lift by cable or hook rather than front forks.

name: fountain
562.description: A fountain is a built water feature consisting of the whole structure—such as a basin, pool, pedestal, sculpture, or paved installation—together with one or more jets, sprays, sheets, or cascades of water. It may be ornamental or architectural, from small garden basins to large plaza displays, and often includes symmetrical tiers, central nozzles, or decorative figures. Colored lighting can appear, but the defining feature is an integrated man-made structure that visibly emits or circulates water.
562.guidelines: Classify as fountain when the image shows a complete man-made water feature, not just a close-up of water alone. Include tiered fountains, plaza fountains, pond spray fountains, and sculptural fountains if the built installation is the subject.
