Do not confuse with waterfalls or rapids, which are natural and lack a constructed fountain structure; with geysers, which are natural vertical eruptions; or with sprinklers, which are simple irrigation devices rather than architectural water features. If multiple fountains are present, treat each separate structure as its own fountain; distinct fountains should be separated by land rather than being parts of one continuous installation.

name: fountain pen
563.description: A writing pen with a rigid barrel and a distinctive split metal nib that tapers to a pointed tip, usually gold- or steel-colored. It often has a removable cap and may be shown writing with liquid ink on paper, with the nib and feed clearly visible.
563.guidelines: Classify as a fountain pen when the pen has an exposed metal nib with a central slit and pointed tip designed to deliver liquid ink. Do not confuse with ballpoint, rollerball, or gel pens, which have a small ball tip instead of a nib, or dip pens, which use a bare nib mounted in a simple holder rather than a self-contained pen body and ink reservoir.

name: four-poster bed
564.description: A bed with a tall post at each of the four corners, often connected by an upper rectangular frame. The structure is usually wood or metal and may be plain or ornate, with turned posts, carved details, curtains, or fabric drapery hanging from the top.
564.guidelines: Classify as a four-poster bed when the bed itself has four prominent corner posts rising well above the mattress, often with a tester or canopy frame joining them. Do not confuse it with a canopy bed if the emphasis is on fabric canopy alone without clearly visible four structural posts; in practice many examples overlap, but the key cue here is the four tall corner posts as part of the bed frame. Exclude ordinary beds with just a headboard and footboard, beds with only two tall posts, or mosquito-net setups suspended from the ceiling rather than supported by four bedposts.

name: freight car
565.description: A railroad car used to carry cargo rather than passengers. It is a large rail vehicle riding on steel wheels, typically boxy or elongated, made of metal, and coupled into freight trains. The class includes multiple cargo-car subtypes such as boxcars, covered hoppers, tank cars, gondolas, and other goods wagons.
565.guidelines: Classify as freight car when the image shows a rail-based cargo wagon or a clear portion of one. Include different freight-car designs and loads, as long as the vehicle is a railroad car for carrying goods. Do not confuse with passenger railcars, locomotives, cabooses, trams, or road vehicles such as trucks and automobiles. Distinguish by railroad wheels on tracks, freight-train coupling, and cargo-oriented bodies such as enclosed boxy sides, cylindrical tanks, open tops, or hopper shapes.

name: French horn
566.description: A brass musical instrument with a long tube wrapped into a compact circular coil, a flared bell, and usually three or four rotary valves operated by the left hand. It is typically made of polished brass or similar metal and has a rounded, looped appearance distinct from straighter brass instruments.
566.guidelines: Classify as French horn when the instrument has tightly coiled circular tubing, rotary valves, and a wide rear-facing or side-facing bell. Do not confuse it with a trumpet or cornet, which are much straighter and more compact; a tuba or euphonium, which are larger and more upright with broader tubing; or a mellophone, which is forward-facing and less tightly coiled. Even partial views often show the signature circular wrap and valve cluster.

name: frying pan
567.description: A shallow round cooking pan with a broad flat or slightly curved base, low sloping sides, and a single long handle; some examples are cast iron, nonstick, stainless steel, or enameled, and may be empty or shown while frying food.
567.guidelines: Classify as frying pan when the vessel is a shallow handled pan meant for frying or sautéing. Include skillets, including cast-iron skillets, if they share the same shallow round form. Do not confuse with a saucepan or sauté pan, which is typically deeper with straighter sides; a wok, which has much higher rounded sides; a griddle, which is flat and usually handleless or rectangular; or a baking/roasting pan, which is ovenware rather than a handheld stovetop frying vessel.

name: fur coat
568.description: A coat made wholly or partly of animal fur or faux fur, typically with a plush, thick, hairy surface. It may be long or short, full-length or cropped, and usually has a soft bulky silhouette with a large collar, lapels, hood, cuffs, or trim. Colors range from white, gray, tan, and brown to black, and some examples show spotted or patterned fur.
568.guidelines: Classify as fur coat when the main garment is an outer coat whose defining visible material is fur or fur-like pile over most of the garment or along prominent trim. Include full fur coats and coats with substantial fur collars, fronts, cuffs, or hoods. Do not confuse with a fur stole, shawl, boa, or cape, which are draped accessories rather than sleeved coats; with shearling or fleece jackets, which usually show suede/leather exteriors and wool only on the lining or edges; or with ordinary wool overcoats that have only small fur accents. The key cues are coat structure plus clearly visible fur as the dominant exterior feature.

name: garbage truck
569.description: A heavy road truck built for waste collection, typically with a large enclosed body for holding trash, a boxy cab, and loading equipment at the front, side, or rear. Common forms include rear-loading compactors and front-loading trucks with lifting forks or arms for emptying bins into the body.
569.guidelines: Classify as garbage truck when the vehicle is clearly a refuse-collection truck with an enclosed waste body and bin-lifting or compaction hardware. Include rear loaders, front loaders, side loaders, and bin lorries. Do not confuse with dump trucks or tipper trucks, which carry open loads and lack trash-compaction bodies; recycling or vacuum tank trucks, which may have utility bodies but not standard refuse-loading mechanisms; or street sweepers, which are smaller cleaning vehicles with brushes rather than trash-compactor bodies.

name: respirator
570.description: Protective respiratory equipment worn over the nose and mouth, and sometimes covering the entire face or head. It is typically made of molded rubber, plastic, or layered filter material, secured with straps, and often includes one or more prominent filters, cartridges, canisters, or exhalation valves on the front or sides. Forms range from disposable cup-shaped masks to half-face and full-face gas-mask styles.
570.guidelines: Classify as respirator when the item is a wearable device intended to filter or block harmful particles, fumes, or gases from inhaled air. This includes disposable filtering masks, cartridge respirators, and full-face gas masks. Do not confuse with oxygen masks, which deliver supplied oxygen and are usually lighter, medical or aviation devices without filter cartridges; scuba masks or diving full-face masks, which have clear underwater faceplates and breathing regulators; or welding helmets and face shields, which protect the face/eyes but are not respiratory filters.

name: gas pump
571.description: A freestanding fuel-dispensing machine, typically found at a filling station, with one or more hoses and nozzle handles for pumping gasoline or other fuel. It usually has a meter or display showing the amount dispensed and price, and may be either a modern rectangular dispenser or an older rounded vintage style with analog dials or mechanical counters.
571.guidelines: Classify as a gas pump when the main object is a fuel dispenser with hose, nozzle, and fuel meter/display. Include both modern service-station pumps and antique visible-pump styles. Do not confuse with parking meters, vending machines, air pumps, EV charging stations, or standalone tanks: gas pumps are specifically designed to dispense liquid motor fuel and almost always show fuel grades, gallon/liter counts, or price information, plus a fuel hose/nozzle.

name: goblet
572.description: A goblet is a drinking vessel with a bowl-shaped cup raised on a stem and foot. It is typically wider and deeper than a flute, often made of glass, metal, ceramic, or wood, and may be plain or highly decorative with colored, cut, engraved, or sculpted surfaces.
572.guidelines: Classify stemmed drinking cups with a broad bowl as goblets. Include ornamental and ceremonial versions as long as they retain the cup-on-stem form. Do not confuse with wine flutes or champagne flutes, which are taller and narrower; chalices, which are usually more explicitly ceremonial or ecclesiastical; tumblers, which have no stem; or vases and urns, which are not drinking vessels.

name: go-kart
573.description: A small, low-slung four-wheeled kart with an open frame or simple bodywork, a single exposed seat, and very small tires. It is typically driven by one person with a steering wheel, sits close to the ground, and often appears on kart tracks or paved racing circuits; some versions have minimal bumper panels or fairings, while others show a bare tubular chassis.
573.guidelines: Classify as go-kart when the vehicle is a compact recreational or racing kart: very low to the ground, single-seat, open, and much smaller and simpler than a car. Do not confuse it with bumper cars, which have a rounded enclosed body and amusement-ride appearance; formula race cars, which are much larger with prominent wings and full racing-car proportions; lawn tractors or ride-on mowers, which have larger bodies and utility features; or ATVs/dune buggies, which are taller, heavier, and built for off-road use.

name: golf ball
574.description: A small hard ball used in golf, typically white though sometimes yellow or other colors, with a nearly spherical shape and a surface covered in many shallow dimples. It is usually shown on grass, a tee, near a hole, or in groups such as practice balls.
574.guidelines: Classify as golf ball when the object is a dimpled golf ball, usually small, smooth-edged, and uniformly spherical. Distinguish it from ping-pong balls, which are larger relative to hand scale and lack dimples; from wiffle balls or practice plastic balls, which have large holes or openings; and from baseballs or softballs, which have visible stitched seams instead of an all-over dimple pattern. Do not rely on color alone, since golf balls may be white, yellow, or other bright colors.

name: golf cart
575.description: A small, low-speed open vehicle with a simple boxy body, bench seating, a roof canopy, and four small wheels, typically used to carry people and golf bags around a golf course. Most have no full doors, a short hood or front cowl, and an upright windshield; some variants are customized for utility, police, resort, or neighborhood use but retain the same compact cart form.
575.guidelines: Classify as golf cart when the vehicle is a compact open-sided cart built for short-distance transport, usually with bench seats, a canopy roof, and golf-course or campus/resort styling. Include customized or decorated versions if the base vehicle is still clearly a golf cart. Do not confuse with ATVs or UTVs, which have larger knobby tires, more rugged off-road frames, and motorcycle-like or side-by-side utility styling; microcars or neighborhood electric vehicles, which usually have full car bodies, doors, and enclosed cabins; or mobility scooters, which are much smaller single-person devices.

name: Venetian gondola
576.description: A long, narrow black rowing boat with a low rounded hull and both bow and stern swept upward. The bow typically carries the distinctive metal prow ornament called a ferro, and many examples have upholstered passenger seats or a small cabin area. It is usually seen in Venice’s canals, propelled by a standing gondolier with a single long oar.
576.guidelines: Classify as Venetian gondola when the boat is the traditional Venice canal craft: very slender, asymmetrical, black, with high upturned ends and the prominent ferro at the bow. Do not confuse it with generic rowboats, skiffs, canoes, or punts, which lack the ornate ferro and characteristic Venetian shape, or with larger canal boats and motorboats, which are wider and not single-oar propelled from a standing position.

name: gong
577.description: A gong is a large circular metal percussion instrument, usually bronze or brass, suspended vertically from a frame or cord and struck with a padded mallet. It appears as a flat or slightly convex disc with a hammered or polished surface, often golden, bronze, or darkened with patina; some examples have a raised central boss while others are nearly flat.
577.guidelines: Classify as gong when the image shows a suspended circular metal disc meant to be struck, typically hanging vertically in a stand or frame. Do not confuse it with a cymbal, which is usually smaller, handheld or paired, and not hung in a large frame; a bell, which is cup-shaped rather than disc-shaped; or a steel drum/pan, which is a horizontal bowl-like instrument with note dents. Bossed and flat tam-tam forms both belong here.

name: gown
578.description: A long, full-length dress with a fitted or shaped bodice and a flowing skirt, usually made for formal, ceremonial, or elegant wear. It may be strapless, sleeveless, or have sleeves, and can range from slim evening silhouettes to voluminous ball- or wedding-style designs, often with draped, pleated, satin, lace, or embellished fabric.
578.guidelines: Classify as a gown when the garment is a long formal dress extending to the ankles or floor, typically with an elegant, occasion-wear silhouette. Include evening gowns, ball gowns, bridal gowns, and similarly formal full-length dresses. Do not confuse with ordinary dresses, which are often shorter or more casual; robes or abayas, which are looser and coat-like; or skirts worn with separate tops. The key cues are a one-piece formal dress structure, full-length cut, and dressy styling.

name: grand piano
579.description: An acoustic piano with a large wing-shaped horizontal body, a full keyboard, and a flat hinged lid that can be raised on a prop. Its strings and hammers lie horizontally inside a polished wooden case, usually on three legs, often with a matching bench.
579.guidelines: Classify as grand piano when the piano has a horizontal wing-shaped case and a lift-up top lid, with the soundboard and strings extending behind the keyboard. Do not confuse with an upright piano or spinet, which have a tall vertical back and strings mounted vertically, or with a digital keyboard, which lacks the large acoustic body and raised lid.

name: greenhouse
580.description: A greenhouse is a glass- or clear-plastic-enclosed structure used for growing or displaying plants. It typically has transparent walls and a peaked or arched roof supported by a metal or wooden frame, with rows of plants, benches, hanging baskets, or planting beds visible inside.
580.guidelines: Classify as greenhouse when the main subject is an enclosed plant-growing structure with transparent glazing and a visible frame. Include both interior and exterior views, from small garden glasshouses to large commercial growing houses. Do not confuse with a botanical garden conservatory, which is usually a larger public greenhouse building but still visually qualifies only if the greenhouse structure itself is the subject; avoid labeling ordinary garden centers, nurseries, or flower shops unless the transparent enclosed growing house is clearly shown. Distinguish from polytunnels by their rigid framed glasshouse appearance, though plastic-covered hoop houses may still count if they are clearly functioning as greenhouses.

name: car grille
581.description: The front grille of a motor vehicle: a rigid panel or opening at the front of the body, typically made of metal or plastic bars, slats, mesh, or a grid. It is usually vertically oriented on the nose of the vehicle, often framed in chrome or body-colored trim, and commonly sits between or below the headlights. Many examples include brand badges or hood ornaments, and older cars often have prominent chrome vertical or horizontal bars.
581.guidelines: Classify as car grille when the image centers on the vehicle’s front air-intake grille or its decorative slatted front fascia. Include close-up views where the grille dominates the image, even if headlights, emblem, bumper, or hood ornament are also visible. Do not confuse with a whole car front or hood: the grille should be the main subject. Distinguish from vents, bumpers, and generic mesh panels by the grille’s location on the front of a vehicle and its characteristic slatted or meshed design. Exclude non-vehicle grilles such as window grilles, speaker grilles, barbecue grates, or radiator cores shown without the car front fascia.

name: grocery store
582.description: A retail food shop or market selling groceries and other household food items. Typical images show store aisles, produce displays, refrigerated cases, shelves of packaged goods, shopping carts, checkout areas, or storefronts, often densely stocked with fruits, vegetables, meats, dairy, snacks, and bottled products.
582.guidelines: Classify as grocery store when the scene is clearly a food-retail environment with multiple grocery categories or a recognizable food-market storefront/interior. This includes supermarkets and small neighborhood grocers. Do not confuse with a produce market or farmers' market, which focus mainly on fresh fruits and vegetables in open stalls, or with a convenience store, which is smaller and usually emphasizes drinks, snacks, and limited groceries. Exclude specialty shops such as bakeries, fish markets, butcher shops, or cheese shops when only one food type is being sold.

name: guillotine
583.description: A guillotine is a tall execution device with two upright posts joined by a crossbeam, forming a frame that guides a heavy angled blade sliding vertically. It usually has a wooden or metal structure, a suspended blade near the top, and a base with a neck opening or restraining board below.
583.guidelines: Classify as a guillotine when the image shows the characteristic vertical frame with a suspended falling blade and execution platform or stock. Do not confuse it with a paper cutter, which is tabletop-sized with a hinged arm, or a chopping/cutting machine, which lacks the tall twin-post execution frame and neck restraint. Gallows and other execution devices may also be similar, but they do not have the distinctive sliding triangular blade mounted between uprights.

name: hair clip
584.description: A small hair accessory used to hold or decorate hair, typically made from metal, plastic, fabric, beads, or other decorative materials. It usually has a clasp, pin, slide, or spring mechanism, and may be plain or highly ornamental with bows, flowers, buttons, rhinestones, feathers, or other embellishments.
584.guidelines: Classify as hair clip when the object is a wearable fastener designed to attach to and hold hair. This includes barrettes, snap clips, and decorated sliding clips. Do not confuse with hair ties or scrunchies, which are flexible loops without a rigid clip; brooches or pins, which are meant for clothing; or jewelry such as earrings and bracelets, which are not hair fasteners. The key cue is a visible clip, bar, pin, or sliding mechanism intended for securing hair.

name: hair spray
585.description: A hairstyling product packaged most often in an aerosol can or spray bottle, used by misting a fine cloud onto hair. It typically appears as a tall cylindrical can with a spray nozzle and cap, and is often shown being sprayed onto a person's hairstyle or as a visible mist plume.
585.guidelines: Classify as hair spray when the product is specifically for styling or setting hair and is presented as a spray can or pump bottle for use on hair. Common look-alikes include deodorant/body spray, air freshener, spray paint, dry shampoo, and other hair products such as mousse or detangler. Distinguish it by hair-related labeling, salon/styling context, and images showing application to hair; exclude non-hair sprays and non-spray hair products.

name: half-track
586.description: A half-track is a vehicle with front wheels for steering and continuous tracks at the rear for propulsion. It typically has a truck-like or armored body, an elongated profile, and a mixed wheel-and-track running gear, often seen on military transport and armored vehicles.
586.guidelines: Classify as half-track only when the vehicle clearly combines front steerable wheels with rear tracks. Do not confuse it with full-tracked vehicles such as tanks or armored personnel carriers, which have tracks on both sides and no front wheels, or with ordinary trucks and armored cars, which use wheels only. Include both armored and unarmored half-track variants, but exclude vehicles where the tracks are only temporary attachments or not part of the basic design.

name: hammer
587.description: A hammer is a hand tool with a weighted head mounted perpendicular to a handle. The head is usually metal and commonly has one flat striking face; many examples also have a claw, peen, or other shaped opposite end. Handles may be wood, metal, or fiberglass. Across images, the defining form is the compact heavy head used for delivering blows.
587.guidelines: Classify as hammer when the object is a handheld striking tool with a transverse weighted head and handle. This includes claw hammers, ball-peen hammers, sledge-style hammers, and similar variants. Do not confuse with mallets, which usually have larger cylindrical or block-shaped heads made of wood, rubber, or soft material; axes or hatchets, which have a sharpened blade; pickaxes or mattocks, which have long pointed or adze-like ends for digging; or chisels/punches, which are struck by a hammer rather than used like one.

name: wicker basket
588.description: A woven basket or basket-like container made from wicker, rattan, reed, or similar natural fibers. It is usually light tan or brown, often rectangular or oval, and may have a carrying handle, fitted lid, or open top. Many examples are boxy picnic or storage baskets, while others are trays, hampers, or small household containers with the same woven wicker construction.
588.guidelines: Classify as wicker basket when the object is a clearly woven natural-fiber basket or hamper, including picnic baskets, storage baskets, and similar wicker containers. The key cue is the interlaced wicker or reed structure. Do not confuse with non-wicker baskets made of plastic, fabric, or metal mesh, or with suitcases, boxes, or bins that are solid rather than woven. If the object is simply a generic basket in another material, use the other class; this class is specifically for wicker-style woven baskets and hampers.

name: hair dryer
589.description: A handheld electric appliance for drying hair, typically shaped like a pistol or T-shaped tool with a handle, a short barrel, and an air outlet nozzle at the front. Most have a rear air intake grille, control switches on the handle, and a power cord; colors and styling vary widely.
589.guidelines: Classify as hair dryer only when the object is a handheld device designed to blow heated or unheated air, usually with a front nozzle and rear intake grille. Do not confuse it with a heat gun, which is usually more cylindrical and tool-like; a vacuum or leaf blower, which is larger and built for cleaning or outdoor use; or a fan/heater without the characteristic handheld hair-dryer form. Images may show the dryer alone or being used on a person's hair.

name: handheld computer
590.description: A small computer designed to be held and operated in the hands, usually with a screen and built-in controls such as a touchscreen, stylus, miniature keyboard, navigation pad, or physical buttons. This category includes PDAs, pocket PCs, industrial handheld terminals, palmtop-style devices, small tablets, e-readers, and handheld game systems. They are generally larger or more computer-like than ordinary mobile phones and are built for computing, data entry, reading, or specialized field use.
590.guidelines: Classify as handheld computer when the device is a self-contained portable computer meant for hand use, especially if it has a PDA-style touchscreen, stylus input, miniature keyboard, rugged barcode/data-terminal form, clamshell palmtop design, or handheld game-console layout. Do not confuse with regular smartphones or feature phones: phones are primarily designed for calling and usually have a clear phone keypad or standard phone form factor. Also exclude laptops and desktop tablets that are too large to be comfortably hand-held. Industrial scanners, Pocket PCs, Palm-style organizers, and PSP-like gaming devices belong here if they are clearly handheld computing devices rather than ordinary phones.

name: handkerchief
591.description: A handkerchief is a small square piece of cloth, usually lightweight cotton or linen, meant to be folded and carried on the person. It is typically plain white or lightly colored, and may have printed patterns, embroidered initials or motifs, lace trim, or decorative borders.
591.guidelines: Classify as a handkerchief when the image shows a small personal cloth square intended to be folded and carried, often soft, thin, and neatly hemmed. Do not confuse it with a napkin, which is usually larger and associated with table settings; a pocket square, which is mainly a suit accessory and often stiffer or more formal; a bandana, which is usually larger and characterized by bold paisley prints; or a tissue, which is paper rather than fabric.

name: hard disk drive
592.description: A hard disk drive is a computer storage device, usually a rectangular metal unit with a printed label on the outside and data/power connectors on one edge. Open units show one or more shiny circular platters and a pivoting actuator arm with read/write heads. It appears in internal desktop or laptop sizes, in drive bays, or inside external enclosures.
592.guidelines: Classify as hard disk drive when the image shows the complete magnetic storage device itself: a sealed rectangular drive body, or an opened drive with reflective platters and an actuator arm. Do not confuse with a solid-state drive (SSD), which lacks platters and moving arms; optical disc drives, which use a tray for CDs/DVDs; floppy disk drives, which are for removable floppy disks; or loose platters/read heads shown without the full drive unless they are clearly part of an opened HDD.

name: harmonica
593.description: A harmonica is a small handheld free-reed instrument with a slim rectangular body, usually metal or metal-capped, with a row of air holes along one long side. It is pocket-sized, typically shiny or chrome-finished, and often has visible cover plates and comb openings.
593.guidelines: Classify as harmonica when the image shows the small rectangular mouth-played instrument with multiple side-by-side holes used for blowing and drawing air. Do not confuse it with an accordion or concertina, which are much larger bellows instruments, or with a pan flute, which has separate tubes. Also exclude jaw harp/Jew's harp, which is a small frame with a single central tongue rather than a row of holes, despite the misleading synonym 'harp' in the original class name.

name: harp
594.description: A harp is a large triangular or arched stringed musical instrument with many parallel strings stretched between a resonant soundbox and a curved neck, usually supported by a front pillar or frame. It is typically made of polished wood, often tall enough to stand on the floor, and is played by plucking the strings with both hands.
594.guidelines: Classify as harp when the instrument has a tall open frame with many strings running vertically or diagonally between a soundboard and a curved neck. Common harps include full-size pedal harps and smaller lever or folk harps, but all keep the characteristic harp frame and numerous plucked strings. Do not confuse with a lyre, which is smaller and U-shaped with two arms and a crossbar; a zither or autoharp, whose strings lie across a flat body; or a piano, whose strings are enclosed inside a keyboard instrument.

name: harvester
595.description: A large agricultural machine used to harvest crops, typically self-propelled and boxy, with a high operator cab, large wheels, and a wide front-mounted cutting or gathering attachment. Depending on the crop, it may carry a grain header, corn header, pickup head, or other specialized harvesting unit, and is often shown working through fields of wheat, corn, rice, or other crops.
595.guidelines: Classify as harvester when the machine is clearly built for collecting and processing crops in the field and has a prominent harvesting head at the front. This category includes different specialized harvesters, not just one crop type. Distinguish it from tractors, which usually pull implements rather than containing the harvesting mechanism themselves; from mowers or reapers, which mainly cut vegetation without the full harvesting body; and from balers or threshers, which are separate post-cutting machines. The key cues are the large integrated body, elevated cab, and wide crop-harvesting attachment.

name: hatchet
596.description: A small one-handed axe with a short handle and a metal head, typically having a broad cutting blade on one side and sometimes a hammer poll or wedge-like back on the other. It is compact, hand-sized, and commonly shown for chopping kindling, trimming branches, or light woodcutting.
596.guidelines: Classify as hatchet when the tool is a compact axe designed for one-handed use, with a short handle and relatively small head. Do not confuse it with a full-sized axe, which is larger and usually two-handed, or a tomahawk, which is typically slimmer and more specialized in style. Exclude tools with very different heads such as hammers, adzes, mattocks, pickaxes, or splitting mauls.

name: handgun holster
597.description: A fitted carrier for a firearm, usually a handgun, made of leather, molded plastic, or fabric. It typically has the distinct outline of a pistol or revolver, with a shaped pocket, trigger-guard area, belt loops, clips, straps, or retention features for wearing on the belt or body.
597.guidelines: Classify as a handgun holster only when the item is clearly designed to hold a firearm or has the unmistakable molded shape of one. Do not confuse it with a scabbard or sheath for a sword, knife, or bayonet, which are longer and blade-shaped, or with a generic pouch/case, which lacks the gun-shaped form and firearm-specific retention features.

name: home theater
598.description: A dedicated or semi-dedicated media viewing space centered on a large television or projection screen, typically paired with speakers and other audio-video equipment. It usually appears as a room or entertainment area with theater-like presentation features such as dim lighting, sofas or recliners, and an entertainment center or media cabinet.
598.guidelines: Classify as home theater when the image shows a residential viewing setup designed for immersive movie or TV watching, usually with a large screen plus visible speakers, projector/screen, or AV components in a living room or theater room. Do not confuse with a plain living room that merely contains a TV; this category emphasizes the overall media-viewing setup. Also distinguish it from an entertainment center, which is the furniture unit itself, and from a projector screen or television, which are single objects rather than the full room setup.

name: honeycomb
599.description: A honeycomb is a sheet or mass of tightly packed hexagonal cells forming a regular cellular pattern. In natural examples it appears as waxy or papery comb built by bees or wasps, usually in cream, yellow, tan, brown, or amber tones, and may be seen as flat panels, hanging comb, or nest sections with open cells or capped cells.
599.guidelines: Classify images as honeycomb when the defining visual feature is the comb itself: a dense array of hexagonal cells in wax or paper, whether in a beehive frame, a natural hanging comb, or a wasp paper nest. Do not require visible insects. Distinguish it from a beehive or nest box, where the wooden box or hive structure is primary rather than the comb. Distinguish it from plain hexagon designs such as tile floors, metal grids, or manufactured mesh by looking for natural waxy or papery texture, irregular edges, brood or honey-filled cells, and nest-like construction.

name: hook
600.description: A hook is a curved or bent piece of metal or other rigid material with one end shaped to catch, hang, pull, or suspend something. It may be J-shaped, S-shaped, U-shaped, or part of a larger fixture, and is commonly seen on walls, racks, chains, hangers, lifting gear, or jewelry fasteners.
600.guidelines: Classify as hook when the defining feature is a curved catching end meant for hanging, snagging, or holding. Include single hooks, double hooks, S-hooks, wall hooks, cargo hooks, and similar fixtures. Do not confuse with hangers, carabiners, clips, clothespins, or claws: hangers are full garment-support frames, carabiners are closed loop fasteners with a gate, clips pinch objects between jaws, and animal claws are biological body parts rather than standalone hardware.

name: hoop skirt
601.description: A very wide, bell-shaped or dome-shaped skirt silhouette created by a rigid internal framework, typically hoops or a cage, that holds the fabric away from the legs. It is usually floor-length or near floor-length and appears smoothly expanded around the lower body with strong circular volume.
601.guidelines: Classify as hoop skirt when the defining feature is the structured, cage-supported skirt shape with pronounced outward volume. Include historical dresses or costumes built over visible or hidden hoops. Do not confuse with ball gowns or full skirts that are voluminous only from layered fabric, petticoats, or tulle; hoop skirts keep a stiff, architectural bell or cone form. Also distinguish from panniers, which extend mainly sideways at the hips rather than forming a round all-around dome.

name: horizontal bar
602.description: A single rigid bar mounted horizontally between two upright supports. In gymnastics it appears as a polished metal bar held high above the ground by tension cables; in playgrounds it may be a simpler fixed bar for hanging or swinging. Images typically show people gripping, hanging from, or rotating around the lone bar.
602.guidelines: Classify as horizontal bar when the defining object is one straight elevated bar supported at both ends, usually used for gymnastics skills or hanging. Include both competitive high-bar apparatus and simple playground horizontal bars. Do not confuse with uneven bars or parallel bars, which have two bars; balance beam, which is a broad solid beam; or pull-up stations/monkey bars, which usually have multiple bars or a larger frame.

name: horse-drawn vehicle
603.description: A horse-drawn vehicle is a wheeled conveyance pulled by one or more horses or similar draft animals by means of shafts or a pole and harness. Across examples it includes simple two-wheeled carts, four-wheeled wagons, passenger carriages, and utility carts, usually with an open or enclosed body riding behind the animal.
603.guidelines: Classify as horse-drawn vehicle when the image shows an animal harnessed to and pulling a wheeled vehicle. This category includes carts, wagons, carriages, and similar road vehicles regardless of whether they are for passengers or cargo. Do not confuse it with a chariot, which is typically a light ancient or ceremonial two-wheeled vehicle with a standing rider, or with a sleigh, which has runners instead of wheels. Exclude images showing only a horse, saddle, or harness without a clearly attached wheeled vehicle, and exclude hand-pulled carts or motor vehicles.

name: hourglass
604.description: A timekeeping device with two clear glass bulbs joined by a narrow neck, usually mounted vertically in a small frame or stand. Fine sand or similar granules flow from the upper bulb to the lower bulb at a steady rate. It is typically symmetrical, with the pinched center and visible falling sand as the key visual feature.
604.guidelines: Classify as hourglass when the image shows the distinctive two-bulb glass timer with material flowing or collected in one bulb and often held in a frame. Do not confuse with laboratory glassware such as flasks, decanters, or double-bulb decorative vessels that lack sand and timing purpose. Distinguish from egg timers, stopwatches, clocks, and other timers by the visible sand-filled glass bulbs and narrow central passage.

name: Apple iPod
605.description: A small handheld digital media player made by Apple, typically a slim rectangular device with a screen and a distinctive circular control wheel or touch controls on the front. Most examples have a clean minimalist face, metallic or glossy plastic body, rounded corners, and white, black, or bright colored finishes. Sizes and proportions vary across models, from very compact square or clip-like units to taller, narrow players.
605.guidelines: Classify as Apple iPod when the device is clearly an iPod model, especially if it has Apple’s characteristic minimalist design, front screen, and click wheel or other recognizable iPod controls. Include different iPod lines such as classic, nano, mini, and shuffle if they are identifiable as iPods. Do not confuse with generic MP3 players, smartphones, or other portable media players: those often lack the iconic iPod wheel layout, Apple branding, or distinctive iPod form factors.

name: clothes iron
606.description: A handheld ironing appliance with a flat heated metal soleplate, a pointed front tip, and an arched handle above the body. Most examples are electric irons with a plastic housing and cord, often in white, blue, gray, or other solid colors; some are steam irons with water reservoirs, while a few are older heavy metal irons with simple handles.
606.guidelines: Classify as clothes iron when the object is specifically a garment-ironing tool with a smooth soleplate meant to press fabric. It may be electric, steam-powered, cordless-base style, travel-sized, or an older cast-iron form. Do not confuse with ironing boards, fabric steamers, heat presses, kettles, or wedge-shaped household appliances. The key cues are the flat soleplate, pointed nose, and top handle designed for pressing clothes.

name: jack-o'-lantern
607.description: A hollowed pumpkin carved with cut-out faces or other Halloween-themed designs and lit from inside, producing a warm orange glow through the openings.
607.guidelines: Classify carved, illuminated pumpkins as jack-o'-lanterns, whether the cut-outs form a classic face, a scary expression, or another recognizable design. Do not confuse with uncarved pumpkins, decorative pumpkin props without carved openings, or lanterns made from other materials. The key cues are a real pumpkin shape with carved cut-out areas and visible internal illumination.

name: jeans
608.description: Trousers made of denim, typically blue or blue-gray, with a waistband, belt loops, fly, and long pant legs. They usually have front and back pockets, visible seams, rivets, and sturdy contrast stitching, and may appear faded, distressed, embroidered, or decorated in different washes and cuts.
608.guidelines: Classify as this category only when the image shows denim pants/blue jeans. Include jeans being worn or laid flat, even with decorative stitching, patches, distressing, or unusual washes. Do not include other denim garments such as jackets, shirts, skirts, shorts, overalls, or dresses. Exclude non-denim pants and trousers. If only part of the garment is visible, look for classic jean cues such as denim fabric, pocket layout, rivets, and jeans-style stitching.

name: Land Rover
609.description: A Land Rover is a rugged SUV or off-road utility vehicle, typically with a tall stance, boxy body, large windows, upright front end, and high ground clearance. Common appearances include flat body panels, a rectangular grille, exposed or simple utilitarian styling, and two- or four-door wagon, pickup, or hardtop forms.
609.guidelines: Classify as Land Rover when the vehicle has the characteristic Land Rover/Range Rover family look, especially the boxy off-road proportions and utilitarian body style seen in Defender and Series models. Do not confuse it with Jeep vehicles, which often have a seven-slot grille and different body shaping, or with other SUVs and crossovers that are more rounded, lower, and road-oriented. Exclude generic SUVs, pickups, and military vehicles unless they are clearly Land Rover models.

name: T-shirt
610.description: A lightweight pullover shirt for the upper body, typically with short sleeves, no front opening, and a round crew neck. It is usually made of knit fabric and may be plain or decorated with printed graphics, logos, text, or simple patterns.
610.guidelines: Classify as a T-shirt when the garment is a casual pull-on top with a simple torso shape, short sleeves, and no buttons or full front opening. Include graphic tees and athletic tees. Do not confuse with a polo shirt (has a collar and partial button placket), dress shirt (structured collar and full opening), tank top (sleeveless), sweatshirt (heavier fabric, usually long-sleeved), or soccer jersey/other sports jersey when the garment is clearly specialized team uniform apparel rather than a generic tee.

name: jigsaw puzzle
611.description: A picture or design cut into many interlocking pieces with distinctive tabs and blanks that fit together to form a flat image or shape. It may appear fully assembled, partly assembled with missing pieces, or as loose individual pieces; common materials are cardboard, wood, or foam, and the finished surface usually shows visible cut lines between pieces.
611.guidelines: Classify as jigsaw puzzle when the object is a set or assembly of interlocking cut pieces meant to be fitted together into one picture or form. Include completed puzzles, in-progress puzzles, close-ups of individual pieces, and novelty piece shapes if they clearly use jigsaw-style interlocking cuts. Do not confuse with mosaic, stained glass, tilework, or patchwork, which may look segmented but do not use removable interlocking pieces. Exclude tangrams, block puzzles, and other assembly toys with geometric parts rather than classic tab-and-blank jigsaw pieces.

name: hand-pulled rickshaw
612.description: A lightweight passenger vehicle with a single bench seat mounted between two large side wheels and long shafts extending forward for a person to pull. It usually has an open front, a raised footrest, and a folding canopy or hood, with upholstery often in red or black.
612.guidelines: Classify as hand-pulled rickshaw when the vehicle is a two-wheeled passenger cart designed to be pulled by a person running or walking between the front shafts. Do not confuse with a cycle rickshaw or pedicab, which has pedals and a bicycle frame; with horse-drawn carriages, which lack human pull shafts; or with wheelchairs and strollers, which are push vehicles with smaller wheels and different seating layouts.

name: joystick
613.description: A hand-operated game or control input device centered on a short stick, thumbstick, or directional control used to steer movement. It may appear as a standalone upright stick on a base, an arcade-style stick mounted on a panel, or as part of a gamepad/controller body with buttons and triggers. Typical forms include a vertical lever with a rounded top and surrounding pivot boot, often paired with one or more action buttons.
613.guidelines: Classify as joystick when the defining control is a stick or thumb-operated directional control for games or similar interactive input, including flight sticks, arcade sticks, and gamepads with analog sticks. Do not confuse with a mouse, trackball, remote control, or generic game controller without a visible joystick-like control. If the image shows a full gamepad, it should still fit only when analog sticks/thumbsticks are the salient feature; otherwise similar categories like gamepad or remote are better.

name: kimono
614.description: A kimono is a traditional Japanese robe with a long, straight, wrap-front shape, wide sleeves, and a broad sash (obi) tied around the waist. It is usually ankle-length and made in solid colors or elaborate woven, dyed, or printed patterns, often floral or geometric.
614.guidelines: Classify as kimono when the garment is a Japanese wrap robe with wide sleeves and an obi, worn as formalwear, casual wear, costume, or displayed on a hanger or mannequin. Do not confuse it with yukata, which is a lighter, more casual cotton summer garment of the same basic form; if the broader robe form is the shared visual category across images, use kimono. Also distinguish it from hanbok, which has a short jacket and full skirt, and from Chinese hanfu or qipao, which use different cuts, collars, and closures rather than the straight wrap-front robe with obi.

name: knee pad
615.description: Protective padding worn over or around the knee, typically as a soft sleeve, wraparound brace, or strapped guard with foam or a hard plastic cap. It covers the front of the knee and sometimes part of the upper shin or lower thigh, and is commonly black but may appear in many colors and sport-specific designs.
615.guidelines: Classify as knee pad when the item’s primary purpose is cushioning or protecting the knee joint. It may be a soft elastic pad, padded sleeve, or hard-shell protective guard. Do not confuse with shin guards, which mainly protect the front of the lower leg; elbow pads, which are smaller and shaped for the elbow; or full knee braces, which usually have rigid side hinges and stronger stabilizing structure rather than mainly padding.

name: knot
616.description: An interlacing or fastening made by looping, crossing, and tightening rope, cord, string, or similar flexible material. Visually, it appears as one or more strands wrapped around themselves or another object, forming a compact tied structure with visible turns, crossings, loops, and free ends.
616.guidelines: Classify images as knots when the main subject is the tied structure itself in rope, cord, string, cable, or similar material. Include both simple and complex tying patterns, whether loose, tight, decorative, or functional, and whether tied around posts, rails, hooks, or other ropes. Do not confuse with an untied coil or bundle of rope, braids or woven strands, chain links, or hardware such as hooks and cleats unless an actual tied knot is clearly visible. The key cue is a deliberate over-under interlacing that secures or joins flexible strands.

name: lab coat
617.description: A lab coat is a knee- to thigh-length white or light-colored coat with long sleeves, a front button closure, and a notched collar, typically worn over regular clothes. It often has large patch or side pockets and is made of plain woven fabric for laboratory, medical, or technical work.
617.guidelines: Classify as lab coat when the main item is this protective work coat, usually white and worn by scientists, doctors, technicians, or shown on its own. Distinguish it from a blazer or suit jacket by the longer straight cut, simpler utilitarian fabric, and workwear pockets; from a chef’s coat by the usually single-breasted front and coat-like length; from scrubs by the structured collar and buttoned opening; and from coveralls or gowns by the open-front coat design rather than a one-piece garment or wraparound robe.

name: ladle
618.description: A ladle is a long-handled utensil with a deep, rounded bowl used for scooping and pouring liquids or soft foods. It is usually made of metal, wood, plastic, or bamboo, and lacks the perforations seen in slotted serving spoons.
618.guidelines: Classify as a ladle when the utensil has a distinctly deep cup-like bowl on a long handle, suited for lifting soup, broth, sauce, punch, or similar liquids. Do not confuse it with a spoon or serving spoon, which has a shallower bowl, or a slotted spoon, which has holes or slots. Exclude dippers and scoops whose form is not the standard kitchen or water-ladling utensil shape.

name: lampshade
619.description: A lampshade is a cover fitted around a light bulb or lamp to diffuse, direct, and soften the light. It is typically conical, cylindrical, drum-shaped, or globe-like, and may be made of fabric, paper, plastic, glass, metal, or woven material. Lampshades are usually translucent or perforated enough to let light pass while reducing glare.
619.guidelines: Classify as lampshade when the image centers on the shade or cover surrounding a light source, rather than the whole lamp. Include shades on table lamps, floor lamps, wall lamps, pendant lights, or ceiling fixtures. Do not confuse with a complete lamp or light fixture, where the base, stand, arm, or mounting hardware is the main subject. Also distinguish from bare light bulbs, lanterns, chandeliers, and reflector housings: a lampshade is specifically the enclosing or surrounding shade that modifies the light.

name: laptop
notebook computer
620.description: A portable personal computer with a thin clamshell design: a flat display hinged to a lower base that contains a keyboard and built-in pointing device such as a trackpad or pointing stick. It is typically rectangular, slim, and sized for use on a desk or lap, whether open or closed.
620.guidelines: Classify as this category when the image shows a portable clamshell computer, open or closed. Include standard laptops and notebooks of different sizes. Do not confuse with desktop monitors or all-in-one PCs, which lack the hinged keyboard base; tablets, which do not have an attached clamshell keyboard; netbooks/mini laptops only if they are clearly still laptops in this broad sense; or briefcases, trays, and other objects merely supporting a laptop. The defining cue is the integrated screen-and-keyboard clamshell form.

name: lawn mower
621.description: A lawn mower is a machine for cutting grass, typically with a low wheeled body that houses rotating blades or a cutting reel and a long handle for pushing or guiding it. It may be powered, manual, or ride-on, but is consistently designed for trimming lawns.
621.guidelines: Classify as lawn mower when the object is clearly a grass-cutting machine with wheels and a mower deck or reel, including push mowers, reel mowers, and riding mowers. Do not confuse it with string trimmers, leaf blowers, tillers, or other yard tools that lack a mower deck or grass-cutting reel. Toy lawn mowers should be excluded unless the category explicitly includes toy examples; real lawn mowers usually have a cutting mechanism, larger wheels, and a more substantial frame.

name: lens cap
622.description: A small removable protective cover for the front of a camera lens, usually circular and flat or slightly domed, typically made of black plastic or metal and often marked with a camera or lens brand name. Many have pinch tabs, side grips, or a slip-on rim for attaching and removing them.
622.guidelines: Classify as lens cap when the object is specifically a detachable cover for a camera lens front element. It may be shown alone, being held, attached to a lens, or branded by camera makers such as Canon, Nikon, Olympus, Fujifilm, Sony, or Tamron. Do not confuse with a camera body cap or rear lens cap, which attach to the camera mount side rather than the lens front, or with a lens hood, which is deeper and ring-shaped rather than a flat cover. Exclude generic caps or lids not clearly made for camera lenses.

name: letter opener
623.description: A letter opener is a small handheld tool with a narrow, elongated blade and a pointed or tapered tip, used for opening envelopes. It often resembles a miniature knife or dagger but typically has a blunt or only lightly sharpened edge. Many examples are decorative, with metal, plastic, wood, or ornate novelty handles.
623.guidelines: Classify as letter opener when the object is a slim, dagger-like or knife-like implement specifically shaped for slitting envelopes, usually with a narrow blade and simple handle. Do not confuse it with a pocketknife or utility knife, which usually have clearly sharpened cutting edges, thicker blades, folding mechanisms, or replaceable blades. Do not label as a pen, stylus, awl, or dip pen nib holder: those are typically shorter, more cylindrical, and designed for writing or piercing rather than opening mail.

name: library or bookstore
624.description: A space devoted to books, either a public/academic library or a retail bookshop. Typical views show tall bookshelves, stacks or display tables of books, reading tables or seating areas, checkout or service desks, and sometimes storefront signs or window displays advertising books. Interiors may range from quiet study rooms to commercial sales floors; exteriors often show shopfronts labeled as bookstores.
624.guidelines: Classify images here when the primary scene is a book-focused interior or storefront: shelves dominated by books, browsing displays, reading areas, or bookstore signage. Include both lending libraries and bookshops. Do not confuse with offices or classrooms, which may have a few books but are organized around desks or teaching equipment rather than book storage and browsing. Distinguish from archives by the presence of ordinary browsable books instead of boxed records or restricted storage, and from general retail stores or newsstands by the dominance of books rather than mixed merchandise or magazines.

name: lifeboat
625.description: A small rescue or survival boat carried by ships or operated from shore, typically with a rigid hull and bright high-visibility coloring such as orange, orange-and-blue, or orange-and-white. It may appear as an open or cabin motor lifeboat, a fully enclosed survival craft, or a ship-mounted emergency boat, but it is generally compact, sturdy, and built for rough water and emergency use rather than cargo or leisure.
625.guidelines: Classify as lifeboat when the vessel is clearly an emergency rescue or evacuation craft: small relative to ships, highly visible, and designed for rescue/survival. Include RNLI-style rescue boats, enclosed survival lifeboats, and davit-mounted ship lifeboats. Do not confuse with inflatable rescue boats, which have obvious air-filled tubes; tugboats or pilot boats, which are larger working vessels and usually not bright orange emergency craft; or ordinary motorboats and ferries, which lack the specialized rescue/survival design and shipboard emergency context.

name: lighter
626.description: A lighter is a small handheld device used to produce a flame. Common examples have a plastic or metal body, a thumb-operated spark wheel or button at the top, and a metal hood around the flame outlet; many are rectangular pocket lighters, though refillable and novelty forms also occur.
626.guidelines: Classify as lighter when the image shows a handheld flame-producing device itself, whether lit or unlit, including disposable, refillable, and novelty lighters. Do not confuse with candles, matches, torches, or cigarette packs: the key cue is a compact pocket-sized igniter body with a built-in spark mechanism and nozzle/hood at the top. Exclude images where the lighter is only incidental and another object is the clear subject.

name: limousine
627.description: A limousine is a very long, chauffeur-driven luxury car or luxury SUV that has been extended well beyond standard vehicle length. It typically has a stretched body, multiple side windows, a long passenger cabin, and often a partitioned, upscale interior with facing seats or added amenities.
627.guidelines: Classify as limousine only when the vehicle is clearly a stretched luxury automobile or SUV with an elongated passenger compartment. Distinguish it from a standard sedan, town car, or luxury SUV by the unusually long wheelbase/body and extra side windows. Exclude buses, vans, hearses, and ordinary long cars that are not visibly stretched for chauffeured passenger service.

name: cruise ship
628.description: A large passenger ship with a tall multi-deck superstructure, long white or dark-painted hull, rows of cabin windows or private balconies, and prominent lifeboats mounted along the sides. These vessels are built like floating hotels, with many stacked decks, bridge and funnels on top, and a broad, boxy profile compared with cargo ships.
628.guidelines: Classify as cruise ship when the image shows a large leisure passenger vessel with many decks, balcony rows or cabin windows, and visible lifeboats. Include modern cruise liners and classic ocean liners used for passenger service. Do not confuse with cargo ships or container ships, which have open decks, cranes, or stacked containers; ferries, which are usually shorter and more utilitarian with vehicle openings; yachts, which are smaller and sleeker; or naval ships, which lack hotel-like balcony decks and lifeboat rows.

name: lipstick
629.description: A cosmetic stick of colored lip product in a small twist-up tube, usually with a slanted or pointed tip. It is most often seen as a solid waxy bullet in shades of red, pink, nude, purple, or brown, either in its casing or being applied to the lips.
629.guidelines: Classify as lipstick when the image shows the solid lip-color stick itself or a typical lipstick tube/bullet. Include both single tubes and groups of lipsticks, and lipstick being applied to lips. Do not confuse with lip gloss or liquid lipstick, which come in liquid form with bottles or wand applicators, or with lip balm, which is usually clear or lightly tinted and packaged more plainly. Exclude general makeup scenes unless lipstick is the clear main subject.

name: loafer
630.description: A loafer is a low-cut slip-on shoe with a closed upper, no laces or buckles, and a moccasin- or apron-style front. It usually has a flat or low heel and appears in leather or suede, often in black, brown, tan, or other solid colors. Common variants include penny loafers, tassel loafers, and bit loafers.
630.guidelines: Classify as loafer when the shoe is a dressy or casual slip-on with no fastening and a structured closed toe. Include penny, tassel, bit, and similar slip-on loafers. Do not confuse with moccasins or driving shoes, which are softer and more slipper-like with rubber pebble soles; ballet flats or pumps, which are more feminine and lack the loafer vamp details; or oxfords/derbies, which have laces.

name: lotion
631.description: A cosmetic or medicinal skin-care liquid or semi-liquid emulsion, usually packaged in bottles, pump dispensers, squeeze tubes, or small jars. It is typically opaque or lightly translucent and appears as a pourable cream or milky fluid used on the skin, scalp, or body.
631.guidelines: Classify as lotion when the product is a bottled or tubed topical emulsion meant to be applied to skin or scalp. Common look-alikes include cream, ointment, gel, toner, shampoo, conditioner, body wash, and perfume. Distinguish lotion from cream by its more fluid, pourable consistency and typical bottle packaging; from ointment by the lack of greasy, petroleum-like appearance; from gel by not being clear or jelly-like; from toner or micellar water by not being a thin watery liquid; and from perfume or aftershave by the absence of a fragrance-bottle form and spray-focused presentation.

name: loudspeaker
632.description: An audio speaker device or speaker component that projects sound. It may appear as a standalone cabinet, bookshelf speaker, floor-standing tower, subwoofer, soundbar, in-wall or car speaker, exposed speaker driver, or horn/megaphone-shaped speaker. Typical visual cues are one or more circular or oval drivers, cones, domes, grilles, or a flared horn opening mounted in a box, panel, or handheld housing.
632.guidelines: Classify as loudspeaker when the image centers on the sound-producing speaker unit itself, whether built into an enclosure or shown as an exposed driver. If a speaker is part of another device such as a radio, stereo, or TV, label only when the speaker portion is the target. Include subwoofers, PA speakers, studio monitors, soundbars, guitar/bass speaker cabinets, car speakers, and megaphones or horn speakers. Do not confuse with microphones (sound input devices, often small with mesh heads), amplifiers/receivers (control boxes with knobs and displays but no prominent speaker cone), radios/boomboxes when the whole appliance is shown, or headphones/earbuds, which are worn on the head or in the ears.

name: magnifier
633.description: A simple optical magnification device with one or more convex lenses, often mounted in a small round frame with a handle, short stem, or eyepiece. It is used close to the eye or close to the object to make small details appear larger. Common forms include handheld magnifying glasses, jeweler's loupes, and head-mounted inspection lenses.
633.guidelines: Classify as magnifier when the main object is a small lens-based viewing aid for enlarging nearby details by direct visual inspection. This category includes handheld magnifying glasses and loupes used by jewelers, watchmakers, or for reading fine print. Do not confuse it with microscopes, which are larger instrument-based devices with a stage and objective system; eyeglasses or goggles, which are worn primarily for vision correction or protection; or camera lenses, which are photographic components rather than direct viewing magnifiers. A visible single inspection lens, often round and compact, is the key cue.

name: sawmill
634.description: An industrial wood-processing facility where logs are cut into boards, beams, planks, or dimensional lumber. Typical images show stacks of rough-cut timber or logs, long straight wooden boards, band saws or circular saw machinery, conveyors, mill buildings, and sawdust-covered work areas.
634.guidelines: Classify as sawmill when the scene centers on milling timber: logs being sawn, lumber emerging from large cutting machinery, or stacks of freshly cut boards within a mill setting. Do not confuse with a lumberyard, which mainly stores and sells finished lumber without visible milling equipment; a logging site, which shows tree felling or transport in the forest; or a carpentry/woodshop, which focuses on making finished products or joinery rather than converting logs into lumber.

name: magnetic compass
635.description: A direction-finding instrument with a magnetized needle or rotating compass card that aligns with Earth’s magnetic field. It is usually circular, with marked cardinal directions and degree markings, often housed in a handheld case, pocket watch–like body, hinged lid, or surveyor-style mount.
635.guidelines: Classify as magnetic compass only when the object is a physical compass showing a freely aligning magnetic needle or compass card with N/E/S/W direction markings. It may be handheld, pocket-sized, mounted in a case, or built into field-navigation gear. Do not confuse it with a gyrocompass (larger marine/navigation instrument without a simple magnetic needle), a sundial (uses a shadow-casting gnomon), a protractor or angle gauge (measures angles but not direction), or GPS/navigation screens and map graphics that merely depict compass symbols rather than real instruments.

name: shoulder bag
636.description: A soft-sided personal carrying bag with one or two handles or a shoulder strap, typically made of leather, fabric, canvas, or synthetic material. It is usually medium-sized, opens with a zipper, flap, or clasp, and is meant to hold everyday personal items. Common forms include handbags, tote-style bags, and messenger-style bags carried by hand or over the shoulder.
636.guidelines: Classify as shoulder bag when the item is an everyday personal bag designed to be carried by hand or from the shoulder, usually with a single main compartment and soft, flexible body. Include handbags, purses, totes, and casual messenger-style bags if they fit this general use. Do not confuse with backpacks (two shoulder straps, worn on the back), briefcases or laptop cases (more rigid, office-oriented rectangular cases), duffel bags (larger cylindrical travel bags), suitcases (structured luggage), or wallets/pouches (much smaller hand-held accessories).

name: mailbox
637.description: A mailbox is a mail-receiving container or public posting box with a slot, flap, door, or front opening for letters and small parcels. It is typically box-shaped but may also be cylindrical, wall-mounted, pedestal-mounted, or roadside with a curved top. Common materials include painted metal, plastic, or wood, and many are marked with postal text, logos, numbers, flags, or collection labels.
637.guidelines: Classify as mailbox when the object is specifically designed for sending or receiving mail and has a recognizable mail slot, access door, or postal form. Include residential curbside mailboxes, wall-mounted letter boxes, and public post boxes. Do not confuse with newspaper boxes, parcel lockers, donation bins, trash cans, or storage cabinets: mailboxes are smaller and have clear mail openings and postal markings. Cylindrical pillar boxes and decorative house mailboxes still belong here if their function as a letter box is visually clear.

name: one-piece swimsuit
638.description: A close-fitting single-piece swimsuit that covers the torso in one continuous garment, usually with shoulder straps and high-cut leg openings. It may vary in neckline, back shape, and pattern, but it is designed as swimwear rather than dancewear.
638.guidelines: Classify as one-piece swimsuit when the garment is clearly a single-piece bathing suit intended for swimming or beachwear. Include fashion, athletic, vintage, and decorative variants as long as they are swimwear. Do not confuse with a leotard: leotards are similar in shape but are typically worn for dance, gymnastics, or performance and are usually shown in studio, stage, or athletic-training contexts rather than beach or pool settings. Also distinguish from bikinis or tankinis, which have separate top and bottom pieces.

name: manhole cover
640.description: A heavy metal access cover set flush into pavement, streets, or sidewalks, usually circular but sometimes square or rectangular. It is typically cast iron or steel, with raised patterns, lettering, utility labels, and sometimes decorative city or regional designs.
640.guidelines: Classify as manhole cover when the image shows a solid utility access cover or hinged lid covering an underground shaft or service opening. It may have small holes, slots, or textured patterns, but it is primarily a cover plate. Do not confuse with drainage grates or trench grates, which are open lattices of bars or many large slots designed for water flow. Also exclude storm-drain inlets, sewer grates, and other grated openings where the open grid is the main structure rather than a solid cover.

name: maraca
641.description: A handheld rattle with a bulbous hollow body and a narrow handle, usually gourd-, egg-, or pear-shaped. It is commonly made from dried calabash, wood, or plastic, often painted or decorated, and contains beads or seeds that make a rattling sound when shaken.
641.guidelines: Classify as maraca when the object is a single handheld shaker with a rounded enclosed head attached to a handle. Maracas are often shown in pairs and may be plain, painted, or carved. Do not confuse with claves or drumsticks, which are straight sticks without a hollow bulb; tambourines, which are ring-shaped with jingles; or shekeres and other gourd rattles covered with external bead netting rather than a simple handled bulb.

name: xylophone
642.description: A mallet percussion instrument with a row of tuned wooden bars arranged from low to high, usually mounted on a frame and often paired with resonators underneath. It is played by striking the bars with one or more mallets. The bars are typically rectangular wood slats in one or two staggered rows, giving a keyboard-like layout.
642.guidelines: Classify as xylophone when the instrument’s sounding bars are wooden and struck with mallets. This category includes marimba-like examples with larger wooden bars and resonators. Do not confuse with vibraphone, which has metal bars and often a pedal and motor-driven resonator fans, or with glockenspiel/metallophone, which also use metal bars. The key cue is wooden bars rather than metal bars.

name: mask
643.description: A mask is a face covering or sculpted facepiece worn over all or part of the face, or displayed as a standalone object. It may be rigid or soft and can be plain or highly decorative, with eye openings and often openings or shaping for the nose and mouth. Common forms include carnival and masquerade masks, theatrical masks, ceremonial and ritual masks, and animal or character masks made from materials such as cloth, plastic, metal, wood, feathers, beads, or paint.
643.guidelines: Classify as mask when the main object is a face covering or carved facepiece designed to conceal, decorate, or represent a face. Include both worn masks and standalone masks shown as objects. Do not confuse with face paint or makeup, where no separate covering is present; helmets or balaclavas, which are protective garments rather than masks; or full costumes where the face covering is not the main subject. Distinguish from eyeglasses and goggles by the broader face-concealing structure and decorative or representational purpose.

name: matchstick
644.description: A matchstick is a small, thin wooden stick with a colored chemical head at one end that ignites when struck or heated. It is usually shown singly or in small groups, either unlit, charred, or burning with a small flame at the tip.
644.guidelines: Classify as matchstick when the object is an individual friction match or a small set of matches: slender wooden splints with distinct match heads, often red, green, or darkened after burning. Do not confuse with candles, incense sticks, toothpicks, cotton swabs, or lighters. Unlike toothpicks or swabs, matchsticks have a chemical head; unlike candles or incense, they are short wooden sticks rather than wax or coated rods.

name: maypole
645.description: A tall upright pole, usually set outdoors, with long colorful ribbons, garlands, or streamers attached near the top and hanging down around it. People often stand in a circle holding the ribbons and dance or walk around the pole, weaving the ribbons as they move.
645.guidelines: Classify as maypole when the central object is a ceremonial pole decorated at the top with multiple long ribbons radiating downward, often with people dancing around it. Do not confuse with a flagpole, tent pole, totem pole, or utility pole: those lack the ring of many ribbons intended for weaving dance. Also distinguish it from a carousel swing ride or pole with bunting, which may have hanging elements but are not simple festive dance poles.

name: maze
646.description: A maze is a deliberately laid-out pattern of winding paths, corridors, or channels with turns, loops, and dead ends or a single circuitous route. It may be formed by trimmed hedges, low walls, stones, paving, mowed grass, crop rows, or simple painted or chalked lines on the ground, often appearing as a geometric or spiral plan viewed from above or at ground level.
646.guidelines: Classify as maze when the image shows a designed navigational path pattern meant to be walked or traced. Include hedge mazes, turf or crop mazes, stone or cobblestone labyrinths, and floor or pavement labyrinth patterns marked only by lines. Do not confuse with ordinary gardens, topiary, or landscaping that lacks a continuous path structure; with spiral or circular decorative motifs that are not walkable path layouts; or with road markings, athletic court lines, and architectural floor designs that do not form a maze-like route.

name: measuring cup
647.description: A measuring cup is a small container for measuring ingredient volume, usually made of clear glass or plastic, with a handle, a pouring spout, and printed or embossed measurement markings on the side. It often resembles a small pitcher or beaker and may be sized in cups, ounces, milliliters, or tablespoons.
647.guidelines: Classify as measuring cup when the object is a vessel specifically designed for measuring volume and has visible graduated markings. It may be glass or plastic and usually has a spout and often a handle. Do not confuse with a pitcher, jug, or ewer, which are mainly for pouring and often lack measurement scales; a mug or cup, which may have a handle but no measuring marks; or laboratory beakers and graduated cylinders, which are scientific glassware rather than kitchen measuring utensils.

name: medicine cabinet
648.description: A small wall-mounted cabinet or recessed cupboard used to store medicines and toiletries. It usually has a front door, often mirrored, and contains shallow interior shelves sized for bottles, tubes, jars, and small household items.
648.guidelines: Classify as a medicine cabinet when the object is a compact storage cabinet, typically in a bathroom, with a door and shallow shelves for personal-care or medical items. It may be recessed into the wall or mounted on the surface, and the door may be mirrored or plain wood/metal. Do not confuse it with a plain wall mirror, a larger kitchen or pantry cabinet, a bookcase, or an open shelving unit. The key cues are small cabinet form, shallow depth, bathroom-style placement, and storage for toiletries or medicines.

name: megalithic structure
649.description: A prehistoric monument or construction made from very large stones, including single standing stones, stone circles, dolmens, tomb chambers, trilithons, and other arrangements of massive upright or capped rocks. The stones are typically rough-hewn or unshaped, oversized relative to people, and set upright, stacked, or aligned in open landscapes or archaeological sites.
649.guidelines: Classify as megalithic structure when the image shows a human-made monument built from one or more very large stones intentionally erected, arranged, or balanced. This includes menhirs, dolmens, cromlechs, stone circles, and similar prehistoric stone monuments. Do not confuse with natural boulders or rock outcrops: megalithic structures show deliberate placement, upright setting, repeated alignment, capstones, gateways, chambers, or circular arrangements. Exclude ordinary masonry ruins, small stone walls, and modern sculptures unless they are clearly megalithic monuments.

name: microphone
650.description: An audio input device used to capture sound, typically with a small handheld or stand-mounted body and a prominent mesh grille or head. Common forms include cylindrical stage microphones, studio condenser microphones, and lavalier or broadcast mics, usually in black, silver, or metallic finishes and often attached to a cable, clip, stand, or shock mount.
650.guidelines: Classify as microphone when the main object is a sound-capturing mic or its recognizable body/grille, whether handheld, mounted on a stand, used for singing, speaking, recording, or broadcasting. Do not confuse with headphones, speakers, radios, or musical instruments near a performer. Distinguish it from a loudspeaker or PA speaker by the small grille-topped pickup form rather than a large sound-output box, and from a telephone handset or intercom by the lack of earpiece/listening components.

name: microwave oven
651.description: A microwave oven is a compact kitchen appliance used to heat or cook food. It is typically a box-shaped unit with a front-opening hinged door, a dark glass or mesh viewing window, and a control panel with buttons, a keypad, knobs, or a digital display on the front or side. Most are countertop models, though some are built in or mounted within cabinetry.
651.guidelines: Classify as a microwave oven when the image shows the familiar small food-heating appliance with a front door and control panel. It may be open or closed, shown in a kitchen, on a counter, or built into cabinets. Do not confuse it with a conventional oven or toaster oven, which are usually larger or have visible heating elements and rack-style interiors, or with other kitchen appliances such as dishwashers, refrigerators, or TV-like monitors. The key cues are the boxy body, front mesh window, side/front controls, and microwave-sized cooking cavity.

name: military uniform
652.description: Clothing worn by members of the armed forces, including field, service, dress, and ceremonial uniforms. Typical examples include matching jackets, trousers, helmets, berets, caps, insignia, rank markings, medals, camouflage patterns, and other standardized military-issued garments or protective wear.
652.guidelines: Classify as military uniform when the image centers on standardized armed-forces clothing or a person wearing it. This includes combat fatigues, service dress, parade uniforms, and military outerwear with clear insignia, rank, medals, or unmistakable military styling. Exclude civilian uniforms such as police, security, airline, school, or scout uniforms unless they are clearly military. Also exclude isolated gear that is not itself a uniform unless it is clearly part of military dress in context.

name: milk can
653.description: A milk can is a tall metal container for transporting or storing milk, usually cylindrical with a narrow neck, wide rim, fitted lid, and one or two side handles. It is commonly made of steel, aluminum, or sometimes copper, and may appear plain, painted, weathered, or heavily patinated.
653.guidelines: Classify as milk can when the object is the traditional metal dairy vessel with a cylindrical body, narrow top opening, lid, and carrying handles. Do not confuse it with a milk churn or butter churn, which is typically a processing vessel rather than a transport can; with watering cans, which have a spout; or with generic buckets, pails, or stock pots, which usually have wider open tops and different handle/lid designs. The classic narrowed neck, domed or fitted lid, and dairy-can form are the key cues.

name: minibus
654.description: A small bus or large van-like passenger vehicle built to carry roughly 9–30 people. It typically has a boxy, elongated body, a higher roof than a standard car, large side windows, and a single cabin volume, often with one passenger door near the front and additional side or rear access.
654.guidelines: Classify as a minibus when the vehicle is clearly a small passenger bus sized between a van and a full-size bus, with multiple rows of seats and bus-style side windows. Do not confuse it with a full-size bus, which is longer, taller, and carries many more passengers, or with a standard van/cargo van, which usually has fewer side windows and is designed mainly for goods. Many minibuses are used as shuttles, ambulances, school transport, or police vehicles; focus on the body form and passenger-carrying layout rather than the livery.

name: miniskirt
655.description: A very short skirt with a hemline ending well above the knee, often around mid-thigh or higher. It may be tight or flared, plain or pleated, and made from many fabrics, but the defining visual feature is its notably short length as a skirt garment.
