655.guidelines: Classify as a miniskirt when the garment is clearly a skirt and its hem sits far above the knee. Include pleated, fitted, A-line, denim, and fashion mini styles. Do not confuse with shorts or skorts, which have separate leg openings, or with short dresses, where the upper bodice and skirt are part of one dress. Also exclude knee-length or longer skirts; the unusually short hemline is the key cue.

name: minivan
656.description: A minivan is a passenger van with a low, car-like body, a long roofline, and a tall, boxy cabin designed to seat about 7–8 people. It typically has four side doors plus a rear liftgate, large side windows, and a spacious interior; many examples have sliding rear side doors.
656.guidelines: Classify as minivan when the vehicle is a family-oriented people carrier with a tall enclosed body, three rows of seating, and a rear hatch, often with sliding side doors. Do not confuse it with an SUV or crossover, which usually sits higher and has a more rugged two-box shape, or with a full-size van, which is taller, more utilitarian, and truck-based. Also exclude station wagons and MPVs that are lower and less spacious-looking than a true minivan.

name: missile
657.description: A missile is a long, slender rocket-shaped projectile with a pointed nose, cylindrical body, and stabilizing fins or control surfaces near the tail or mid-body. It may be shown mounted on a launcher, carried under an aircraft, displayed in a museum, or launching with exhaust and smoke. Sizes and details vary, but the overall form is a weapon-like guided rocket rather than a simple shell or unguided rocket.
657.guidelines: Classify as missile when the object is a self-propelled military projectile with the characteristic rocket body and fins, often associated with launch rails, mobile launchers, or anti-aircraft/ballistic/cruise weapon systems. Do not confuse with rockets or space launch vehicles, which are usually larger spaceflight launch systems rather than weapons; bombs, which are finned but not rocket-propelled and usually lack a long pointed rocket body; or artillery shells/projectiles, which are simpler solid rounds without prominent guidance fins and missile-launch context.

name: mitten
658.description: A mitten is a hand covering with one large compartment for the four fingers and a separate thumb section. It is usually soft and flexible, commonly knitted, woven, quilted, felted, or insulated, and may be plain or patterned in many colors and lengths.
658.guidelines: Classify as mitten when the item has a single shared section for the fingers plus a separate thumb. Annotate each mitten separately, not as a pair. Do not confuse with gloves, which have separate finger stalls for each finger, or oven mitts, which are thicker kitchen protective mitts with a stiffer, bulkier construction.

name: mixing bowl
659.description: A wide, round bowl with a broad open top and curved sides, typically deeper and larger than a cereal or soup bowl. It is made to hold and combine ingredients, and is commonly seen in glass, ceramic, metal, or plastic, often as a plain or patterned nesting set.
659.guidelines: Classify as mixing bowl when the object is a relatively large, open kitchen bowl intended for preparing or mixing ingredients. Look for a broad mouth, rounded body, and stable base, sometimes with pouring spouts or nesting sizes. Do not confuse it with a serving bowl or salad bowl, which may be shallower or styled for table use, or with a measuring cup, saucepan, or storage container, which usually have handles, lids, straighter sides, or other specialized features.

name: manufactured home
660.description: A factory-built dwelling with the proportions of a small house, typically long and rectangular with siding, windows, and a door like a permanent home. It is built on a transportable chassis and is often seen being hauled, set on blocks, or standing as a narrow single-wide or similar unit; some examples show visible wheels, axles, or trailer undercarriage.
660.guidelines: Classify as a manufactured home when the object is a transportable prefabricated residence intended as a house. It should look like a full dwelling, not a travel trailer. Distinguish it from campers, caravans, and Airstream-style trailers, which are smaller recreational vehicles with clearer towing-trailer forms and RV styling. Also distinguish it from tiny houses or site-built houses being moved: manufactured homes usually have the standardized long, narrow mobile-home form and width constraints for road transport.

name: Ford Model T
661.description: An early 20th-century Ford automobile with a tall, narrow body, upright cabin or open touring layout, thin spoked wheels, separate rounded fenders, a simple boxy hood, and vintage brass or black trim. It appears in stock antique-car form, though body styles vary from roadster and touring car to sedan, delivery, and depot-hack variants.
661.guidelines: Classify as Ford Model T only when the vehicle is recognizably a Model T or a close stock-bodied variant. Accept different factory-era body styles, but exclude modern custom hot rods, heavily modified rat rods, and generic antique cars. Distinguish it from the Ford Model A and other vintage cars by its older, taller carriage-like proportions, narrower wheels and tires, simpler upright body, and pre-1920s look. If the car has chopped roofs, oversized exposed engines, radically altered frames, or clearly custom styling, it should not be labeled Model T.

name: modem
662.description: A modem is a small network device, usually a plain box or upright unit in black, white, or gray, with status LEDs on the front or top. It commonly has labels such as Power, DSL, Cable, DS, US, Online, Internet, Link, LAN, or Ethernet, and usually only one Ethernet/LAN port plus a phone, coaxial, or cellular connection. Some versions are compact USB or cellular broadband modems for mobile internet use.
662.guidelines: Classify as modem when the device’s main role is linking a home or computer to an internet service line such as DSL, cable, fiber ONT-style broadband, or cellular data. Typical clues are ISP-style indicator lights, a single Ethernet output, and no emphasis on multiple LAN ports. Do not confuse with a router or Wi‑Fi router: routers usually have several Ethernet ports, clearer Wi‑Fi branding, and often visible antennas. Also exclude switches and hubs, which mainly have many Ethernet ports and no DSL/coax/cellular connection indicators.

name: monastery
663.description: A monastery is a religious complex centered on communal life for monks or nuns. Visually it often appears as a group of stone or stucco buildings rather than a single sanctuary, commonly including a church or chapel plus cloisters, courtyards, arcades, gardens, cells, walls, gates, and other enclosed residential or devotional spaces.
663.guidelines: Classify as monastery when the image shows a monastic complex or its identifiable parts: cloisters, enclosed courtyards, residential wings, monastery gates, or a church clearly integrated into a larger conventual enclosure. Do not confuse with a church or cathedral, which is usually just the main worship building seen alone with emphasis on the nave, facade, or steeple. Also distinguish from castles and palaces by the presence of crosses, chapels, cloisters, arcades, and religious architecture rather than defensive or royal features.

name: computer monitor
664.description: A flat-panel electronic display screen, usually rectangular and mounted on a stand, wall, or desk. It has a broad viewing surface with a thin to moderately thick bezel and is commonly used to show computer output, video, or other digital imagery.
664.guidelines: Classify as a computer monitor when the main object is a standalone display intended for viewing computer or video output. Include LCD, LED, and similar flat-panel monitors. Do not confuse with televisions: monitors are often shown on desks beside keyboards, mice, or computers and typically lack obvious TV framing or living-room context. Exclude laptops, tablets, smartphones, and all-in-one computers where the screen is integrated with another device.

name: moped
665.description: A small, lightweight two-wheeled motorized cycle with a step-through or low frame, bicycle-like proportions, a narrow saddle, small engine, and often pedals or pedal-like cranks. It is ridden astride the frame rather than with the feet together on a front platform.
665.guidelines: Classify as a moped when the vehicle is a compact motorized bike with an astride riding position and bicycle-like frame or step-through body, often with small wheels and a modest engine. Do not confuse it with a scooter, which has a flat footboard/platform in front of the rider and typically encloses more of the frame; or with a motorcycle/dirt bike, which is larger, heavier, and lacks the bicycle-like moped form. Exclude bicycles and e-bikes with no clear small-engine moped construction.

name: mortar and pestle
666.description: A mortar and pestle is a small, heavy grinding tool consisting of a thick-walled bowl and a matching club-shaped grinder. The mortar is usually round and deep or shallow with a broad rim, and the pestle is a short, blunt rod sized to fit inside for crushing and grinding. Common materials include stone, marble, ceramic, porcelain, wood, and metal.
666.guidelines: Classify as mortar and pestle when the image shows the distinctive bowl-and-grinder set, or a mortar clearly intended for use with a pestle. Do not confuse it with a regular kitchen bowl, cup, or planter, which lack the thick grinding bowl form and matching pestle; with a molcajete, which is typically a rough volcanic-stone Mexican mortar with three feet; or with a spice grinder or food processor, which are mechanical devices rather than a hand tool.

name: mortarboard
academic cap
667.description: A stiff, brimless academic cap with a flat square board mounted on top of a close-fitting skullcap, usually black and often finished with a tassel attached at the center of the square.
667.guidelines: Classify as mortarboard when the image shows the distinctive flat square top and fitted cap associated with graduation or academic dress. It may be worn on the head or shown alone, sometimes with a tassel, diploma, gown, or books. Do not confuse with other academic headwear such as a Tudor bonnet or tam, which are round and soft rather than square, or with non-academic caps and hats that lack the rigid square top.

name: mosque
668.description: An Islamic place of worship, typically a building with one or more domes, tall slender minarets, arched entrances or colonnades, and exterior decoration such as geometric tilework, stone, or stucco. Mosques range from simple modern prayer halls to large historic complexes with courtyards and multiple domes.
668.guidelines: Classify as mosque when the structure is clearly an Islamic religious building, especially if domes and minarets appear together or if Islamic architectural details such as crescents, arches, and patterned tilework are visible. Do not confuse with churches or cathedrals, which use crosses, bell towers, or spires rather than minarets; with synagogues or temples, which lack the characteristic mosque minaret-and-dome combination; or with generic domed civic buildings and palaces that may have domes but no Islamic worship architecture.

name: mosquito net
669.description: A mosquito net is a lightweight mesh canopy or enclosure made of fine translucent netting, typically white or pale-colored, used around a bed, crib, or sleeping area. It may hang loosely from a single point or frame in a conical or draped shape, or be supported by hoops or pop-up frames to form a boxy tent-like enclosure.
669.guidelines: Classify as mosquito net when the main object is a fine mesh barrier designed to surround a sleeping space and keep insects out. Common forms include hanging bed canopies, rectangular bed nets, crib nets, and pop-up mesh bed enclosures. Do not confuse with decorative bed curtains or canopy drapes made of opaque fabric: mosquito nets are sheer mesh and function as an insect screen. Also distinguish from camping tents, play tents, and laundry hampers by the thin net material, open-bottom bed-covering design, and clear association with a bed, crib, or sleeping area.

name: motor scooter
670.description: A small step-through motorcycle with a flat foot platform, a front fairing that extends down around the rider’s legs, small wheels, and a seat over the enclosed rear bodywork. It typically has a compact, rounded or streamlined body and handlebars mounted above the front shield.
670.guidelines: Classify as a motor scooter when the vehicle has a step-through frame and a rider footboard rather than a fuel tank or top tube between the legs. Distinguish it from motorcycles and mopeds by the enclosed body panels, leg shield, and flat floorboard; motorcycles usually have a straddled frame and larger exposed engine components. Do not rely on style alone: both classic Vespa-like scooters and larger modern maxi-scooters belong here if they retain the step-through scooter layout.

name: mountain bike
671.description: A bicycle built for off-road riding, typically with a sturdy frame, wide knobby tires, flat handlebars, and often front or full suspension. It usually has a more upright riding position and components designed for rough trails, rocks, dirt, and uneven terrain.
671.guidelines: Classify as mountain bike when the bicycle is clearly designed for trail or off-road use: look for thick treaded tires, flat bars, robust frame geometry, and suspension forks or rear suspension. Do not confuse with road bikes or racing bikes, which have drop handlebars and thin smooth tires; hybrid or commuter bikes, which usually have less aggressive tires and no trail-focused geometry; or BMX bikes, which are smaller, single-speed stunt bikes with 20-inch wheels.

name: camping tent
672.description: A portable fabric shelter used for camping, typically with a low freestanding or pitched structure made from flexible poles and a taut rainfly. Most examples are small dome or tunnel-style tents with sloping sides, zippered door openings, and synthetic fabric in bright or muted outdoor colors.
672.guidelines: Classify as camping tent when the image shows a portable personal shelter designed for outdoor camping. Include common backpacking, dome, tunnel, and similar recreational tents. Do not confuse with larger permanent or semi-permanent shelters such as yurts, marquees, pavilions, or military tents. Distinguish from canopy tents and gazebos by the enclosed fabric walls and sleeping-shelter form, and from tarps or bivy sacks by the clear tent body with poles creating a structured enclosure.

name: computer mouse
673.description: A small hand-operated computer pointing device, usually oval or rounded with a low domed top sized to fit the palm. It commonly has one or more top buttons, often a central scroll wheel, and may be wired or wireless. Most examples are smooth plastic in black, white, gray, or other solid colors, viewed from above, side, or underside.
673.guidelines: Classify as computer mouse when the object is a handheld pointing device for controlling a computer cursor. Include wired and wireless mice, optical and mechanical designs, and standard desktop forms. Do not confuse with a trackball, which has an exposed ball on top; a touchpad, which is flat and rectangular; a remote control, which has many buttons; or other small electronics and desk accessories. The defining cues are the palm-sized rounded body, left/right click surface, and typical mouse shape.

name: mousetrap
674.description: A small device designed to catch mice, most often a rectangular wooden, plastic, or metal base fitted with a spring-loaded snap bar, trigger plate, and bait holder. Common examples are compact and low to the ground, with exposed wire or metal parts and a simple mechanical layout.
674.guidelines: Classify as mousetrap when the image shows a dedicated mouse-catching trap, especially the classic spring snap trap with a baited trigger and snapping bar. Include different materials and brands if the object is clearly a mouse trap. Do not confuse with rat traps, which are usually larger and heavier; general animal traps such as cage traps, glue traps, or snares; or toy/novelty trap-shaped objects. The key cues are the compact size and the recognizable spring-trigger snap mechanism made specifically for mice.

name: moving van
675.description: A truck, box truck, van, or tractor-trailer used for household or office moving, typically with a large enclosed cargo body. It is often branded by a moving or storage company, and may be shown being loaded with furniture, boxes, or other personal belongings.
675.guidelines: Classify as a moving van when the vehicle is clearly intended for moving possessions, usually indicated by moving-company branding, rental moving branding, or visible household goods being loaded or carried. Do not label ordinary delivery trucks, cargo vans, panel vans, or generic box trucks as this class unless moving use is explicit or obvious. Distinguish it from a standard box truck by mover branding or moving context, and from freight semitrailers by signs that it is transporting household goods rather than commercial cargo.

name: muzzle
676.description: A muzzle is a fitted restraint worn over an animal’s snout, usually secured with straps around the head. It may be basket-like, cage-like, mesh, leather, fabric, or plastic, and typically covers the nose and mouth while leaving the eyes and rest of the head exposed.
676.guidelines: Classify as muzzle only when the image shows the wearable restraint itself or an animal wearing it. Do not confuse it with an animal’s natural muzzle or snout, which is a body part, not equipment. Also exclude collars, harnesses, halters, bridles, and face masks that do not specifically cover the mouth area to prevent biting or unwanted eating.

name: nail
677.description: A nail is a slender metal fastener with a straight shank, a pointed tip, and usually a flat or slightly rounded head. In images it is often seen hammered into or protruding from wood, sometimes rusted, bent, or partially embedded, but it retains the basic form of a simple pointed metal shaft with a head at one end.
677.guidelines: Classify as a nail when the object is a simple pointed metal fastener driven by hammering, typically with a straight shank and distinct head. Do not confuse it with screws, which have helical threads; bolts, which are thicker and used with nuts; pins or needles, which are much finer and often headless or decorative; tacks, which usually have broad flat heads and short bodies; staples, which are U-shaped; or spikes, which are much larger, heavier nails.

name: cervical collar
678.description: A rigid or semi-rigid medical brace worn around the neck to limit cervical spine movement. It appears as a foam, plastic, or padded ring or split collar that wraps closely around the neck, often white, beige, or gray, and may include chin support, front openings, Velcro straps, or molded brace panels.
678.guidelines: Classify as cervical collar when the object is a medical neck brace designed to immobilize or support the neck. Include soft foam collars and rigid emergency collars with chin/chest extensions. Do not confuse with scarves, turtlenecks, jewelry neck rings, pet cones, or decorative elongated-neck coils: a cervical collar is a supportive orthopedic/medical device with structured padding or plastic form, fitted snugly around the neck for stabilization.

name: necklace
679.description: A necklace is an item of jewelry worn around the neck. It typically consists of a chain, cord, strand of beads, or linked decorative elements, and may include pendants, gemstones, charms, or other ornamental pieces hanging at the front.
679.guidelines: Classify any neck-worn jewelry piece as a necklace if its main function is ornamenting the neck, whether it is a chain, beaded strand, pendant necklace, collar-style necklace, or multi-strand design. Do not confuse it with earrings, bracelets, anklets, or brooches. A choker can be included if it is clearly a neck necklace rather than a separate clothing collar. Exclude non-jewelry neckwear such as scarves, neckties, ribbons, or medical lanyards.

name: baby bottle nipple
680.description: A soft rubber or silicone feeding attachment for a baby bottle, typically shaped like a short rounded teat with a narrow tip and a wider flange or screw-on base. It is usually translucent, white, yellow, or colored, and may appear alone or mounted on an infant feeding bottle.
680.guidelines: Classify as baby bottle nipple when the image shows the teat-like sucking piece used on infant bottles, either by itself or attached to a baby bottle. Do not confuse it with a pacifier, which usually has a larger shield and handle for soothing rather than feeding; a medicine dropper or pipette, which is longer and more tube-like; or an animal teat/nipple, which is part of a body rather than a detachable bottle accessory.

name: laptop
681.description: A portable clamshell personal computer with a hinged screen attached to a flat base that contains the keyboard and built-in electronics. It is typically thin and rectangular, opens and closes like a book, and may vary from small netbook-sized models to larger notebooks. Common appearances include dark or silver plastic or metal bodies, a trackpad below the keyboard, and use either on a desk or on a person's lap.
681.guidelines: Classify as laptop when the device is a single foldable computer with an integrated screen and keyboard joined by a hinge. Include notebooks and netbooks. Do not confuse with desktop computers, which have separate monitors and keyboards; tablets, which lack a built-in physical keyboard in the same clamshell body; or detachable 2-in-1 devices when the keyboard is clearly separate. Ignore surrounding accessories such as external mice, monitors, or docking setups if the main object is still the hinged portable computer.

name: obelisk
682.description: A tall, slender stone monument with four flat sides that taper slightly upward to a pointed pyramidal tip, often set on a pedestal or base. Many examples are plain, while others bear carved inscriptions or reliefs, especially in the Egyptian style.
682.guidelines: Classify as an obelisk when the structure is a freestanding, tapering four-sided pillar with a pyramidal top. Do not confuse it with columns or pillars, which usually have cylindrical shafts or capitals; spires or steeples, which are parts of buildings; pyramids, which are broad-based solid monuments; or clock towers and skyscrapers, which have openings, floors, or architectural detailing. The key cues are the monolithic shaft, slight taper, square cross-section, and pointed pyramidion.

name: oboe
683.description: A slender woodwind instrument with a straight, narrow tube, a small flared bell, many metal keys along the body, and a short exposed double reed at the top rather than a separate mouthpiece. It is usually black or dark brown with silver-colored keywork, though some examples are wooden throughout.
683.guidelines: Classify as an oboe when the instrument is a straight, narrow double-reed woodwind with dense metal keywork and a small bell. Distinguish it from a clarinet, which uses a single reed with a mouthpiece and usually has a larger mouthpiece section; from a recorder or shawm, which has finger holes and little or no modern keywork; and from a bassoon or English horn, which are larger and differently shaped. The visible double reed and compact straight body are the main cues.

name: ocarina
684.description: A small vessel flute with a hollow enclosed body, usually oval, teardrop-shaped, or slightly animal-like, with a short protruding mouthpiece and several round finger holes on the top and sometimes underside. It is commonly made of ceramic, clay, plastic, or wood and often has a smooth, polished surface.
684.guidelines: Classify as ocarina when the object is a handheld enclosed flute with a bulbous body, a distinct blow mouthpiece, and multiple finger holes. Do not confuse it with recorders, tin whistles, or other tubular flutes, which are long pipe-shaped instruments rather than enclosed vessels. Also exclude decorative pottery or whistle-like toys unless they clearly have the characteristic vessel-flute form and playing holes of an ocarina.

name: odometer
685.description: A vehicle dashboard distance counter, usually shown as a small numeric display or row of rolling digits within or near the instrument cluster. It reports total distance traveled, and may also include a trip reading, but it is separate from the main speedometer dial and does not indicate current speed.
685.guidelines: Classify as odometer when the image focuses on the mileage/trip counter display—the numbers showing accumulated distance traveled on a vehicle dashboard. It may appear as mechanical rolling digits or a small digital window inside the gauge cluster. Do not confuse it with a speedometer, which is the large dial with a needle and speed markings (mph or km/h), or with a tachometer, fuel gauge, or other dashboard instruments. If the main visible subject is the speed dial rather than the mileage readout, it should not be labeled as odometer.

name: oil filter
686.description: An automotive oil filter: a small replaceable engine part, usually cylindrical and compact. It may appear as a sealed metal spin-on canister with a threaded opening and ring of inlet holes on one end, or as a pleated cartridge element made of folded paper or fabric, often tan, brown, black, or white. The defining feature is a filter body or pleated insert designed to trap contaminants from engine oil.
686.guidelines: Classify as an oil filter when the object is specifically an engine oil filtration component, either a spin-on canister or an oil-filter cartridge. Common look-alikes include air filters, fuel filters, and hydraulic filters. Distinguish it from air filters by the smaller, denser form and automotive oil-system context rather than large flat panels or intake housings; from fuel filters by the absence of hose nozzles and the typical threaded base or cartridge core; and from generic machine filters by labels, packaging, or installation context indicating engine oil use.

name: pipe organ
687.description: A large keyboard musical instrument identified visually by its arrays of vertical metal or wooden pipes mounted in an architectural case, often built into a church, concert hall, or balcony. The facade usually shows many tall, parallel pipes of different lengths arranged symmetrically, often with ornate woodwork, gilding, towers, and decorative panels around a console and wind chest.
687.guidelines: Classify as pipe organ when the image shows a permanent organ installation with multiple visible organ pipes arranged in ranks or decorative towers. Typical settings are churches, cathedrals, chapels, and concert halls. Do not confuse with a theater organ or electronic organ, which may have keyboards but no large exposed pipe arrays, or with other pipe instruments such as panpipes or calliopes, which are much smaller and not architectural installations. The key cue is a monumental, built-in instrument dominated by many vertical pipes.

name: oscilloscope
688.description: An oscilloscope is an electronic test instrument with a boxy benchtop form, a front-panel display, many knobs and buttons, and input connectors for probes. The screen is typically overlaid with a measurement grid and often shows one or more waveform traces representing electrical signals.
688.guidelines: Classify as an oscilloscope when the device is clearly a waveform-viewing electronic instrument with probe inputs and a gridded display for signal traces. It may be analog or digital, with a CRT, LCD, or simulated on-screen display. Do not confuse it with spectrum analyzers, logic analyzers, signal generators, multimeters, or generic monitors: oscilloscopes are identified by their time-varying waveform display, vertical/horizontal control layout, and front-panel probe connectors.

name: overskirt
689.description: An overskirt is an extra outer skirt layer worn over an underlying skirt, petticoat, or dress. It may be attached or removable, and is typically shorter, open-front, draped, split, or otherwise styled to reveal the layer beneath.
689.guidelines: Classify as overskirt when the defining garment is a secondary skirt layer clearly worn over another skirt or dress. The key cue is visible layering: an outer skirt panel, apron-like layer, bustle-like drape, or split skirt that exposes an underskirt. Do not confuse with a regular skirt or dress, which lacks a distinct outer overlayer, or with an apron, which is usually a protective front panel rather than a decorative skirt layer integrated into the outfit. Also distinguish from petticoats and underskirts, which are worn underneath rather than over the main skirt.

name: oxcart
690.description: A simple two- or four-wheeled cart or wagon designed to be pulled by one or more oxen, typically attached by a wooden yoke. It is usually an open flatbed, platform, or box-like cart made largely of wood, sometimes with metal wheels or fittings, and may carry people, crops, hay, tools, or other loads.
690.guidelines: Classify as an oxcart when the image shows a cart or wagon specifically drawn by oxen or cattle yoked to it. The oxen may be in front, beside the shaft, or partially out of frame, but the cart-and-ox draft setup should be evident. Do not confuse with horse-drawn carts, donkey carts, buffalo carts, or generic wagons without visible oxen. Distinguishing cues are the bovine draft animals, usually with horns and a neck yoke, pulling a simple rural cart.

name: oxygen mask
691.description: A mask that fits over the nose and mouth, typically made of clear plastic or rubber, and connected to a tube, hose, bag, or valve that delivers oxygen or another breathable gas. It is usually cup-shaped or contoured to the face and secured with straps or elastic.
691.guidelines: Classify as oxygen mask when the main object is a face mask specifically used to supply oxygen or breathable air through tubing or an attached breathing system. It may appear in medical, aviation, diving, firefighting, or emergency equipment contexts. Do not confuse with a gas mask or respirator: those usually emphasize filtration canisters or filter cartridges rather than oxygen delivery tubing. Also exclude simple surgical masks or dust masks, which cover the face but are not connected to an oxygen supply.

name: packet
692.description: A packet is a small, usually thin, lightweight container made of paper, plastic, foil, or laminated film, typically sealed on all sides and sized to hold a small portion of goods. It often appears as a flat sachet, pouch, sleeve, or small wrapped bundle for items such as food, seeds, sugar, medicine, tobacco, or other single-use portions.
692.guidelines: Classify as packet when the item is primarily a small sealed wrapper or pouch intended to contain a modest quantity of product, often disposable after opening. Include sachets, small food wrappers, seed packets, sugar packets, and cigarette packets. Do not confuse with boxes, cartons, bags, envelopes, or bottles: packets are usually smaller, thinner, and more flexible, though some cigarette packets may be box-like. Exclude larger shopping bags or shipping mailers unless the object is clearly a small retail packet.

name: paddle
693.description: A paddle is a hand-held implement used to propel or steer small watercraft. It has a long shaft with a broad flat blade at one end, or blades at both ends in a kayak paddle; blades may be oval, rectangular, spooned, or pointed, and are commonly made of wood, plastic, fiberglass, or metal.
693.guidelines: Classify as paddle when the defining object is a hand-held boating implement with one or two broad blades attached directly to a shaft and used without rowlocks. Includes canoe paddles, kayak paddles, gondola paddles, and similar boat paddles. Do not confuse with an oar, which is usually longer, used in pairs, and pivoted in oarlocks; or with a pole, which lacks a broad blade; or with a shovel/spatula-like tool used on land rather than for paddling watercraft.

name: paddle wheel
694.description: A large wheel fitted around its rim with broad flat paddles or blades, usually mounted on the side or stern of a boat. It has a spoked or trussed circular frame, often metal or painted wood, and is shown partly submerged or splashing water as it rotates to propel the vessel.
694.guidelines: Classify images as paddle wheel when the defining object is a boat-mounted wheel with multiple flat paddles attached around the circumference for water propulsion. Do not confuse it with a water wheel, which is typically a stationary mill wheel beside a stream or building, or with a turbine/propeller, which has fewer blade-like vanes rather than many rim-mounted paddles. The wheel should be clearly associated with a vessel or marine propulsion context.

name: padlock
695.description: A portable lock with a solid body and a curved metal shackle that opens and closes to fasten through a hasp, chain, zipper, or similar fixture. Usually made of metal, it may be brass, steel, painted, or laminated, and often has a keyway, combination dials, or other unlocking mechanism on the body.
695.guidelines: Classify as padlock only when the object is a detachable lock with a visible shackle and compact lock body. Include keyed, combination, laminated, weatherproof, decorative, and miniature padlocks. Do not confuse with door locks, deadbolts, knob locks, or latch hardware that are built into a door, nor with handcuffs, carabiners, or plain shackles that lack a lock body. The defining cue is the self-contained lock body plus U-shaped shackle designed to secure external items.

name: brush
696.description: A brush is a handheld tool with a handle or ferrule supporting a cluster of bristles, hairs, or synthetic filaments at one end. The bristle head may be flat, round, tapered, fan-shaped, or fluffy, and can range from stiff to very soft depending on use. Common examples in this category include paintbrushes and cosmetic brushes.
696.guidelines: Classify as this category when the object’s defining feature is a bristled head attached to a handle, used to apply, spread, dust, or sweep material. Include artist’s brushes, house-paint brushes, and makeup brushes. Do not confuse with pens, pencils, markers, or styluses, which have solid tips rather than bristles; combs, which have rigid teeth; brooms and mops, which are much larger cleaning tools; or rollers and spatulas, which lack a tuft of bristles.

name: pajamas
697.description: Sleepwear consisting of a matching top and bottom, typically made of soft fabric. Common forms include long-sleeved or short-sleeved shirts with long pants, shorts, or footed bottoms; they are often loose-fitting and may be plain or printed with playful patterns.
697.guidelines: Classify as pajamas when the clothing is clearly a sleepwear set or one-piece sleep garment meant for bed or lounging. Include matching two-piece pajama sets and footed sleepers commonly referred to as pajamas. Do not confuse with robes or bathrobes, which are open-front wrap garments; nightgowns or nightshirts, which are single-piece sleep garments without separate pants; jumpsuits or rompers worn as daywear; or regular loungewear/sweats, which may look similar but are not clearly sleepwear. The key cue is coordinated sleep clothing, usually soft, loose, and bed-oriented.

name: palace
698.description: A grand, highly ornate monumental residence associated with royalty, nobility, or state power. Palaces are typically large formal buildings with refined facades, broad windows, elaborate interiors, domes, colonnades, decorated halls, courtyards, or ceremonial entrances, and they generally emphasize luxury and display rather than military defense.
698.guidelines: Classify as palace when the main subject is a monumental royal or ceremonial residence with elegant, decorative architecture. Include former royal residences and palace complexes even if partly castle-like. Do not confuse with castles: castles usually show clear defensive features such as battlements, thick fortified walls, towers, moats, or narrow openings. Do not confuse with government buildings, capitols, museums, mansions, hotels, or temples; those may be grand, but they are not primarily palatial residences. If the structure looks fortified and defensive, prefer castle; if it looks formal, expansive, and luxurious with little or no fortification, prefer palace.

name: pan flute
699.description: A wind instrument made of a row of hollow tubes of gradually different lengths, usually bamboo or cane, bound or glued side by side in a straight or curved arrangement. The pipes are open at the top and closed at the bottom, forming a stepped outline from short to long tubes.
699.guidelines: Classify as a pan flute when the object is a bundle of many parallel pipes of different lengths played by blowing across their top openings. Do not confuse it with a flute, recorder, or fipple flute, which are single tubes with finger holes, or with bagpipe pipes, organ pipes, or decorative bamboo bundles. The defining cue is multiple attached tubes arranged in ascending or descending length.

name: paper towel
700.description: A roll or sheet of absorbent paper used for cleaning, typically white and thicker, stronger, and more textured than toilet paper. It usually appears as a large cylindrical roll on a holder or in a dispenser, with perforated tear-off sheets and an embossed surface pattern.
700.guidelines: Classify as paper towel when the item is an absorbent cleaning paper product, usually sold or used in larger rolls with thicker, sturdier sheets. Do not confuse with toilet paper, which is usually softer, narrower, and less robust; napkins or paper hand towels, which are commonly folded into stacks rather than wound on rolls; or tissues, which are thinner and dispensed from boxes.

name: parachute
701.description: A parachute is a fabric canopy used to slow descent through the air. It is usually seen as a large suspended canopy with many thin lines attached to a harness or load below. In these images, most are modern ram-air parachutes with a rectangular or slightly curved inflated wing made of colored fabric cells, though some round canopies also appear.
701.guidelines: Classify as parachute when the main object is a deployed descent canopy attached by suspension lines to a person or payload. Look for a skydiver or hanging load beneath the canopy and the characteristic network of lines. Do not confuse with a paraglider, which has a longer, smoother airfoil wing and is usually flown horizontally rather than descending vertically; a parasail, which is typically towed behind a boat; or a kite, which has no suspended person in a harness below. Hot-air balloons and parachute-like advertising inflatables lack the skydiving harness-and-lines setup.

name: parallel bars
702.description: Two straight horizontal bars of equal height running parallel to each other, supported by upright posts. They are typically metal and spaced so a person can support themselves between them, most often for gymnastics, exercise, or rehabilitation walking practice.
702.guidelines: Classify as parallel bars when the image shows a matched pair of side-by-side horizontal bars intended to be used together. Include gymnastics parallel bars and rehabilitation/physical therapy walking bars. Do not confuse with uneven bars (two bars at different heights), a single horizontal bar/high bar, ballet barres mounted along a wall, handrails, or playground/climbing structures that are not a distinct parallel pair for supported movement.

name: park bench
703.description: A long outdoor bench for multiple people, typically with a slatted wooden or metal seat and backrest, supported by legs or side frames, often with armrests. It is usually freestanding and placed along paths, sidewalks, gardens, plazas, or lawns; despite the name, it does not have to be located in a park.
703.guidelines: Classify as park bench when the image shows an outdoor seating bench meant for public or garden use, usually a long slatted bench with a backrest. Include straight or slightly curved versions and benches made of wood, metal, or composite materials. Do not confuse with picnic tables (which include a table), bleachers (tiered rows), sofas or indoor benches, porch swings, or single-seat chairs. If the object is primarily a standalone outdoor multi-person bench rather than another kind of seating structure, it belongs here.

name: parking meter
704.description: A parking meter is a curbside device used to collect payment or display time status for a single parking space or a small pair of spaces. It is typically a narrow metal post or pedestal topped with a rounded or hooded head, often with a coin slot, digital display, dial, button panel, or small door on the front. Common colors are gray, black, blue, or green, and many are installed directly beside parked cars along a street.
704.guidelines: Classify as parking meter only when the image shows the dedicated street-side parking payment/time device itself, usually mounted on a post next to a parking space. Do not confuse it with a multi-space parking pay station or parking kiosk, which is larger and serves many spaces; parking signs, which are flat signs without a meter head or payment mechanism; gas pumps, which are much larger fueling devices; or utility meters such as water, gas, or electric meters, which are attached to buildings and lack the characteristic curbside single-space form.

name: railroad passenger car
705.description: A non-powered railway vehicle built to carry passengers. It is a long railcar with steel or painted sides, rows of windows along the body, doors at the ends or sides, and a full passenger interior such as seats, aisles, or compartments. It may appear as a coach, lounge car, or similar passenger carriage, but it is not the locomotive.
705.guidelines: Classify as this category when the image shows an individual passenger-carrying railway car or its interior. Include coaches, carriages, and other passenger cars coupled into a train. Do not confuse with locomotives, which have driving cabs, engines, pantographs, or a distinct powered front; freight cars, which lack passenger windows and seating; cabooses, which are short crew cars often with a cupola; or buses and street vehicles, which do not run on railway tracks.

name: patio
706.description: An outdoor living or sitting area adjoining a house, restaurant, or other building, typically with a flat floor of concrete, stone, tile, brick, or wood. It is usually open to the sky or lightly covered, and often contains outdoor furniture, planters, railings, columns, or nearby garden landscaping.
706.guidelines: Classify as patio when the image centers on a ground-level or slightly raised outdoor area used for sitting, dining, or relaxing next to a building. Common look-alikes include porch, veranda, deck, balcony, and courtyard. A porch or veranda is more clearly roofed and architecturally part of the building facade; a deck is usually a distinctly raised wooden platform; a balcony projects from an upper story; a courtyard is more enclosed by surrounding walls or buildings. Use patio for the broader outdoor terrace-like space itself, especially when furnished and directly connected to a home or restaurant.

name: payphone
707.description: A public telephone installed in a booth, wall unit, or freestanding station, typically with a handset attached by a cord and a keypad or rotary dial, plus a coin slot, card reader, or payment panel.
707.guidelines: Classify as payphone only when the image shows a public pay telephone meant for shared use, usually fixed in place and equipped for paid calls. It may be enclosed in a booth or mounted openly on a wall or pedestal. Do not confuse it with ordinary landline telephones, office or hotel lobby phones, intercoms, emergency call boxes, parking meters, ticket machines, vending machines, or phone booths without a visible telephone unit. The key cues are the attached handset and the public payment/control hardware.

name: pedestal
708.description: A pedestal is a supporting base beneath a statue, monument, column, shrine element, or other upright object. It is typically a solid raised structure of stone, concrete, metal, or masonry, often blocklike, tapered, or columnar, and may be plain or ornamented with carvings, inscriptions, moldings, or stepped sides.
708.guidelines: Classify as pedestal when the main visible subject is the support or base that elevates another object or architectural element. Include statue bases, monument plinths, and column supports. Do not confuse it with the statue or column itself: the pedestal is the lower supporting part, usually broader and more massive. Exclude standalone statues, obelisks, memorial columns, gravestones, and buildings unless the image clearly centers on their base/support structure.

name: pencil case
709.description: A small container for holding pencils, pens, erasers, and other stationery. It is usually narrow and portable, commonly made of fabric, plastic, metal, or vinyl, and may be soft and zippered like a pouch or rigid with a hinged lid. Typical forms are rectangular, cylindrical, or wedge-shaped, often with decorative prints or school-themed designs.
709.guidelines: Classify as pencil case when the item is a stationery holder sized for writing tools. Include both soft zip pouches and hard pencil boxes. Do not confuse with a cosmetic bag or toiletry pouch, which is usually larger and less specifically shaped for pens; an eyeglass case, which is typically a rigid clamshell sized for one pair of glasses; a wallet or coin purse, which is flatter and organized for money/cards; or a lunchbox/storage box, which is larger and meant for food or general storage.

name: pencil sharpener
710.description: A small handheld or desk-mounted tool for sharpening pencils by shaving away the wood around the graphite core. Common forms include compact metal blocks with one or two tapered holes and an exposed blade, plastic sharpeners with shavings containers, and larger crank-operated desktop models.
710.guidelines: Classify as pencil sharpener when the object’s primary purpose is to sharpen pencils and it has a pencil-entry hole leading to a cutting blade or rotary shaving mechanism. Include handheld wedge-shaped sharpeners, container sharpeners, and crank sharpeners. Do not confuse with erasers, hole punches, staplers, or other small desk tools. A pencil sharpener is distinguished by the conical pencil hole, visible blade or cutter, and often pencil shavings nearby.

name: perfume
711.description: A fragrance product typically sold in a small decorative bottle or spray flacon, often made of glass and paired with branded packaging. Bottles vary widely in shape, color, and cap design, but are usually compact, polished, and intended for personal scent application.
711.guidelines: Classify as perfume when the image shows a fragrance bottle, atomizer, or retail perfume packaging for personal scent. Include both men's and women's fragrances and designer cologne-style bottles. Do not confuse with essential oils, cosmetics, shampoo, lotion, or other toiletries: perfume packaging is usually a single fragrance bottle with a stopper or spray top, often with luxury branding. Exclude bottles whose primary purpose is medicinal, culinary, or general household liquid storage.

name: Petri dish
712.description: A shallow, round, transparent dish with a flat base and low vertical sides, usually made of clear glass or plastic and often shown with a slightly larger loose-fitting lid. It is commonly seen empty or containing agar, microbial colonies, seeds, samples, or small experimental materials.
712.guidelines: Classify as Petri dish when the image shows the characteristic shallow circular culture dish used in laboratories, typically clear and paired with a lid. Do not confuse it with deeper food containers, bowls, jars, beakers, or test tubes. Unlike a microscope slide, it is round and lidded; unlike a culture flask or specimen cup, it is very shallow and wide.

name: printer
713.description: A printer is an office or desktop machine that outputs documents or images onto paper. It is usually a boxy device in white, gray, or black plastic, often with a paper tray, output slot, control panel, and sometimes a flatbed scanner lid or automatic document feeder on top. The class includes standalone printers as well as larger copier-style and multifunction printer units.
713.guidelines: Classify as a printer when the main object is a machine for printing onto paper, including multifunction printer/copier devices. It may have scanner or copier features, but the overall device should be a printer-sized or copier-sized paper-output machine. Do not confuse with a standalone scanner, which is usually flatter and centered on a glass scan bed without prominent paper trays or output bins; a fax machine, which is typically smaller and organized around telephone-style document feeding; or a plotter, which is usually much wider and designed for roll media or large-format printing.

name: guitar pick
plectrum
714.description: A small, thin plate used to pluck stringed instruments, most often guitar strings. It is typically flat and rigid or slightly flexible, with a rounded triangular or teardrop outline, smooth faces, and a pointed or rounded tip. Common materials include plastic, nylon, celluloid, metal, wood, felt, or other composites, and picks often have printed logos, text, or textured grip areas.
714.guidelines: Classify only handheld string-plucking picks: small, flat plectra meant to strike strings. Typical examples are guitar picks shown alone, in a hand, or resting on guitar strings. Do not confuse with larger medieval-style plectrums, thumb picks or finger picks that wrap around the finger, or drumsticks and other music accessories. Also exclude unrelated small flat objects such as plastic tabs, chips, badges, or tokens; this category is defined by the characteristic pick shape and its use with stringed instruments.

name: Pickelhaube
715.description: A rigid German spiked helmet with a rounded crown, short brim, and a tall pointed spike mounted on top. It is typically made of dark leather or metal, often glossy black, and may carry a front plate, cockades, chin strap, and metal trim in brass or silver.
715.guidelines: Classify as Pickelhaube when the helmet has the distinctive central top spike and the formal 19th- to early-20th-century German military style. Do not confuse it with other spiked helmets or parade helmets: the Pickelhaube usually has a smooth domed body, front visor and rear neck guard, and German imperial insignia. Exclude modern combat helmets, pith helmets, shakos, and helmets with plumes instead of a fixed spike.

name: picket fence
716.description: A fence made of a row of narrow, evenly spaced vertical wooden slats or pickets attached to horizontal rails, typically painted white. The pickets often have pointed, rounded, or decorative tops, and the fence is usually low and used around yards, gardens, or house fronts.
716.guidelines: Classify as picket fence when the defining structure is a low fence of repeated vertical pickets with gaps between them. Include common variations in picket-top shape and paint condition. Do not confuse with privacy fences or stockade fences, which have closely packed boards with little or no spacing, or with split-rail, post-and-rail, chain-link, or wrought-iron fences, which use different construction and materials. 'Paling' can overlap, but this class is specifically the classic picket-style fence.

name: pickup truck
717.description: A pickup truck is a road vehicle with an enclosed passenger cab and a separate open cargo bed behind it. It typically has a boxy front, upright stance, medium to large wheels, and a rear bed with low side walls and a tailgate. Examples range from modern full-size trucks to older classic models, but the defining feature is the combination of cab plus open rear load bed.
717.guidelines: Classify as a pickup truck when the vehicle clearly has a passenger cab in front and an open cargo bed behind it. Include both modern and vintage pickups, extended-cab and regular-cab models, and customized trucks, as long as the rear bed is present. Do not confuse with flatbed trucks or stake trucks, which have a commercial cargo platform rather than a standard pickup bed; SUVs or vans, which have an enclosed rear body instead of an open bed; or large lorries/semi-trucks, which are much bigger commercial vehicles with separate trailers or heavy-duty cargo bodies.

name: pier
718.description: A pier is a raised platform or walkway that projects from the shore out over water, typically supported by piles, posts, or columns. It is usually long and narrow, with a flat deck of wood, concrete, or similar material, and may include railings, mooring posts, shelters, or boats alongside it.
718.guidelines: Classify as pier when the main structure is an elevated deck extending out over the water on supports, allowing access above the water surface. Do not confuse with a breakwater, which is a low solid barrier built to block waves and is often broader, rock- or concrete-built, and not primarily an elevated walkway on piles. Also distinguish from docks or floating pontoons, which are often lower, modular, or floating rather than clearly pile-supported structures projecting from shore.

name: piggy bank
719.description: A pig-shaped coin bank, usually a small hollow container with a coin slot on top or along the back. It typically has a rounded body, short legs, a snout, pointed ears, and a simplified cartoon-like pig face. Common materials include ceramic, porcelain, plastic, or metal, and colors vary widely, though pink is especially common.
719.guidelines: Classify as piggy bank only when the object is clearly a coin bank shaped like a pig, typically showing a money slot and pig features such as snout, ears, and stubby legs. Do not confuse it with toy pigs, pig figurines, or plush pigs that lack a coin slot or banking function. Also exclude non-pig coin banks shaped like other animals or objects, and real pigs or pig sculptures not intended for holding coins.

name: prescription pill bottle
720.description: A small cylindrical medicine container, usually translucent amber or orange plastic, with a white child-resistant screw cap. It is typically used to hold tablets or capsules and often has a printed pharmacy label with dosage or warning text.
720.guidelines: Classify as prescription pill bottle when the image shows the plastic medication container itself, especially the standard amber pharmacy vial with a safety cap. Do not confuse it with loose pills or capsules alone, vitamin/supplement bottles that are larger retail containers, glass medicine bottles, or other storage jars. The key cues are the small pharmacy-style vial shape, orange/amber translucent plastic, and child-proof cap with prescription labeling.

name: pillow
721.description: A soft fabric-filled support cushion, usually sewn as a square, rectangular, or sometimes round pad. It typically has a smooth or textured cloth cover and appears plump, compressible, and lightly bulging at the center, with many examples showing decorative prints, patchwork, embroidery, or patterned upholstery fabric.
721.guidelines: Classify as pillow when the object is a soft stuffed pad intended to support the head or body or serve as a decorative cushion. Include bed pillows and throw pillows in varied shapes and fabrics. Do not confuse with mattresses, cushions that are clearly part of fixed furniture, folded blankets, or beanbags. The key cue is a standalone, fabric-covered, padded form that looks soft and compressible, usually with stitched edges and a pillow-like silhouette.

name: table tennis ball
722.description: A small, lightweight, hollow plastic ball used in table tennis, typically white or orange with a smooth matte surface and a nearly perfect spherical shape.
722.guidelines: Classify as a table tennis ball when the object is the small plastic ball used for table tennis, usually seen with paddles and a table or sold in packs. Do not confuse it with larger balls such as golf balls (dimpled), beer pong balls (similar but usually in cup-game contexts), or toy balls. The key cues are very small size, smooth untextured surface, and the white or orange ball commonly used in table tennis.

name: pinwheel
723.description: A small wind-driven toy made from several folded or curved vanes arranged around a central pin on a stick. It is usually brightly colored, often made of paper or plastic, and forms a flower- or star-like rotor that spins freely when blown by wind or breath.
723.guidelines: Classify as pinwheel when the object is a handheld or mounted toy with multiple blades attached to a central hub and stick, designed to spin in moving air. Do not confuse it with a wind turbine or windmill, which are much larger mechanical structures, or with a fan, propeller, or flower decoration that may look similar but is not a toy pinwheel on a stick.

name: pitcher
725.description: A pitcher is a handled vessel for pouring liquids, typically with an open top and a pronounced spout or pinched rim. It may be made of ceramic, glass, or metal, and ranges from small cream pitchers to larger water or beverage jugs, but it keeps the same basic form: a container with one main handle and a pouring lip.
725.guidelines: Classify as pitcher when the object is an open pouring vessel with a handle and clear spout or pouring rim. Include creamers, jugs, and ewers used for serving liquids if their main form is a handled pourer. Do not confuse with a teapot, which usually has a lid and a side spout; a watering can, which has a long narrow spout for plants; a vase, which lacks a pouring spout and is meant for flowers; or a mug/cup, which is primarily for drinking rather than pouring.

name: woodworking hand plane
726.description: A woodworking hand tool with a long, flat sole and a body of wood or metal, fitted with an angled blade that shaves thin layers from wood. Most examples have a front knob and rear handle or a simple wooden body, and are used by pushing the tool along the wood surface.
726.guidelines: Classify as a woodworking hand plane when the object is a manual planing tool with a flat base and exposed or partially enclosed cutting iron for smoothing, trimming, or shaping wood. Do not confuse it with a spokeshave, which is smaller and meant for curved work with side handles, or with a scraper plane, block plane, or powered planer unless the broader hand-plane form is still clearly shown. The key cues are the elongated flat sole, blade set into the body, and hand-pushed woodworking design.

name: planetarium
727.description: A planetarium is typically a large domed building or theater designed for astronomy shows. Visually it is most often identified by a prominent hemispherical dome, sometimes smooth, ribbed, perforated, mirrored, or geodesic, usually mounted on a low circular or cylindrical base or attached to a larger public building. Many examples have glass-fronted entrances, ring-shaped lower levels, ramps, or institutional architecture associated with museums or science centers.
727.guidelines: Classify as planetarium when the structure’s defining feature is an astronomy-style projection dome or a building clearly identified as a planetarium. Include both classic standalone dome theaters and modern spherical or dome-clad planetarium buildings. Do not confuse with observatories: observatories usually have telescope housings with slit openings or retractable roofs rather than a public theater-like dome. Do not confuse with capitol domes, sports arenas, or generic domed auditoriums, which lack the distinctive science-museum/astronomy context. Geodesic domes, mirrored spheres, and exhibition domes count only when they are specifically planetarium buildings rather than decorative sculptures or other dome structures.

name: plastic shopping bag
728.description: A thin, flexible, lightweight bag made of plastic film, usually with an open top and loop or cutout handles, used for carrying or storing items. It is often translucent or opaque, crinkled, and may be plain or printed with logos or text.
728.guidelines: Classify as plastic shopping bag when the image shows a disposable or reusable carry bag made from thin plastic film. Common look-alikes include trash bags, zip-top storage bags, paper bags, and cloth tote bags. Distinguish it from trash bags by the typical retail-bag shape with handles and a smaller carry size; from zip bags by the lack of a sealing strip; from paper bags by the glossy or translucent plastic material; and from tote bags by the thin crinkly film rather than woven fabric.

name: plate rack
729.description: A rack or stand designed to hold plates upright in individual vertical slots. It is typically made of wood, wire, or plastic, mounted on a wall, set on a countertop, or built into a cabinet, and often also holds other dishes such as cups or bowls.
729.guidelines: Classify as plate rack when the defining feature is a series of narrow vertical dividers or grooves that store plates on edge. Include wall-mounted dish racks, cabinet-integrated plate holders, and decorative open shelving made specifically for plates. Do not confuse with a dish drainer or drying rack, which is mainly for drying washed dishes near a sink and often includes trays or mixed utensil compartments, or with a general shelf/cabinet that merely displays plates without clear plate-separating slots.

name: plow
730.description: A farm implement used to cut, lift, and turn soil, typically with one or more curved blades or moldboards mounted on a metal frame. It is often long and narrow, may have wheels or handles, and can be pulled by animals or attached to a tractor.
730.guidelines: Classify as plow when the implement is designed to break and turn soil with distinct plow bottoms, shares, or moldboards. Do not confuse it with a harrow or disc harrow, which has many exposed discs or tines for breaking up soil rather than turning furrows; a cultivator, which usually has multiple lighter tines; or a shovel/spade, which is a hand tool. The key cue is a heavy soil-turning blade assembly meant to open and invert the earth.

name: plunger
731.description: A plunger is a handheld cleaning tool with a long straight handle attached to a flexible rubber suction cup or bell-shaped head, most often red, black, or dark blue. The head is usually round, domed, or accordion-like and is designed to seal over a drain opening or toilet outlet.
731.guidelines: Classify as plunger when the object is a drain-unclogging tool with a handle and a rubber suction head. Include both sink-style cup plungers and toilet plungers with deeper or flanged bell shapes. Do not confuse with a toilet brush, which has bristles instead of a solid rubber cup; a suction cup toy or dart, which lacks the long handle and drain-cleaning purpose; or a mace, bat, or pole, which may have a shaft but no rubber suction head.

name: Polaroid camera
732.description: A camera made by Polaroid, typically a boxy instant camera with a prominent front lens, built-in flash or flash bar area, and often a folding or pop-up body. Examples include classic Polaroid Land Cameras, OneStep/Sun models, Spectra models, and other vintage Polaroid instant-camera designs in black, gray, white, or brown plastic or metal bodies.
732.guidelines: Classify as this category only when the camera itself is a Polaroid-branded camera or a well-known Polaroid camera design. It may be rigid, folding, or bellows-style, but it should be the camera, not just film, packaging, or accessories. Do not confuse with other vintage cameras, SLRs, rangefinders, or Kodak/Fujifilm instant cameras; Polaroid cameras usually have a distinctive boxy instant-camera form, front flash module, and often visible Polaroid branding or characteristic Land Camera / OneStep-style construction.

name: pole
733.description: A tall, slender upright post, usually cylindrical and made of wood or metal, with one end fixed in the ground or mounted to a base. It appears as a long vertical shaft and may be plain or support wires, lights, signs, flags, or other fixtures.
733.guidelines: Classify as pole when the main object is a simple vertical post or mast-like support. Include utility poles, signposts, lamp posts, and similar upright posts when the pole itself is the focus. Do not confuse with columns or pillars, which are thicker architectural supports; stakes or rods, which are usually smaller; or towers, which are larger framed structures. Wires, lamps, or signs may be attached, but the defining feature is the long upright post.

name: police vehicle
734.description: A road vehicle used by police and marked as such, typically with the word POLICE or a local equivalent, emergency light bars, high-visibility striping or checker patterns, and official livery. Examples may be sedans, station wagons, vans, or larger transport vehicles, but they are consistently identifiable as police-operated vehicles.
734.guidelines: Classify as police vehicle when the vehicle itself is clearly police-marked by livery, text, or emergency equipment. Include police cars, police vans, patrol wagons, and similar marked law-enforcement road vehicles. Do not confuse with ambulances, fire vehicles, security cars, or ordinary vans with similar flashing lights; police vehicles usually show explicit police markings and police-style patrol livery. Exclude unmarked civilian vehicles unless they are unmistakably identifiable as police vehicles.

name: poncho
735.description: A loose outer garment made from a single broad piece of fabric or knitwear, usually draped over the shoulders with an opening for the head. It commonly hangs cape-like with wide, unstructured sides and may be rectangular, square, or triangular, often with fringed hems, stripes, or crocheted/knitted textures.
735.guidelines: Classify as poncho when the garment is a one-piece shoulder covering with a central neck opening and no full front opening or set-in sleeves. It may be woven, knitted, crocheted, or waterproof. Distinguish from a cape or cloak, which is more tailored and often opens in front; from a shawl or wrap, which is draped around the shoulders without a fixed neck opening; and from a sweater or cardigan, which has defined sleeves or a fitted torso.

name: billiard table
736.description: A large rectangular cue-sports table with a flat cloth-covered playing surface, raised cushioned rails around the edges, and usually six corner and side pockets. It is typically made of wood with sturdy legs and is commonly covered in green, red, or blue felt.
736.guidelines: Classify as billiard table when the image shows the full cue-sports table itself: a cloth-covered rectangular table with surrounding rails and, in most examples, pockets. Do not confuse it with air hockey or shuffleboard tables, which lack cushioned rails and billiard pockets, or with ping-pong tables, which have a net. If balls, cues, or a triangle rack are visible alongside a cue-sports table, that supports this category, but the table should be the main object.

name: soda bottle
737.description: A bottle used for soft drinks or carbonated beverages, typically made of glass or plastic. It usually has a narrow neck, a capped opening, and a printed or molded brand label; the body may be straight-sided, contoured, or slightly waisted, and is often clear, green, or tinted by the drink inside.
737.guidelines: Classify as a soda bottle when the object is specifically a soft-drink beverage bottle, whether glass or plastic, including branded bottles for cola, lemon-lime soda, ginger ale, and similar drinks. Do not confuse it with cans, cups, or generic water/juice bottles. Compared with water bottles, soda bottles are more often branded for soft drinks and may have classic contour glass shapes or thicker plastic bodies. Exclude other beverage containers unless they are clearly soft-drink bottles.

name: flowerpot
738.description: A flowerpot is a small to medium container used to grow or display plants. It is typically round, oval, or square with an open top, solid sides, and a flat base, and may be made of terracotta, ceramic, plastic, metal, or similar materials. Many images show soil and a living plant emerging from the pot, but the defining object is the pot itself.
738.guidelines: Classify as flowerpot when the image centers on a portable plant container, usually holding soil and often a plant. Include terracotta pots, ceramic planters, plastic nursery pots, and decorative plant pots. Do not confuse with garden beds or in-ground plantings, which lack a distinct container; vases, which are mainly for cut flowers in water; or large fixed planters integrated into architecture. The key cue is a discrete pot-shaped container intended for growing or holding a plant.

name: potter's wheel
739.description: A potter's wheel is a circular rotating wheelhead, usually mounted on a stand or table, used to shape wet clay by hand into symmetrical vessels. In images it often appears with spinning clay centered on the disk, with the potter's hands forming a bowl, cup, or vase; the wheel may be foot-powered, kick-driven, or motorized.
739.guidelines: Classify as potter's wheel when the defining object is the ceramic-forming wheel: a flat round spinning disk with clay being centered or shaped by hand. Include traditional kick wheels and modern electric pottery wheels. Do not confuse with a lathe, which cuts wood or metal with tools rather than wet clay by hand; a spinning wheel, which is for making thread; or a generic turntable/lazy Susan, which lacks the pottery-making setup and clay-forming context.

name: power drill
740.description: A handheld powered drilling tool with a pistol-grip or inline body, a motor-driven rotating chuck at the front, and a drill bit or driver bit attached. It is usually electric, either corded or cordless, and commonly appears in plastic housings with trigger controls and a forward-facing spindle for boring holes or driving fasteners.
740.guidelines: Classify as power drill when the image shows a handheld motorized drill/driver with a rotating chuck and bit. This includes corded and cordless consumer drills and drill-drivers. Do not confuse with an impact driver, which is usually shorter with a hex collet instead of a 3-jaw chuck; a rotary hammer or hammer drill, which is bulkier and often has an auxiliary front handle for masonry work; or a rotary tool such as a Dremel, which is much smaller and pen-like. Exclude drill presses and other stationary shop machines.

name: prayer rug
741.description: A small rectangular rug or mat used for prayer, typically shown singly or in rows. Most examples are richly patterned textile rugs with a niche- or arch-shaped motif at one end indicating orientation, often with geometric, floral, or mosque-like designs and fringed ends. Common colors include red, green, blue, burgundy, cream, and gold. Islamic prayer rugs generally avoid animal or human figures, while Christian prayer rugs may include living creatures.
741.guidelines: Classify as prayer rug when the object is a portable prayer mat or rug with religious layout cues, especially a mihrab-like arch, directional end, mosque imagery, or repeated mosque-floor arrangement. Do not confuse with ordinary area rugs, runners, or decorative carpets, which lack a clear prayer orientation and devotional design. Also distinguish from towels, blankets, and tapestries: prayer rugs are thicker woven mats meant to lie on the floor and usually have a framed, symmetrical prayer-oriented pattern.

name: printer
742.description: A printer is a machine that produces text or images on paper or other media. It may be a small desktop unit or a large office/industrial machine, and often has a paper tray, output slot, buttons or a control panel, and sometimes a flatbed scanner on top in multifunction models.
742.guidelines: Classify as printer any device whose main function is printing documents, labels, or images onto physical media, including desktop printers, office laser printers, multifunction printer-scanners, and large copier-style printers. Do not confuse with a standalone scanner, which has only a flatbed scanning surface and no paper output path; a photocopier, if clearly presented as a dedicated copier rather than a general printer; or a fax machine, which is usually smaller and centered on telephone document transmission. If a machine includes scanning/copying features but is fundamentally a print device, it still belongs here.

name: prison
743.description: A prison is a secure detention facility with barred doors and windows, metal grilles, locked cells, narrow cell blocks, and austere institutional interiors. Typical views show rows of cells, heavy steel doors, corridors lined with bars, and enclosed holding spaces designed to confine people.
743.guidelines: Classify as prison when the image shows jail or prison cells, barred detention rooms, or cell-block corridors in a correctional facility. Do not confuse with a castle: castles are large historic fortified buildings with towers, stone facades, battlements, or grand exterior architecture rather than modern or plain detention interiors. Also avoid confusing with cages, kennels, or playground structures; prisons are human-scale secure confinement spaces with cells, bars, and correctional architecture.

name: missile
744.description: A missile is a long, narrow projectile or self-propelled weapon, typically cylindrical with a pointed nose and stabilizing fins. It is usually shown mounted on a launcher, displayed in a museum, carried on military equipment, or ascending with exhaust and smoke; some examples are guided rockets or ballistic missiles with smooth metal bodies in white, gray, olive, or black.
744.guidelines: Classify as missile when the main object is a weapon-like rocket or guided projectile with a slender fusiform body, pointed tip, and tail fins, whether in flight, on a launcher, or on display. Do not confuse with space launch vehicles or sounding rockets, which are usually larger space-oriented rockets with prominent multistage structures, boosters, or spacecraft context. Also exclude model rockets and toy rockets, which are smaller recreational objects, and bombs or torpedoes, which generally lack the same rocket-propelled missile form or launcher context.

name: projector
745.description: A projector is a device that casts an enlarged image onto a screen, wall, or other surface using a bright light source and a lens. Common forms include modern digital projectors in box-shaped housings with a prominent front lens and ventilation grilles, as well as older film or slide projectors with reels, lamp housings, and projection lenses.
745.guidelines: Classify as a projector when the device is built to throw an image outward through a lens onto another surface. Typical cues are a large projection lens on the front, vents, control buttons, and sometimes film reels or a slide/film mechanism. Do not confuse with cameras, which capture images rather than project them; slide viewers or microscopes, which are meant for direct viewing; scanners or printers, which do not project light images; or spotlights/flashlights, which emit light but do not form detailed images.

name: hockey puck
746.description: A hockey puck is a small, flat, solid rubber disc, usually black, with a round shape, low height, and smooth sides and faces. It is the hard disk used on the ice in ice hockey.
746.guidelines: Classify as a hockey puck when the object is the thick black rubber disc used in ice hockey, whether loose on the ice, on a stick blade, or shown alone with team logos printed on it. Do not confuse it with ringette rings, curling stones, frisbees, or washers: a hockey puck is much smaller than a frisbee, flatter and simpler than a curling stone, and a solid disc rather than a hollow ring.

name: punching bag
747.description: A padded striking target used for boxing or martial-arts training, usually made of leather or synthetic vinyl and stuffed or weighted. Most examples are cylindrical heavy bags that hang vertically or stand on a base, but the category also includes speed-bag and reflex-bag variants with a rounded or teardrop shape. Common colors are black, red, blue, or white, often with printed brand logos.
747.guidelines: Classify as punching bag when the main object is a purpose-built boxing training bag meant to be hit. Include hanging heavy bags, freestanding bags, speed bags, and similar padded punch-training bags. Do not confuse with a punching pad or focus mitt, which is handheld; a gym sandbag or duffel bag, which lacks boxing-specific mounting and shape; or a balloon or toy bop bag, which is lightweight and not standard gym equipment. The key cues are thick padded construction, boxing/gym context, and either hanging chains/straps, a spring mount, or a weighted stand.

name: purse
748.description: A small handheld pouch or case for carrying money and small personal items. It is typically made of fabric, leather, or synthetic material, and often has a zipper, snap, fold-over flap, or metal clasp closure. Common forms include soft zip pouches, clasp coin purses, and compact wallet-like cases.
748.guidelines: Classify as purse when the item is a small personal carrying pouch meant for coins, cash, cards, or other small essentials, usually held in the hand rather than worn on the back or shoulder. Do not confuse with a handbag or shoulder bag, which is usually larger and has longer handles or straps; a wallet, which is flatter and more strictly card-and-bill oriented; or a pencil case/cosmetic bag, which may look similar but is primarily for pens or toiletries rather than money and everyday valuables.

name: quill pen
749.description: A writing implement made from a large bird feather, typically with the hollow shaft cut and shaped into a nib or mounted in a decorative pen holder. It has a long central shaft with soft vanes along part of its length, giving it the unmistakable appearance of a feather used for writing.
749.guidelines: Classify as quill pen when the object is clearly a feather intended or presented as a pen or calligraphy tool, often paired with ink, paper, or a stand. Do not confuse it with an ordinary feather, which is just plumage and lacks a writing tip or pen-like presentation, or with a dip pen/fountain pen, which may have metal nibs and rigid manufactured bodies rather than a visible feather shaft and vanes.

name: comforter
750.description: A large fabric bed covering used as the top layer of bedding, typically spread over a bed or draped over furniture. It appears as a broad rectangular textile, often padded or thick, with a soft quilted, stitched, or puffed surface. Common examples are solid-colored or patterned with plaid, floral, striped, cartoon, or other decorative prints.
750.guidelines: Classify as comforter when the main object is a thick top bed covering meant to cover most or all of a bed. It may be quilted, stitched, or visibly stuffed, and is usually larger and more bed-shaped than a throw blanket.
