The key cue is a seat suspended from above by flexible supports.

name: light switch
844.description: A manually operated electrical switch, usually mounted on a wall, panel, or device housing. It typically appears as a small toggle, rocker, push-button, rotary knob, or lever set into a switch plate or control panel, often made of plastic or metal and used to open or close an electrical circuit.
844.guidelines: Classify images as light switch when the central object is a manual electrical switching control. Include common wall switches, panel toggles, rocker switches, and rotary on/off switches. Exclude electrical outlets, plugs, sockets, dimmers without a clear switching function, circuit breakers, and other controls whose main role is regulation or protection rather than simple switching. Distinguish from outlets by the absence of receptacle holes for plug prongs, and from knobs/dials by the presence of discrete on/off or directional switching positions.

name: syringe
845.description: A syringe is a small handheld device with a cylindrical barrel marked with measurement lines, a sliding plunger, and a narrow tip that may hold a needle. It is typically made of clear plastic or glass so liquid inside is visible, and often appears with a long thin metal needle, colored hub, or protective cap.
845.guidelines: Classify images as syringe when the main object is the plunger-and-barrel injection or dispensing device, with or without a needle attached. Include medical syringes, oral dosing syringes, and large dispensing syringes if they share the same barrel-and-plunger form. Do not confuse with hypodermic needles shown alone, pipettes or droppers without a plunger, IV bags or tubing, pens or mechanical tools, or bottles/vials that may appear alongside a syringe.

name: table lamp
846.description: A small freestanding electric lamp designed to sit on a table, desk, nightstand, or other furniture surface. It typically has a base, an upright stem or support, and one or more bulbs often covered by a lampshade. Shapes and materials vary widely, but the object is portable and sized for tabletop use rather than floor mounting or wall/ceiling installation.
846.guidelines: Classify as table lamp when the lamp is clearly a self-supporting light fixture resting on furniture or another raised surface. Include common bedside, desk, decorative, and accent lamps, even when the style is unusual. Do not confuse with floor lamps, which are much taller and stand directly on the floor; wall lamps or sconces, which attach to a wall; ceiling lights or pendant lamps, which hang overhead; or lanterns/candle holders, which lack the typical table-lamp base-and-shade form.

name: armoured fighting vehicle
847.description: A heavily armored military vehicle built for combat, typically with a low, robust body, thick protective plating, tracked or wheeled running gear, and mounted weapons such as a cannon, machine gun, or missile launcher. Shapes vary from turreted tanks to boxier troop carriers and reconnaissance vehicles, but all are visibly weaponized and protected for battlefield use.
847.guidelines: Classify as armoured fighting vehicle when the vehicle is a purpose-built armored military combat platform, whether tracked or wheeled, and whether it is a tank, infantry fighting vehicle, armored car, or similar combat vehicle. Do not confuse it with unarmored military trucks, engineering vehicles, civilian construction vehicles, or self-propelled guns that lack the enclosed armored combat-vehicle form. Key cues are armored hull panels, battlefield weapon mounts, heavy-duty tracks or military wheels, and an overall protected combat design.

name: cassette player
848.description: A device for playing audio cassette tapes, including portable players, home stereo components, boomboxes, car stereos, and cassette decks. Typical examples have a rectangular body with a cassette slot or hinged cassette door, playback controls such as play, stop, rewind, and fast-forward, and often a display, speakers, headphone jack, or recording controls.
848.guidelines: Classify as cassette player when the object is a machine designed to play compact cassette tapes. Include portable Walkman-style players, boomboxes, home cassette decks, integrated stereos, and car cassette units. Do not confuse with the cassette tape itself, VHS players, CD players, turntables, reel-to-reel tape recorders, or generic radios without a cassette mechanism. The key cue is a compact-cassette bay or slot sized for an audio cassette, usually with familiar tape transport controls.

name: teapot
849.description: A teapot is a vessel for brewing and serving tea, typically with a rounded or squat body, a pouring spout, a side handle, and a fitted lid at the top. It is commonly made of ceramic, porcelain, clay, glass, or metal, and may range from plain and functional to highly decorative.
849.guidelines: Classify as teapot when the object is a lidded pot designed to hold and pour brewed tea, with a distinct body, spout, and handle. Include decorative, novelty, and traditional forms as long as the object is still a teapot. Do not confuse with a kettle, which is primarily for heating water and often has a top handle for stovetop use; a coffee pot, which is usually taller and shaped for coffee service; or a pitcher/jug, which typically lacks a lid or tea-brewing form.

name: teddy bear
850.description: A stuffed toy bear with a soft plush, furry, or knitted exterior and a simplified bear-like body: rounded head, small rounded ears, short snout, button or bead eyes, and soft arms and legs. It is usually small enough to hold and may appear in many colors, fabrics, and clothing styles, but the defining appearance is a cuddly bear-shaped soft toy.
850.guidelines: Classify as teddy bear when the object is clearly a stuffed or plush toy shaped like a bear. Include knitted or crocheted bear toys and decorative teddy bears in varied colors or outfits. Do not confuse with other stuffed animals such as dogs, pandas, lambs, or generic plush toys; the key cue is a bear form with rounded ears, a short muzzle, and a classic teddy-bear body. Exclude real bears, bear figurines made of hard materials, and dolls or toys whose animal identity is not bear.

name: television set
851.description: A standalone television receiver: a boxy electronic display unit with a screen on the front, usually housed in plastic or wood, often with control knobs, buttons, vents, or built-in speakers. In these examples most are CRT TVs, with thick bodies and slightly curved glass screens, shown either on their own or as the main object in the scene.
851.guidelines: Classify as this category when the object is a self-contained TV set itself, especially a household television with an integrated screen and cabinet. Do not confuse it with a computer monitor, which usually lacks TV tuner controls and is paired with a computer; a microwave or oven, which has a door and cooking chamber rather than a display screen; or an old radio/speaker cabinet, which has dials and grilles but no visible television screen. Ignore what is being shown on the screen; the object must be the television set.

name: tennis ball
852.description: A tennis ball is a small spherical sports ball, usually bright fluorescent yellow or yellow-green, covered in fuzzy felt and marked with a curved white seam that wraps around the surface.
852.guidelines: Classify as a tennis ball when the object is a felt-covered ball with the characteristic curved white seam, typically neon yellow-green. Do not confuse it with a table tennis ball or beer pong ball, which are smooth hard plastic and smaller, usually white or orange; a baseball, which is white leather with red stitching; a lacrosse ball, which is smooth rubber without felt; or pet toy balls, which may be fuzzy but usually lack the standard tennis-ball seam pattern.

name: thatched roof
853.description: A roof covered with thatch: a thick outer layer of dried plant material such as straw, reed, palm leaves, or similar vegetation. It typically appears tan, yellow-brown, or gray-brown, with a coarse fibrous texture, layered bundles, and deep eaves or rounded roof contours.
853.guidelines: Classify as thatched roof when the visible category is the roof covering itself made from bundled dried vegetation. Look for densely layered straw- or reed-like material and a shaggy, fibrous surface. Do not confuse with shingle, tile, slate, or metal roofs, which have hard regular panels or tiles, nor with woven walls, fences, haystacks, or huts where the main subject is the whole structure rather than the thatched roofing material.

name: theater curtain
854.description: A large fabric curtain at the front of a stage or theater, usually heavy and pleated or draped, often red, burgundy, purple, gold, or blue. It spans the proscenium opening and may hang in vertical folds, swagged sections, or multiple panels that open sideways or rise before a performance.
854.guidelines: Classify as theater curtain when the main subject is the stage front curtain in a theater or performance venue. It is typically a broad decorative curtain covering the stage opening, often seen from the audience with theatrical lighting, proscenium framing, or auditorium seats. Do not confuse with ordinary household curtains or drapes, which are smaller and associated with windows; shower curtains, which are plain bathroom partitions; or backdrops and cycloramas, which are flat scenic surfaces behind the stage rather than the front curtain.

name: thimble
855.description: A thimble is a small, hard cap worn on a finger while sewing. It is usually metal, but can also be ceramic, plastic, glass, or leather. Most are cup-shaped with a closed top and a slightly wider opening at the base, and the outer surface typically has dimples or textured bumps to keep a needle from slipping.
855.guidelines: Classify as a thimble when the object is a small finger-sized sewing guard, usually a dimpled cap for pushing a needle. Include decorative souvenir thimbles and open-sided or novelty thimbles if they clearly serve or imitate this sewing form. Do not confuse with shot glasses, small cups, bottle caps, metal sleeves, or fingertip protectors: thimbles are much smaller, finger-worn, and usually have a domed or capped shape with a textured exterior for needle work.

name: threshing machine
856.description: A threshing machine is a farm machine used to separate grain or seed from harvested stalks and straw. It is typically a large wheeled or trailer-like machine, often boxy and open-framed, with a feed table or intake where bundles are inserted, an internal drum or separator, and chutes or spouts for discharging grain and straw. Examples range from antique steam-powered and belt-driven threshers to later mobile threshing units, but all are distinct harvesting-processing machines rather than simple wagons or trailers.
856.guidelines: Classify as a threshing machine only when the machine is clearly built for threshing: look for a crop intake/feed opening, visible separating body, and output chutes or conveyors for grain and straw. Include both old stationary or belt-driven threshers and mobile threshing units. Exclude ordinary field trailers, wagons, and grain carts that are just containers without threshing mechanisms. Also distinguish from combine harvesters, which are self-propelled field harvesters with a large front cutting header, and from balers, which form tied bales rather than separating grain from straw.

name: throne
857.description: A throne is a ceremonial high-status seat, usually larger, taller, and more ornate than an ordinary chair. It often has a prominent high back, armrests, and a raised platform or canopy, and is commonly decorated with carving, gilding, rich upholstery, symbolic motifs, or architectural framing.
857.guidelines: Classify as throne when the image shows a formal seat of rulership, sovereignty, or religious authority designed for display and ceremony rather than everyday sitting. Typical cues are monumental scale, central placement, lavish ornament, a dais or steps, and regal or sacred context. Do not confuse with ordinary armchairs, dining chairs, benches, pews, stalls, or sofas; those lack the symbolic ceremonial design and elevated presentation. Also exclude cathedras, judge's chairs, or decorative high-backed chairs unless they clearly function as a ceremonial seat of authority.

name: tile roof
858.description: A roof surface covered with overlapping roofing tiles, typically arranged in regular rows. The tiles may be curved, flat, or interlocking, and are commonly made of clay, terracotta, concrete, slate, or ceramic, giving roofs a textured pattern in red, brown, gray, or weathered mossy tones.
858.guidelines: Classify as tile roof when the defining visible feature is a roof clad in distinct overlapping tiles. Include barrel, pantile, flat, and interlocking roof tiles across different materials and colors. Do not confuse with shingle roofs, which use thinner flat pieces such as asphalt or wood; metal roofs, which have large continuous sheets or panels; thatched roofs, which are fibrous and straw-like; or slate roofs when the image emphasizes stone shingles rather than the broader tiled-roof category. The key cue is repeated individual roof tiles forming the roof covering.

name: toaster
859.description: A toaster is a small countertop kitchen appliance used to brown slices of bread. It is typically compact and boxlike, usually metal or plastic, with one or more narrow slots on the top, a browning control, and a side lever or button; some examples are rounded, retro-styled, novelty-shaped, or toaster-oven variants.
859.guidelines: Classify as toaster when the object is a bread-toasting appliance with top loading slots or a clearly recognizable toaster-oven form. Common look-alikes include microwave ovens, sandwich presses, waffle makers, radios, and other small kitchen appliances such as kettles or coffee makers. Distinguish it by the bread slots, pop-up mechanism, heating function for toast, crumb tray, and browning controls; unlike a microwave or oven, it is much smaller and specialized for toast.

name: tobacconist
860.description: A retail shop devoted to tobacco products and smoking accessories. Typical images show a street-facing storefront, hanging sign, shutter or window display, or an interior counter lined with cigarettes, cigars, pipes, rolling papers, humidors, and related merchandise. Signage often prominently includes words like “tobacco,” “tabac,” “tabacos,” “tabacchi,” “cigars,” or “pipes.”
860.guidelines: Classify as a tobacconist when the place is clearly a shop specializing in tobacco or smoking goods, identified by tobacco-related signage or displays of cigars, cigarettes, pipes, or accessories. Do not confuse with a general convenience store, supermarket checkout, gift shop, liquor store, or newsstand that merely sells some cigarettes; this class should look like a dedicated tobacco retailer. Also exclude cannabis dispensaries or vape shops unless the shop is specifically presented as a traditional tobacco/cigar/pipe store.

name: toilet seat
861.description: A toilet seat is the hinged ring-shaped seat attached to the rim of a toilet bowl, usually paired with a matching lid. It is typically oval or U-shaped and made of plastic, painted wood, or molded composite, in plain white or colored finishes, and may be plain or decorated.
861.guidelines: Classify images as toilet seat when the defining object is the hinged seat ring or seat-and-lid assembly attached to a toilet. Include open or closed seats, replacement seats, and decorative seat covers. Do not confuse it with a whole toilet when the entire fixture is the subject, with a toilet lid alone, or with similar bathroom fixtures such as bidets and urinals, which lack the characteristic hinged seat ring.

name: torch
862.description: A torch is a handheld or mounted stick-like object with a combustible, flame-bearing tip. It typically has a long handle or pole and an exposed orange-yellow flame at one end, often with wrapped cloth, wick, or fuel material that glows and burns brightly, especially in dark scenes.
862.guidelines: Classify as torch when the object is a pole, stick, or handle designed to carry an open flame at its tip, such as ceremonial torches, tiki torches, or parade torches. Do not confuse it with a flare, which is a pyrotechnic signal that usually emits intense colored light and smoke from a tube; a candle, which is short and wax-bodied with a small wick; a match or lighter, which is much smaller and hand-sized; or a bonfire/fire pit, which is a free-standing fire rather than a flame attached to a carried implement.

name: totem pole
863.description: A tall, upright carved wooden pole, usually made from a single tree trunk and decorated with stacked human, animal, or supernatural figures, masks, and crest symbols. It is typically vertical and elongated, with bold painted or carved facial features, beaks, wings, claws, and repeated emblematic forms arranged one above another.
863.guidelines: Classify as a totem pole when the image shows a freestanding carved pole with multiple symbolic figures or faces stacked vertically in the Northwest Coast Indigenous style. Do not confuse it with a generic carved post, tiki statue, or sculpture: totem poles are usually much taller, pole-like rather than blocky, and feature several integrated figures along one trunk. Exclude single figurative statues, plain utility poles, and unrelated ornamental columns without stacked crest imagery.

name: tow truck
864.description: A tow truck is a road service truck built to recover, lift, pull, or transport other vehicles. It is typically a medium or heavy truck chassis fitted with towing equipment such as a boom, wheel-lift, underlift, winch, or a flatbed rollback platform, often with amber warning lights and service markings.
864.guidelines: Classify as tow truck when the vehicle itself is a truck designed for vehicle recovery or transport. Common forms include flatbed rollback wreckers, hook-and-chain or boom wreckers, and wheel-lift trucks. Do not confuse with a flatbed truck or car carrier used mainly for hauling cargo or multiple cars; tow trucks usually have recovery gear, winches, underlifts, or a rollback bed for disabled vehicles. Exclude ordinary pickup trucks, trailers, and transport trucks unless they clearly function as a wrecker.

name: toy store
865.description: A retail shop or shop display devoted primarily to toys, with shelves, bins, or window displays crowded with playthings such as dolls, action figures, stuffed animals, model kits, games, and colorful children’s products. Scenes are typically indoors or in storefront windows and emphasize merchandise arranged for sale.
865.guidelines: Classify as toy store when the image shows a commercial retail space or display whose main purpose is selling toys. Key cues are dense assortments of toys on shelves, in display cases, or in shop windows, often with price tags, packaging, store fixtures, or shoppers. Do not confuse with a child’s bedroom, playroom, nursery, arcade, gift shop, hobby shop, or a single toy close-up. If the image focuses on one toy object rather than the retail environment, it should not be labeled as toy store.

name: tractor
866.description: A tractor is a heavy motor vehicle built mainly for traction and pulling power, typically with a large rear pair of deeply treaded wheels or continuous tracks, a smaller front pair or articulated steering, a tall engine hood, and an open or enclosed driver’s seat/cab. Most examples are farm or utility machines, often with hitches, power take-off hardware, loaders, blades, or other attachments, and they appear in a wide range of colors, sizes, and vintages.
866.guidelines: Classify as tractor when the vehicle’s primary form is an agricultural or utility traction machine designed to pull or power implements. Include old and modern farm tractors, compact utility tractors, and similar tractor units even when attachments are present. Do not confuse with combine harvesters, excavators, skid-steer loaders, forklifts, or bulldozers: tractors usually have a simple body with prominent rear drive wheels, a central driver position, and towing/implement connections rather than a dedicated digging bucket, lifting mast, or large integrated harvesting body. Lawn mowers and garden tractors are only included if they clearly appear to be tractor-type machines rather than ordinary riding mowers.

name: semi-trailer truck
867.description: A heavy-duty commercial road vehicle built for hauling freight, typically consisting of a large tractor unit pulling one or more box, tanker, flatbed, or curtain-sided semi-trailers. It is much larger than a standard truck, with a tall cab, multiple axles, and a long articulated overall profile.
867.guidelines: Classify as a semi-trailer truck when the vehicle is a tractor-and-trailer combination used for heavy freight transport. Include box trailers, tankers, flatbeds, and similar semitrailer configurations. Do not confuse with straight trucks or box trucks, which have a single rigid body with no separate trailer; pickup trucks, which are much smaller; buses, which carry passengers; or detached trailers without a tractor. The key cue is the articulated combination of a tractor unit in front and a long freight trailer behind.

name: tray
868.description: A tray is a shallow, flat serving or carrying piece, usually with a raised rim or edge and often with handles. It may be round, oval, rectangular, square, or decorative in outline, and can be made of wood, metal, plastic, ceramic, or other rigid materials. The defining appearance is a broad open surface for holding items, with sides low enough to keep objects from sliding off.
868.guidelines: Classify as tray when the object is a portable flat or slightly concave platform meant for carrying, serving, or presenting food, drinks, or other items. Look for a shallow profile, open top, and low surrounding rim; side cutout handles or small grips are common but not required. Do not confuse with plates, platters, or dishes, which are primarily tableware for serving/eating and usually lack carrying handles or tray-like raised sides; baking pans or casseroles, which are deeper cookware for oven use; or boxes and baskets, which are substantially deeper and more container-like.

name: trench coat
869.description: A long, tailored coat in the classic trench style, typically double-breasted with a wide lapel collar, belted waist, and often shoulder epaulettes, cuff straps, and a storm flap. Most examples are knee-length or longer and made from smooth woven fabric in khaki, beige, black, navy, or similar solid colors.
869.guidelines: Classify as a trench coat when the coat has the characteristic belted, military-inspired design, especially a double-breasted front, broad lapels, and mid- to long-length silhouette. Do not confuse with a peacoat, which is shorter and heavier with no waist belt; an overcoat/topcoat, which is usually single-breasted or more simply tailored; or a raincoat, which may be waterproof but lacks the classic trench details such as epaulettes, storm flap, and structured belted shape.

name: tricycle
870.description: A tricycle is a cycle with three wheels, usually powered by pedals and steered with handlebars. It may be a small child's trike with a low frame and one front wheel plus two rear wheels, or a larger cargo or passenger tricycle with an extended frame, basket, platform, or carriage body.
870.guidelines: Classify as tricycle when the vehicle is a pedal cycle built on three wheels. Include children's trikes, adult trikes, cargo trikes, and cycle rickshaws if the three-wheeled cycle itself is the main object. Do not confuse with bicycles (two wheels), balance bikes or scooters (typically two wheels and no pedal drivetrain), pedal cars or toy ride-on vehicles shaped like cars or animals, or wheelchairs and strollers, which are not bicycles.

name: trimaran
871.description: A trimaran is a multihull boat with one central main hull and two smaller outrigger hulls, or floats, connected by side beams. In images it usually appears as a very wide sailing craft with three distinct hulls, a tall mast, and large sails; many examples are lightweight racing yachts, though trimarans can also be built for leisure, ferry service, or military use.
871.guidelines: Classify as trimaran only when three separate hulls are visible or clearly implied: one main hull in the center plus two side floats joined by crossbeams. Do not confuse with a catamaran, which has only two parallel hulls and no single larger central hull, or with a monohull sailboat, which has just one hull. Hydrofoiling sailboats may look unusual, but if the craft still has three hulls it is a trimaran.

name: camera tripod
872.description: A three-legged support stand for photographic equipment, typically with extendable legs and a mounting head or plate at the top for attaching a camera, telescope, or similar imaging device. It may be full-size, tabletop, or flexible-legged, but the defining feature is a stable three-leg structure designed to hold photographic gear steady.
872.guidelines: Classify as camera tripod when the image shows a three-legged stand intended to support photographic equipment. Include folded or partially visible tripods if the three-legged support and camera-mounting function are clear. Do not confuse with monopods, light stands, microphone stands, music stands, speaker stands, easels, or generic three-legged furniture. The key cues are three support legs plus a camera-style mounting head, quick-release plate, or visible use with a camera or related imaging device.

name: triumphal arch
873.description: A freestanding monumental arch built as a commemorative or celebratory structure, typically in stone or masonry. It usually has one large central arched opening, often with a rectangular mass above it, and may include columns, relief sculptures, inscriptions, carved panels, or statues on top. It is designed as a standalone monument rather than as part of a defensive wall or functional gateway.
873.guidelines: Classify as triumphal arch only when the structure is a standalone commemorative arch monument. Common look-alikes include city gates, garden gates, fortified gateways, bridge arches, and ordinary building entrances. Distinguish it by its monumental freestanding form, decorative sculptural program, and ceremonial purpose. Exclude arches that are clearly attached to walls, used mainly as practical gates, or part of a larger building or bridge.

name: trolleybus
874.description: A trolleybus is a road-going public transit bus powered by electricity from two overhead wires through roof-mounted trolley poles. It has the body shape of a bus rather than a rail vehicle, appears in single-deck, double-deck, rigid, or articulated forms, and is commonly seen in urban street service beneath visible overhead wiring.
874.guidelines: Classify as trolleybus only when the vehicle is clearly a bus drawing power from overhead wires, typically via two trolley poles connected to twin wires. Do not confuse it with a tram or streetcar, which runs on rails, or with an electric bus that lacks trolley poles and overhead-wire pickup. Also exclude ordinary motorbuses, which may look similar in body shape but have no wire connection above.

name: trombone
875.description: A brass musical instrument with a long cylindrical tube folded back on itself, a wide flared bell, and a straight hand slide that moves in and out to change pitch. Usually metallic gold, brass, or silver in color, it is longer and more linear in profile than most brass instruments.
875.guidelines: Classify as trombone when the instrument has a prominent telescoping slide and a flared bell. Do not confuse it with a trumpet or cornet, which use valves and are much more compact, or with a tuba/euphonium, which have large coiled bodies without a long slide. It can resemble a slide trumpet, but a trombone is typically larger with a longer slide and broader bell.

name: turnstile
877.description: A turnstile is a controlled entry gate used to admit one person at a time, usually after payment or authorization. It commonly consists of a waist-high metal housing with rotating horizontal arms, or a full-height cylindrical cage with vertical bars that spins around a central axis.
877.guidelines: Classify as turnstile when the main object is a pedestrian access-control gate with rotating barriers that regulate one-at-a-time entry. Includes tripod turnstiles, optical fare gates with rotating arms, and full-height revolving turnstiles. Do not confuse with ordinary doors, swinging gates, railings, ticket barriers without rotating parts, or revolving doors for buildings; turnstiles are specifically entry-control devices designed to meter pedestrian passage.

name: typewriter keyboard
878.description: A typewriter keyboard is the key arrangement on a mechanical or electromechanical typewriter, typically made up of round or square raised keys set in staggered rows. The keys are usually labeled with letters, numbers, and punctuation, often in a QWERTY layout, and are mounted on a metal typewriter body with visible platen, typebars, or other typing mechanisms nearby. Common appearances include black, gray, or colored metal housings and vintage keytops with glass, plastic, or painted caps.
878.guidelines: Classify this category when the image shows the keyboard section of a typewriter or a typewriter prominently identified by its distinctive typing keys. Distinguish it from computer keyboards, which are flatter, more rectangular, and lack a platen and typewriter mechanics, and from calculators or cash registers, which have different key layouts and no typing carriage. Vintage round keycaps, the presence of a roller platen, and exposed mechanical parts are strong cues for a typewriter keyboard.

name: umbrella
879.description: A handheld canopy used for rain or sun protection, typically formed by a fabric cover stretched over folding ribs and a central shaft, often with a hooked or straight handle. It is usually dome-shaped when open and appears in many solid colors, patterns, and transparent styles.
879.guidelines: Classify as umbrella when the defining object is a portable, hand-held folding canopy with visible ribs, shaft, and handle. Include standard rain umbrellas and parasols. Do not confuse with canopies, awnings, tents, patio umbrellas, or beach umbrellas, which are larger fixed or ground-mounted shelters, or with paper fans and other handheld accessories that lack the characteristic ribbed dome on a central shaft.

name: unicycle
880.description: A one-wheeled cycle with a single large wheel, pedals attached directly to the hub, a forked frame, and usually a small saddle mounted above the wheel. It is ridden by one person balancing upright over the wheel, with no second wheel, chain drive, or large bicycle frame.
880.guidelines: Classify as a unicycle only when the vehicle has exactly one main wheel with the rider seated or balanced directly above it. Do not confuse with bicycles or penny-farthings, which have two wheels; balance bikes or scooters, which have different frame layouts; or artistic/circus tall unicycles, which still count as unicycles if they keep the one-wheel direct-above-wheel structure.

name: upright piano
881.description: A piano with a tall, vertical cabinet and a standard keyboard on the front, with strings and soundboard mounted upright inside the case rather than extending horizontally. It is more compact than a grand piano and is commonly finished in wood or black lacquer, often with a rectangular front, top lid, and lower pedals.
881.guidelines: Classify as upright piano when the piano body is vertical and the instrument stands against a wall or as a tall cabinet, with the keyboard projecting from the front. Do not confuse with grand piano or baby grand, which have a long horizontal body and wing-shaped top; digital piano, which is slimmer and usually lacks a full acoustic cabinet; or square piano/keyboard instruments such as xylophones, which do not have the tall vertical piano case.

name: vacuum cleaner
882.description: A household cleaning appliance that removes dust and debris by suction. It typically has a motorized body with a dust bag or clear collection bin, plus a hose, wand, floor head, or an upright/stick form. Common home versions include canister, upright, handheld, and stick models, usually made of plastic and metal in varied colors.
882.guidelines: Classify as vacuum cleaner when the object is a home-use suction cleaning appliance with a floor nozzle, hose, wand, or integrated upright/stick body. Include canister, upright, stick, and handheld household vacuums. Do not confuse with shop vacuums or industrial wet/dry vacs, which are bulkier utility machines, or with floor polishers/scrubbers, which use rotating pads or brushes rather than suction nozzles. Also exclude carpet sweepers and mops, which lack a powered suction unit.

name: vase
883.description: A vase is a decorative or utilitarian container, typically taller than it is wide, with a stable base and an open top, often with a narrow neck or flared mouth. It may be made of glass, ceramic, metal, stone, or other materials, and can range from plain to highly ornamented. Common forms include bulbous, cylindrical, amphora-like, bottle-shaped, and sculptural vessels, especially those intended to hold flowers or branches or to stand alone as decoration.
883.guidelines: Classify as a vase when the object is primarily a freestanding ornamental vessel with an open mouth, especially one designed to hold cut flowers or branches. Include empty decorative vessels and sculptural flower vessels of many materials and shapes. Do not confuse with bottles, which are usually made for storing liquids and often have much narrower openings or closures; pitchers/jugs, which typically have a pouring spout and are meant for serving; pots, planters, and urns, which are often wider, heavier, or designed for planting or funerary use; or cups, bowls, and mugs, which are smaller tableware forms. If the object reads mainly as a decorative flower container rather than storage or cookware, it is a vase.

name: vault (architecture)
884.description: An arched interior ceiling or roof structure that spans a space, typically built of stone, brick, or concrete. It appears as a continuous curved or ribbed overhead form such as barrel, groin, rib, fan, or similar vaulting, often supported by walls, columns, or piers.
884.guidelines: Classify only indoor architectural views where the ceiling itself is a vault. Look for a self-supporting arched overhead structure extending across a room, aisle, crypt, or nave. Common confusions: domes—especially domes on pendentives—should be classified as dome, not vault; flat coffered or beamed ceilings are not vaults; ordinary arches over doors or arcades are not enough unless the image shows the vaulted ceiling spanning the interior space. Favor vault when the defining feature is the repeated or continuous arched ceiling form rather than a single hemispherical dome.

name: velvet
885.description: A soft pile fabric with a dense, smooth, plush surface and a rich, light-catching appearance. It is often seen in deep or saturated colors and can look lustrous, luxurious, and slightly shaded as the nap reflects light differently from different angles.
885.guidelines: Classify images as velvet when the defining cue is the fabric itself: a short, dense pile that gives a soft, plush, shimmering surface. It may appear in clothing, upholstery, cushions, bags, or crafts. Do not confuse it with velour, which is usually stretchier and more casual-looking; suede or nubuck, which have a matte leather nap rather than woven pile; or satin, which is glossy and smooth but lacks the fuzzy pile texture. If the surface looks plush and directional, with visible nap-related dark/light shifts, it is likely velvet.

name: vending machine
886.description: A vending machine is a tall, boxy coin- or card-operated cabinet that automatically dispenses goods. It usually has a front display window or product grid, visible rows of drinks, snacks, cigarettes, magazines, or other small items, plus selection buttons, a payment interface, and a dispensing slot near the bottom.
886.guidelines: Classify as a vending machine when the image shows a self-service retail machine designed to dispense products after payment. Common variants include drink, snack, cigarette, newspaper, and small-item vending machines. Do not confuse with ATMs, ticket machines, arcade machines, gumball/capsule toy dispensers, or lockers: vending machines show purchasable goods or product labels and have a delivery chute/bin for items. Exclude refrigerators, display cases, and kiosks that lack the coin/card-operated dispensing interface.

name: vestment
887.description: Religious ceremonial clothing: ornate robes, capes, tunics, mantles, and related garments worn in worship or used to dress sacred figures. They are typically made from rich fabric and heavily decorated with embroidery, brocade, metallic thread, crosses, floral motifs, heraldic patterns, or other religious symbols; many appear long, layered, and formal, often in gold, white, blue, red, purple, or green.
887.guidelines: Classify as vestment when the main subject is formal religious ceremonial attire or a sacred robe-like garment with clear liturgical ornamentation. This includes chasubles, copes, dalmatics, embroidered altar-related garments, and similar ecclesiastical robes. Do not confuse with secular royal robes, costumes, or ordinary dresses: vestments usually feature explicitly liturgical styling, church use, or Christian iconography such as crosses and church embroidery. Also distinguish from choir robes or graduation gowns, which are plainer and less richly embellished.

name: viaduct
888.description: A viaduct is a long elevated bridge-like structure, often built of stone, brick, concrete, or steel, that carries a railway or road across a valley, floodplain, river, or other low ground. It typically appears as a linear sequence of repeated arches or spans supported by tall piers, extending much farther than an ordinary single-span bridge.
888.guidelines: Classify as viaduct when the structure is a long multi-span elevated crossing, especially with many repeated arches over low ground or a broad valley. Do not confuse with an aqueduct, which is built to carry water; a regular bridge, which usually has fewer spans and crosses a more specific obstacle; or a modern overpass/flyover, which is typically shorter and uses girder or highway construction rather than a long arched series.

name: violin
889.description: A violin is a small bowed string instrument with a narrow waist, rounded upper and lower bouts, two f-holes, four strings, a short fingerboard, and a scroll at the end of the neck. It is typically made of polished wood in amber to reddish-brown tones and appears compact, light, and slender when held under the player's chin.
889.guidelines: Classify as violin when the instrument is the small, standard soprano member of the violin family. Do not confuse it with a viola, which is similar in shape but visibly larger and bulkier, with a longer body and neck. Also exclude cello and double bass, which are much larger and played upright rather than under the chin.

name: volleyball
890.description: A volleyball is a lightweight spherical ball used in volleyball and beach volleyball. It has a smooth or slightly textured synthetic or leather outer cover divided into curved stitched panels, and is commonly white or white with bright accent colors such as blue, yellow, or pink.
890.guidelines: Classify as volleyball when the object is the distinctive paneled ball used in indoor or beach volleyball, often seen in play near a net or being served, set, blocked, or held. Do not confuse it with a soccer ball, which usually has black-and-white pentagon/hexagon patches; a basketball, which is orange with ribbed channels; or a beach ball, which is inflatable and has broad striped segments. Plain white training volleyballs still count if they have the characteristic stitched panel pattern and volleyball size.

name: waffle iron
891.description: A waffle iron is a hinged cooking appliance with two heated metal plates that close together. The plates have a raised grid or patterned surface, usually round or rectangular, that presses batter into the characteristic waffle shape.
891.guidelines: Classify as a waffle iron when the object is the appliance or mold with two patterned plates for making waffles. It may be electric, stovetop, or cast-iron, and may be open or closed. Do not confuse it with a panini press, sandwich maker, or grill, which have flat or ridged plates rather than waffle grids, or with a pizzelle iron, which usually has shallower decorative cookie patterns instead of deep waffle pockets.

name: wall clock
892.description: A wall clock is a clock designed to be mounted on a wall, with a visible clock face and hands or display for showing the time. Examples include round, square, novelty, decorative, and pendulum clocks, as long as the clock itself is hanging on or attached to an interior or exterior wall. Freestanding clocks are not included.
892.guidelines: Classify as wall clock when the main object is a timekeeping device mounted on a wall. Include decorative and functional wall-mounted clocks of many shapes and styles. Exclude tower clocks and clocks built into a building facade or wall structure rather than mounted on it. Also exclude wristwatches, pocket watches, alarm clocks, desk clocks, floor clocks, and other freestanding timepieces. The key cue is a standalone clock visibly attached to a wall.

name: wallet
893.description: A wallet is a small, flat, foldable personal case, usually rectangular and made of leather, fabric, or synthetic material. It typically opens like a book or bifold and contains compartments or slots for paper money, cards, and identification; some examples are tri-fold or long flap styles but share the same compact carry form.
893.guidelines: Classify as wallet when the object is a compact folding holder for cash, cards, or ID. Common variants include bifold, trifold, and checkbook-style wallets. Do not confuse with a coin purse or pouch, which is usually smaller and not organized around bill/card compartments; a clutch or handbag, which is larger and meant to carry more items; or a passport holder/document organizer, which is typically larger and sized primarily for passports or full documents. The key cues are a slim portable form and an interior arranged for bills and cards.

name: wardrobe
894.description: A tall cabinet or built-in storage unit for clothing, typically with one or more doors and an interior fitted with hanging space, shelves, and sometimes drawers. It may be freestanding or built into a wall, and is usually made of wood, laminate, or similar furniture materials.
894.guidelines: Classify as wardrobe when the image shows a clothes-storage cabinet or built-in closet structure intended for garments. Common appearances include freestanding armoires, modern wardrobes with hinged or sliding doors, and open wardrobes with hanging clothes visible inside. Do not confuse with a chest of drawers or dresser, which mainly has stacked drawers and no full-height hanging compartment; a bookcase or cabinet, which is used for general storage and lacks clothing-oriented layout; or a door to a room/closet when the storage unit itself is not visible. Include both closed and open clothing wardrobes, but exclude simple hanging racks without an enclosing cabinet or closet structure.

name: warplane
895.description: An aircraft designed for military use, typically with a streamlined fuselage, swept or straight wings, a cockpit canopy, and markings such as national insignia or squadron paint. Examples include fighter jets, bombers, attack aircraft, and carrier-based military planes, often shown with weapons, external tanks, arresting gear, or camouflage.
895.guidelines: Classify as warplane when the main subject is a military aircraft rather than a civilian airplane. Key cues are military paint schemes, insignia, weapons pylons, radomes, tandem or bubble canopies, carrier-deck context, and combat-oriented shapes. Avoid confusing it with civilian airliners, private planes, aerobatic aircraft, or generic airplanes, which usually lack armament, military markings, and combat-specific design features.

name: washbasin
896.description: A washbasin is a fixed sink for washing hands or face, usually made of white ceramic, porcelain, stone, or similar smooth material. It has a shallow bowl with a drain and one or more faucets, and may be wall-mounted, set into a countertop, mounted on a pedestal, or designed as a vessel basin.
896.guidelines: Classify as washbasin when the main object is a bathroom or washroom sink intended for personal washing. Look for a relatively shallow basin with faucet hardware, typically indoors in a bathroom or restroom. Do not confuse with a kitchen sink, which is usually deeper, larger, and often paired with counters for dishwashing; a bidet, which is shaped for washing the body and usually sits lower like a toilet fixture; a bathtub, which is much larger and meant for bathing; or a drinking fountain, which is designed for drinking and usually has a bubbler nozzle rather than a normal sink faucet.

name: washing machine
897.description: A washing machine is a household or commercial appliance for laundering clothes. It is typically a boxy white or light-colored machine with a metal or plastic body, a wash drum inside, and a control panel with buttons, dials, or a display. Common designs are front-loading machines with a circular glass door on the front and top-loading machines with a lid on top.
897.guidelines: Classify as a washing machine when the image shows a laundry appliance with a wash drum for clothes, usually with a front door or top lid and wash controls. Include both front-load and top-load models, including compact, stacked, and coin-operated units. Do not confuse with a clothes dryer, which is similar in shape but is used for drying and often has a larger plain door and different controls; or with dishwashers, which usually have a flat front door and no visible laundry drum. Exclude sinks, cabinets, and other bathroom or laundry fixtures unless the washing machine itself is clearly the main object.

name: water bottle
898.description: A water bottle is a portable container for drinking water, usually tall and narrow with a cylindrical or slightly contoured body, a narrow neck or spout, and a screw cap, snap cap, or pull-top lid. It may be clear disposable plastic, translucent or opaque reusable plastic, or metal, and often has labels, ridged sides, squeezable walls, or a sports cap.
898.guidelines: Classify as water bottle when the object is a personal handheld container primarily designed to carry and drink water. This includes both disposable bottled-water containers and reusable sports water bottles. Do not confuse with thermoses or vacuum flasks, which are typically insulated and bulkier; canteens, which are often flatter or military-style; baby bottles, which have nipples and measurement markings; or laboratory/chemical bottles, which are not meant for drinking. The key cues are a drinkable bottle form, portable size, and a cap or spout intended for direct drinking.

name: jug
899.description: A jug is a handled vessel for holding and pouring liquids. It typically has a rounded, cylindrical, or bulbous body, a single side handle, and a narrowed neck or formed pouring lip/spout. It may be made of glass, ceramic, pottery, or metal, and can be plain or decorated, but the defining visual features are the container body plus a handle and a pour-friendly rim.
899.guidelines: Classify as jug when the vessel is primarily a pourable liquid container with one handle and a shaped lip or spout. Include glass, ceramic, and metal examples with varied body shapes. Do not confuse with a pitcher; pitchers are often larger and more open at the top, though the boundary can overlap. Distinguish from a carafe or decanter, which usually lack a side handle, and from an ewer, which is typically more ornate with a taller neck and sometimes a lid. Exclude cups, mugs, vases, and teapots unless they clearly function and appear as handled pouring vessels.

name: water tower
900.description: A tall elevated water-storage structure with a large tank mounted high above the ground on steel legs or a central column. The tank is usually cylindrical, spherical, or bulb-shaped, often with a domed top or rounded bottom, and may have ladders, railings, pipes, or painted town names on the side.
900.guidelines: Classify as water tower when the main object is an elevated storage tank raised on legs or a pedestal for municipal or industrial water supply. Common look-alikes include silos, grain bins, and smokestacks. Unlike silos or grain bins, water towers are lifted well above ground on an open support frame or tall stem and usually have a distinct tank at the top. Unlike smokestacks or chimneys, they have a broad storage vessel rather than a simple vertical tube. Include both modern steel towers and older wooden tank towers if the elevated water tank structure is clear.

name: whiskey jug
901.description: A whiskey jug is a rounded bottle or stoneware vessel for storing or pouring whiskey, typically with a bulbous or cylindrical body, short narrow neck, small mouth often sealed with a cork or stopper, and often a single side handle. Common examples are glazed ceramic or stoneware in brown, tan, cream, or white, though glass and metal versions also occur.
901.guidelines: Classify as whiskey jug when the object is a jug-shaped liquor container, especially a handled ceramic or glass vessel with a short neck and small opening used for whiskey. Do not confuse it with a generic bottle, decanter, or crock: bottles usually lack the squat jug body and side handle; decanters are typically more elegant glass vessels with a stopper and no jug handle; crocks and storage jars are wider-mouthed and less pour-oriented. Printed whiskey branding is common but not required—the key cues are the jug form, narrow mouth, and frequent handle.

name: whistle
902.description: A whistle is a small handheld sound-making device, usually made of plastic or metal, with a short tube-shaped or boxy body, a mouthpiece, and an opening or slit where air exits. It is often plain or brightly colored, and many examples include a key ring, lanyard, or coiled strap.
902.guidelines: Classify as whistle when the object is a blowable signaling noisemaker with a mouthpiece and air channel. It may be cylindrical, rectangular, flat, novelty-shaped, or attached to a keychain. Do not confuse with flutes, recorders, or pipes, which are musical instruments with multiple finger holes and longer bodies; nor with calls or horns that have larger resonating chambers; nor with unrelated keychain gadgets such as flashlights or laser pointers that lack a blowing mouthpiece and whistle opening.

name: wig
903.description: A wig is a removable artificial or natural-hair covering worn on the head to imitate or replace hair. It may be short or long, straight, wavy, curly, or highly styled, and comes in many colors, including natural shades and bright costume colors.
903.guidelines: Classify as wig when the image shows a separate hairpiece meant to be worn on the head, often displayed on a mannequin, stand, or person. Include costume wigs, fashion wigs, theatrical wigs, and toupees if the main object is the removable hairpiece. Do not confuse with natural hair or ordinary hairstyles: wigs often look like a complete detachable cap of hair, may sit on mannequins, and can appear unnaturally uniform, synthetic, or exaggerated in color and style. Exclude hair extensions, individual braids, hats, and animal fur.

name: window screen
904.description: A window screen is a thin mesh panel fitted into a window frame, usually made of metal, fiberglass, or plastic. It appears as a regular grid of small square or rectangular openings stretched across a frame, often dark gray, black, or silver, and is seen in front of outdoor views, insects, or light.
904.guidelines: Classify as window screen when the image shows fine mesh screening mounted in or associated with a window opening. The key cue is the uniform insect-screen grid visible as a translucent barrier over a view or object. Do not confuse it with chain-link fence, which has much larger diamond-shaped openings and heavier wire; wire mesh or hardware cloth, which is thicker, more rigid, and often used in cages or construction; or fabric netting, which is softer and less regularly framed. If the mesh is clearly part of a window or insect screen, choose window screen.

name: window shade
905.description: An interior window covering mounted over a window opening, typically made as a flat sheet or a series of horizontal slats, pleats, or fabric bands. It is usually rectangular and hangs vertically, often in neutral or light colors, and may filter light, cast striped shadows, or partially obscure the view through the window.
905.guidelines: Classify as window shade when the main subject is a mounted window covering such as a blind, roller shade, Roman shade, cellular shade, or similar light-blocking or light-filtering panel. Common look-alikes are curtains/drapes, shutters, and exterior awnings. Unlike curtains, window shades are structured and mounted within or above the window frame rather than hanging as loose fabric. Unlike shutters, they are made of slats, pleats, or fabric panels rather than rigid hinged panels. Exclude images where the window itself, shadows, or the room is primary and the shade is only incidental.

name: necktie
906.description: A long, narrow piece of cloth worn under a shirt collar and tied at the neck, usually hanging down the front of the chest. It is typically tapered, often silk or similar fabric, and comes in many colors, prints, and widths.
906.guidelines: Classify as necktie when the image shows the conventional long tie worn with a collared shirt, whether tied, draped, or laid flat. Do not require a Windsor knot specifically; different knots and tie widths still belong here. Exclude bow ties, ascots/cravats, bolo ties, scarves, and ribbon-like costume neckwear, which do not have the standard long tapered necktie shape.

name: wine bottle
907.description: A wine bottle is a tall, narrow glass bottle with sloping shoulders, a long neck, and a cork or screw-cap closure, typically with a printed label on the body and often a foil capsule over the top. Most are green, brown, or clear glass and are shown singly, in racks, cases, or store displays.
907.guidelines: Classify as wine bottle when the main object is the characteristic bottle used for wine packaging. Look for the classic tall glass form with long neck, wine label, and cork/foil or screw cap. Do not confuse it with liquor bottles, which are often shorter, wider, or more decorative; beer bottles, which are usually smaller with stubbier proportions and crown caps; champagne bottles, which are heavier with a punt and sparkling-wine styling; or olive-oil/vinegar bottles, which may look similar but usually have culinary branding rather than wine labeling.

name: aircraft wing
908.description: A rigid lateral airfoil structure attached to an aircraft, typically extending from each side of the fuselage. It is usually broad and flat with a tapered planform, and may show features such as flaps, ailerons, winglets, engine nacelles, struts, or landing gear attachment points depending on the aircraft type.
908.guidelines: Classify this category when the defining subject is the wing of an airplane or other aircraft, whether shown close up or as the most visually salient part of the aircraft. Do not confuse it with the whole airplane, tailplane, fin, rotor blades, or bird wings. Aircraft wings are fixed airfoil surfaces with straight or swept edges and often include control surfaces, wing-mounted engines, or winglets; tails are smaller rear surfaces, and rotor blades are long narrow rotating parts.

name: wok
909.description: A wok is a deep, wide cooking pan with sloping sides and a rounded or sometimes flat bottom, commonly used in Asian cooking. It may have a long handle or a pair of small loop handles, and is typically metal, dark steel, or cast iron.
909.guidelines: Classify as wok when the pan has a broad bowl-like shape with high flared sides and a round-bottomed or wok-style flat-bottomed profile. Include both single-handled and two-handled woks. Do not confuse with a frying pan or skillet, which is shallower with lower sides and usually a flat cooking surface, or with a saucepan/stockpot, which has straighter vertical sides and is deeper rather than broadly flared.

name: wooden spoon
910.description: A spoon made of wood, typically with a long, narrow handle and a rounded or oval bowl. It is usually smooth, carved from a single piece, and appears in natural wood tones ranging from pale beige to dark brown.
910.guidelines: Classify as wooden spoon when the object is clearly a spoon-shaped utensil made primarily of wood. Include cooking spoons, serving spoons, and carved wooden spoons with decorative variation, as long as the defining spoon bowl and wooden construction are present. Do not confuse with wooden spatulas, paddles, ladles with very deep cups, salad servers, or other wooden utensils such as forks and scoops. The key cue is a shallow spoon bowl attached to a handle, made of wood.

name: yarn
911.description: Spun fiber formed into long strands, typically shown wound into skeins, hanks, balls, or cakes. It appears as soft, flexible cord made of twisted or plied fibers, in solid, heathered, or multicolored varieties, and is often pictured alone or as the material used in knitting and crochet projects.
911.guidelines: Classify as yarn when the image centers on spun textile strands used for knitting, crochet, or similar crafts, especially in skeins, balls, or visible knitted/crocheted stitches. Do not confuse with raw wool or fleece, which looks like loose fluffy fiber; with woven or knitted fabric, where the finished cloth is the main subject rather than the strand; or with rope, cord, and twine, which are usually stiffer, coarser, and more utilitarian.

name: split-rail fence
912.description: A rustic wooden fence made from long rails stacked in an alternating zigzag line, usually without posts. The rails overlap at angled corners to form self-supporting crisscross joints, giving the fence a low, irregular, snaking appearance across fields or farmyards.
912.guidelines: Classify as split-rail fence when the fence is built from horizontal wooden rails laid in a zigzag or serpentine pattern with crossed corner stacks, typically postless. Do not confuse it with straight post-and-rail fences, which run in straight lines between vertical posts, or with woven wattle/hurdle fences, which use thin interlaced branches. Stone walls, picket fences, chain-link fences, and gates are not this category unless the distinctive zigzag stacked rail construction is the main subject.

name: shipwreck
913.description: A ruined or abandoned boat or ship, typically with a broken, partially collapsed, stranded, submerged, or heavily rusted hull. Common visual cues include exposed ribs and framing, missing planks or panels, corroded metal, weathered wood, tilted or half-sunken bodies, and wreckage resting on beaches, mudflats, shallow water, or underwater.
913.guidelines: Classify as shipwreck only when the vessel is clearly wrecked: heavily damaged, skeletal, beached and decaying, submerged as wreckage, or otherwise no longer an intact working craft. Do not confuse with intact boats or ships, docks, piers, floating platforms, or old but usable vessels. The key distinction is obvious structural ruin—collapsed hull sections, severe rust or rot, missing large parts, or a stranded/sunken state.

name: yawl
914.description: A yawl is a sailboat with two masts: a taller mainmast forward and a much smaller mizzen mast set very near the stern. The mizzen sail is small and mainly used for balance, and the hull is typically a small to medium monohull with fore-and-aft sails.
914.guidelines: Classify as a yawl only when the boat clearly has two masts and the rear mizzen mast is very small and positioned at or near the stern. Do not confuse it with a ketch: a ketch also has two masts, but its mizzen mast is larger and placed farther forward, ahead of the rudder post. Exclude single-masted sailboats such as dinghies, sloops, and cutters, and larger square-rigged ships whose sail plan is different.

name: yurt
915.description: A yurt is a portable, circular tent-like dwelling with a low cylindrical wall, a domed or conical roof, and a central roof opening or crown. It is typically covered in white or tan felt, canvas, or fabric over a visible wooden lattice frame, with a single door on the side.
915.guidelines: Classify as yurt when the structure is a round portable dwelling with fabric or felt covering stretched over a lattice framework and a domed roof, often with a central skylight ring. Do not confuse it with tipi tents, which are cone-shaped and supported by long poles, or modern camping tents and gazebos, which usually lack the rigid circular wall, crown, and traditional lattice construction.

name: website
916.description: A website shown as a browser page or screen capture, typically with a webpage layout containing headers, navigation menus, columns, text blocks, images, links, and other interface elements displayed on a computer or mobile screen.
916.guidelines: Classify as a website when the image mainly shows a webpage or website interface as seen in a browser or screenshot. Include full-page browser views, partial webpage screenshots, and mobile browser views. Do not confuse with general software interfaces, desktop applications, code editors, or documents/PDFs; websites usually have webpage structure, browser chrome or URL bar, navigation links, and page sections intended for online browsing.

name: comic book
917.description: A comic book is a printed publication made up primarily of sequential art panels with illustrations, speech balloons, captions, and short blocks of text. It is usually a thin, stapled or bound booklet with a colorful illustrated cover, though it can also appear as thicker collected editions or digest-sized formats.
917.guidelines: Classify as comic book when the item is a publication whose main content is comics presented in sequence. Typical examples show illustrated covers, interior pages with panel layouts, and booklet-like physical form. Do not confuse with magazines or catalogs that are mostly prose or photos, children's picture books with single full-page illustrations, manga/light novels without visible comic-panel structure, or comic strips shown only as isolated clippings. The key cue is a printed book or booklet whose primary content is sequential comic art.

name: crossword puzzle
918.description: A word puzzle made of a rectangular grid of white and black squares, with numbered entries filled by letters running across and down. It is typically printed on paper or shown in a book, newspaper, magazine, worksheet, or screen, often with clue lists beside or below the grid.
918.guidelines: Classify as crossword puzzle when the image shows the characteristic interlocking letter grid with black separator squares and across/down clues or filled answers. Do not confuse with Sudoku or other number puzzles, which use digits and usually lack black squares; Scrabble or letter-tile arrangements, which use movable tiles rather than a printed clue grid; or generic word-search puzzles, which are dense letter arrays without numbered across/down entries.

name: street sign
919.description: A posted sign used on or beside a street or road, typically mounted on a pole, wall, or overhead support. It usually consists of a flat board or shaped plate with printed symbols, arrows, route or street names, parking information, warnings, or traffic instructions. Common forms include rectangular street-name signs, octagonal stop signs, triangular warning or yield signs, circular regulatory signs, and parking signs.
919.guidelines: Classify signs whose primary purpose is road, traffic, parking, route, or street identification. This includes street-name plates and standard traffic-control or warning signs. Do not include commercial or storefront signs, advertisements, business logos, or decorative building text. Also exclude house numbers, memorial plaques, and unrelated posted notices unless they function as official road or street signage. The key cue is official roadside/public-way use rather than commercial display.

name: traffic light
920.description: A traffic light is a road signal device with a vertical or horizontal housing containing circular colored lenses, most often red, yellow/amber, and green. It is typically mounted on a pole, mast arm, or overhead wire above or beside a roadway or intersection, and may also appear in pedestrian or bicycle-specific versions.
920.guidelines: Classify as traffic light when the image shows the signal head itself: a multi-lamp road traffic control device with colored lights and a distinct signal housing. Include standard vehicle signals as well as pedestrian or bicycle signal variants. Do not confuse with railroad signals, vehicle taillights, illuminated signs, or streetlights. Railroad signals are tied to train tracks and usually have paired round lamps on a crossbuck-style or rail-specific assembly; streetlights are for illumination rather than traffic control; neon signs and lit storefronts lack the standardized signal housing and red-yellow-green control layout.

name: dust jacket
book jacket
921.description: A removable paper cover wrapped around a hardback book, usually printed with the title, author, publisher text, and often illustrations or photographs on the front, spine, and back. It typically fits over the boards with folded inner flaps and may be glossy or matte.
921.guidelines: Classify as a dust jacket when the image shows the printed outer paper wrapper of a hardcover book, often including the front cover, spine, and flap text. Do not confuse it with a paperback book cover, which is the book’s permanent outer cover and has no folded flaps, or with a bare hardback binding/boards, which are cloth, paper, or leather covers underneath the jacket. If only a book is visible, look for signs of a removable wrapper such as overhanging paper edges, folded flaps, or a glossy illustrated cover on a hardback.

name: menu
922.description: A menu is a printed, handwritten, or digitally displayed list of food and drink items offered by a restaurant, café, bar, or similar venue, usually organized by category and often accompanied by prices. It may appear as a single sheet, booklet, board, placard, laminated card, wall display, or takeout order form, and typically consists mainly of text with occasional photos or graphic layout elements.
922.guidelines: Classify as menu when the image shows a document or display whose main purpose is listing items available to order, usually foods or beverages, often with prices and section headings. Include handheld menus, table menus, wall-mounted menu boards, chalkboard café menus, and takeout order sheets. Do not confuse with advertisements, flyers, brochures, recipe pages, food packaging, or invoices/receipts: menus are organized around selectable dishes or drinks for purchase. A receipt records what was already bought, while a sign or poster mainly promotes a brand or single item rather than presenting a fuller order list.

name: plate
923.description: A plate is a broad, usually flat dish used for serving or eating food. It is typically round or oval with a shallow raised rim, and is commonly made of ceramic, porcelain, glass, metal, or plastic. Plates are shown from above or at a slight angle and often hold a meal, dessert, or arranged portions of food.
923.guidelines: Classify as plate when the main object is a flat or shallow eating dish with a wide open surface and low rim. Include dinner plates, salad plates, dessert plates, and similar serving plates. Do not confuse with bowls, which are deeper with taller sides; trays or platters, which are usually larger serving pieces; or saucers, which are smaller dishes made specifically for cups. If food is present, focus on the dish shape rather than the cuisine.

name: guacamole
924.description: A thick avocado-based dip or spread, usually pale to vivid green and mashed to a smooth, creamy, or chunky texture. It is commonly served in a bowl or as a topping, and often contains visible bits of onion, tomato, cilantro, or chili mixed into the avocado.
924.guidelines: Classify as guacamole when the food is clearly an avocado mash or dip with a green, creamy-to-chunky appearance, whether served alone, with chips, or as a topping. Do not confuse it with avocado salsa or salad, which is usually looser and more distinctly diced, or with plain mashed avocado, which may lack the typical mixed-in seasonings and dip-like presentation. It can resemble green hummus or other dips, but guacamole usually has the characteristic avocado color, richer mashed texture, and visible add-ins like tomato, onion, or cilantro.

name: soup
925.description: A liquid dish served in a bowl, usually based on broth or stock and ranging from clear, tea-colored soups to lightly cloudy or ingredient-filled preparations. It may contain small pieces of vegetables, meat, seafood, herbs, noodles, or dumplings, but the defining appearance is a bowl of spoonable liquid rather than a dry or solid food.
925.guidelines: Classify as soup when the main item is a bowl or pot of liquid food intended to be eaten with a spoon, whether clear or with ingredients suspended in broth. Do not restrict to consommé only: these examples include many broth-based soups. Avoid confusing it with stew or curry, which are usually thicker and chunkier, or with sauces and gravies, which are condiments rather than standalone dishes. If the liquid is the primary dish and served as a course on its own, it is likely soup.

name: hot pot
926.description: A communal cooking dish centered on a deep metal pot of simmering broth, often set on a tabletop burner. The pot may be plain or divided into two sections with different soups, and diners cook thinly sliced meat, seafood, tofu, vegetables, noodles, and similar ingredients in the broth.
926.guidelines: Classify as hot pot when the image shows a pot of actively simmering broth used for cooking food at the table, often with raw ingredients or dipping utensils nearby. Do not confuse it with fondue, which usually features melted cheese, chocolate, or oil rather than soup broth; with ordinary soup or stew, which is typically served already cooked rather than cooked communally at the table; or with a standalone stockpot or saucepan on a stove that lacks the recognizable hot-pot dining setup.

name: trifle
927.description: A layered dessert served in a clear bowl, glass, or cup, typically showing distinct bands of sponge cake or biscuits, custard, fruit or jelly, cream, and often a whipped-cream topping. It is usually soft, creamy, and colorful, with visible stacked layers rather than a single uniform texture.
927.guidelines: Classify as trifle when the dessert is clearly built from visible layers of cake or biscuits, custard or cream, and often fruit or jelly in a transparent serving dish. Do not confuse it with parfaits or verrines, which are often narrower single-portion layered desserts without the classic cake-custard-cream structure; with tiramisu, which is usually coffee-colored, cocoa-dusted, and lacks fruit/jelly layers; or with plain pudding/custard desserts, which are not distinctly layered.

name: ice cream
928.description: A frozen dairy-based dessert typically shown as one or more smooth, rounded scoops or soft swirls in bowls, cups, cones, or as a topping on other desserts. It appears in many colors and flavors, from white and cream to chocolate brown, pink, blue, or mixed swirls, and may include visible mix-ins, sauces, whipped cream, fruit, nuts, or candy.
928.guidelines: Classify as ice cream when the main subject is a scoop or serving of creamy frozen dessert, whether plain or used in sundaes, floats, or as a topping. Exclude popsicles and ice pops, which are frozen water or juice on a stick; exclude sorbet or shaved ice when the texture looks icy, crystalline, or granular rather than creamy; and exclude frozen yogurt or gelato only if the image is clearly labeled or visually distinctive in a way that identifies those specific desserts. The key cue is a creamy, scoopable frozen dessert rather than an icy frozen treat.

name: popsicle
ice pop
929.description: A popsicle is a frozen water-, juice-, or syrup-based treat molded around a stick. It is usually brightly colored, smooth, and translucent or semi-opaque, often in a simple bar or rounded rectangular shape, and may be single-flavor or striped in multiple colors.
929.guidelines: Classify as popsicle/ice pop when the item is a frozen non-cream ice treat on a stick. Include plain juice bars and multicolored ice pops. Do not confuse with ice cream bars or other frozen novelties coated in chocolate or made from creamy dairy ice cream; those belong with ice cream. Also exclude handheld candy lollipops, which are hard candy rather than frozen treats.

name: bread
930.description: A baked loaf of bread, typically made from wheat flour dough and shown as an elongated or oval loaf with a browned crust. It may be smooth or lightly floured, often with slashes on top, and ranges from pale golden to dark brown.
930.guidelines: Classify as bread when the main object is a plain baked loaf or roll shape rather than a specific prepared sandwich, pastry, or topped dish. Includes elongated loaves, oval loaves, and similar everyday bakery bread forms. Do not confuse with baguette when the loaf is not distinctly long, thin, and stick-like; with sandwich or hot dog when the bread is filled; or with pizza, bruschetta, and garlic bread when toppings or strong preparation cues dominate.

name: bagel
931.description: A bagel is a dense, round bread roll with a hole in the center, usually smooth and glossy on the outside and often topped with sesame seeds, poppy seeds, onion, salt, or other seasonings. It is typically golden brown and can appear plain, seeded, whole grain, or filled or sliced for sandwiches.
931.guidelines: Classify as bagel when the food is a ring-shaped bread roll with a chewy, compact crumb and a characteristic central hole. Include plain, seeded, whole wheat, and sandwich bagels. Do not confuse with donuts, which are usually sweeter, softer, and often glazed or cakey; pretzels, which have a twisted shape; bread rolls or buns, which usually lack the hole; or bundt cakes and other ring-shaped baked goods, which are larger and cake-like rather than bread-like.

name: pretzel
932.description: A pretzel is a baked bread snack or pastry formed from a rope of dough twisted into a distinctive knot with three holes or looped arms. It is usually glossy brown from baking, often topped with coarse salt, and may be soft or hard, plain, chocolate-coated, or otherwise flavored.
932.guidelines: Classify as pretzel when the defining pretzel twist or knot shape is visible, whether it is a large soft bakery pretzel or a small hard snack pretzel. Do not confuse with bagels or doughnuts, which are simple rings without the twisted crossover, or with other breads and pastries that may be glazed or salted but lack the characteristic pretzel knot.

name: cheeseburger
933.description: A hamburger served on a bun with a ground-beef patty topped with melted cheese, often with additional toppings such as lettuce, tomato, onion, pickles, bacon, and condiments. It may be a single or multiple-patty burger, but the defining visual feature is cheese on the burger patty within a sandwich bun.
933.guidelines: Classify as cheeseburger when the image shows a burger-style sandwich with a beef patty in a bun and visible cheese. Include variations with different buns, patty counts, and toppings. Do not confuse with a plain hamburger, which lacks cheese, or with other sandwiches such as chicken burgers, pulled-pork sandwiches, or breakfast sandwiches. The key cue is a burger patty plus clearly visible cheese in a bun.

name: hot dog
934.description: A hot dog is a cooked sausage served in a long, split soft bun. It is usually cylindrical and elongated, with the sausage extending along most of the bun, and is often topped with condiments such as mustard, ketchup, relish, onions, chili, cheese, or sauerkraut.
934.guidelines: Classify as hot dog when the image shows a sausage in a long bun or clearly presented as that food item, even with varied toppings or partial wrapping. Do not confuse it with a plain sausage or frankfurter shown without a bun, a sandwich/submarine sandwich with sliced fillings, or a hamburger in a round bun with a patty. If the defining long bun-and-sausage form is absent, it is likely not a hot dog.

name: mashed potato
935.description: A soft, creamy potato dish made from cooked potatoes mashed into a smooth or slightly luffled mound. It is usually white to pale yellow, sometimes glossy with butter or cream, and may show small lumps, ridges, spoon marks, gravy, herbs, or bits of skin or mix-ins.
935.guidelines: Classify as mashed potato when the food is a mashed, fluffy, spoonable potato preparation, whether smooth or slightly chunky, plated as a mound or served in a bowl. Do not confuse it with potato salad, which has distinct chunks in dressing; whipped cream or ice cream, which look dessert-like and are usually smoother or more aerated; polenta or grits, which are more uniform and porridge-like; or cauliflower mash, which is often wetter and less starchy-looking. Presence of gravy, butter, or herbs is common but not required.

name: cabbage
Brassica oleracea Group Capitata
936.description: A compact leafy vegetable forming a dense rounded or slightly flattened head of overlapping leaves. Most are green to blue-green, but some are red-purple or deeply crinkled like savoy types. Outer leaves are broader and looser, while the inner leaves are tightly packed into a firm head.
936.guidelines: Classify as cabbage when the plant forms a tight head of broad leaves. Include green, red, and savoy head cabbages. Do not confuse with lettuce, which has softer thinner leaves and a less dense head; with Chinese cabbage such as napa, which is more elongated with pale ribs; or with kale and collards, which usually have loose open rosettes rather than a compact head.

name: broccoli
Brassica oleracea var. italica
937.description: A green cruciferous vegetable with a thick pale-green stalk that branches into a dense crown of tightly packed small flower buds. It typically appears as one large head or several clustered florets with a bumpy, tree-like surface and attached broad bluish-green leaves in fresh garden specimens.
937.guidelines: Classify as broccoli when the image shows the characteristic thick branching stem and compact green flowering head made of many tiny buds. Do not confuse it with cauliflower, which has a usually white or cream curd, or Romanesco broccoli, which has pointed spiral cones.
